akhfash:1-1.t: He said: ﴿طه﴾. Some of them claim that it is two letters, like ﴿حَمّ] and some of them say {طه﴾ means "O man" in one of the dialects of the Arabs. «[Translator's note: the brackets in the source are mismatched; the text is reproduced as written.]»

akhfash:3-3.t: And He said ﴿إِلاَّ تَذْكِرَةً لِّمَن يَخْشَىٰ﴾ as a badal (substitute) for His word ﴿لِتَشْقَىٰ﴾ [2], so he made it "We did not send down the Quran upon you except as a reminder".

akhfash:4-4.t: And He said ﴿تَنزِيلاً﴾, i.e. Allah sent that down as a sending-down (تنزيلا).

akhfash:5-5.t:
And He said ﴿ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ﴾, i.e. "He is the Most Merciful". Some read ﴿ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ﴾, i.e. "a sending-down from the Most Merciful".
And He said ﴿عَلَى ٱلْعَرْشِ ٱسْتَوَىٰ﴾: He means "عَلاَ" (He rose above), and the meaning of "عَلاَ" is "He had power (قَدَر)". He never ceased to be powerful, but He informed of His power.

akhfash:18-18.t: And He said ﴿مَآرِبُ أُخْرَىٰ﴾: its singular is "مَأْرُبَةٌ" (need).

akhfash:22-22.t: And He said ﴿آيَةً أُخْرَىٰ﴾, i.e. "it brought out another sign", and he made it a badal (substitute) for His word ﴿بَيْضَآءَ﴾.

akhfash:42-42.t: And He said ﴿وَلاَ تَنِيَا﴾: it is from "وَنَى" and "يَنِي", "وَنْياً" and "وُنِيّاً" (to slacken).

akhfash:44-44.t: And He said ﴿لَّعَلَّهُ يَتَذَكَّرُ﴾, like a man's saying to his companion: "افرَعْ لَعَلَّنَا نَتَغَدّى" (finish, perhaps we may have lunch), the meaning being: "so that we may have lunch" and "until we have lunch". And you say to a man: "اِعْمَلْ عَمَلَكَ لَعَلَّكَ تَأْخُذُ أَجْرَكَ" (do your work, perhaps you will take your wage), i.e. so that you may take it.

akhfash:53-53.t: And He said ﴿أَزْوَاجاً مِّن نَّبَاتٍ شَتَّىٰ﴾: He means "diverse pairs (أَزْواجاً شَتَّى) of plants"; or it is the plants that are diverse. All of that is sound.

akhfash:63-63.t:
And He said ﴿إِنْ هَـٰذَانِ لَسَاحِرَانِ﴾: light (إنْ) in the meaning of the heavy one (إنّ). It is the dialect of a people who use the nominative (after it) and bring in the lām to distinguish it from the one that has the meaning of "ما" (not). We read it heavy, and that is a dialect of the Banū al-Ḥārith ibn Kaʿb.
And He said ﴿ٱلْمُثْلَىٰ﴾: the feminine of "الأَمْثَل" (the best), like "القُصْوَى" and "ألأَقْصَى" (the farthest).

akhfash:69-69.t: And He said ﴿ٱلسَّاحِرُ حَيْثُ أَتَىٰ﴾; in the reading of Ibn Masʿūd it is ﴿أيْنَ أَتَى﴾. The Arabs say: "جِئْتُكَ من أيْنَ لا تَعْلَم" and "مِنْ حَيْثُ لا تَعْلَم" (I came to you from where you do not know).

akhfash:72-72.t: And He said ﴿لَن نُّؤْثِرَكَ عَلَىٰ مَا جَآءَنَا مِنَ ٱلْبَيِّنَاتِ وَٱلَّذِي فَطَرَنَا﴾: He means "we will not prefer you over the One who created us".

akhfash:77-77.t: And He said ﴿لاَّ تَخَافُ دَرَكاً﴾, i.e. ﴿اِضْرِبْ لَهُمْ طَريقا﴾ (strike for them a path) ﴿لاَّ تَخَافُ﴾ in it ﴿دَرَكاً﴾ (being overtaken). He omitted "فيه" (in it), just as you say: "زيدٌ أَكْرَمْتُ" (Zayd, I honoured), meaning "أَكْرَمْتُهُ" (I honoured him), and as He said ﴿وَٱتَّقُواْ يَوْماً لاَّ تَجْزِي نَفْسٌ عَن نَّفْسٍ شَيْئاً﴾, i.e. in which (a soul) will not avail.

akhfash:81-81.t: And He said ﴿فَيَحِلَّ﴾ and explained it as "يَجِب" (become due). Some read ﴿يَحُلَّ﴾ in the sense of "alighting", so they used ḍamma. And he said ﴿يَصِدُّونَ﴾ in the sense of "يَضِجُّونَ" (they clamour), and I consider it nothing but a dialect variant, like "يَعْكِفُ" and "ويَعْكُف", in the meaning of "يَصدّ". «[Translator's note: ﴿يَصِدُّونَ﴾ is from Q 43:57, not this verse; it appears here as written in the source.]»

akhfash:111-111.t: And He said ﴿وَعَنَتِ ٱلْوُجُوهُ﴾: one says "عَنَتْ" "تَعْنُو" "عُنُوّاً" (to be humbled).

akhfash:129-129.t: And He said ﴿وَلَوْلاَ كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ مِن رَّبِّكَ لَكَانَ لِزَاماً﴾: He means "and were it not for a word and ﴿أَجَلٌ مُّسَمًّى﴾ (a stated term), it would have been inevitable".

akhfash:132-132.t: And He said ﴿لِلتَّقْوَىٰ﴾: for the people of taqwā (God-consciousness). In the reading of Ibn Masʿūd: ﴿وإِنْ العاقِبَةَ لِلتَّقْوى﴾.

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿طه﴾ — Allah knows best what He intends by that.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿مَا أَنْزَلْنَا عَلَيْكَ الْقُرْآنَ﴾ — O Muḥammad — ﴿لِتَشْقَى﴾ — so that you exhaust yourself with what you did after its revelation, by standing long in the night prayer; i.e. lighten things for yourself.

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿إِلَّا﴾ — but We sent it down — ﴿تَذْكِرَةً﴾ — as a reminder through it — ﴿لِمَنْ يَخْشَى﴾ — for whoever fears Allah.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿تَنْزِيلًا﴾ — a substitute (badal) for the utterance of its verb that puts it in the accusative — ﴿مِمَّنْ خَلَقَ الْأَرْضَ وَالسَّمَاوَاتِ الْعُلَى﴾ — plural of ʿulyā, like kubrā and kubar. He is

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿الرَّحْمَنُ عَلَى الْعَرْشِ﴾ — and in the language it is the throne of the king — ﴿اسْتَوَى﴾ — an istiwāʾ (rising) befitting Him.

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا﴾ — of created things — ﴿وَمَا تَحْتَ الثَّرَى﴾ — it is moist soil, and what is meant is the seven earths, because they are beneath it.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿وَإِنْ تَجْهَرْ بِالْقَوْلِ﴾ — in remembrance or supplication, then Allah has no need of saying it aloud — ﴿فَإِنَّهُ يَعْلَمُ السِّرَّ وَأَخْفَى﴾ — than it, i.e. what the soul speaks to itself, and what crosses it without its speaking of it; so do not strain yourself by speaking aloud.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿اللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ لَهُ الْأَسْمَاءُ الْحُسْنَى﴾ — the ninety-nine mentioned in the ḥadīth; and al-ḥusnā is the feminine of al-aḥsan.

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿إِذْ رَأَى نَارًا فَقَالَ لِأَهْلِهِ﴾ — to his wife — ﴿امْكُثُوا﴾ — here; and that was on his journey from Madyan heading for Egypt — ﴿إِنِّي آنَسْتُ﴾ — I have seen — ﴿نَارًا لَعَلِّي آتِيكُمْ مِنْهَا بِقَبَسٍ﴾ — with a flame at the tip of a wick or a stick — ﴿أَوْ أَجِدُ عَلَى النَّارِ هُدًى﴾ — i.e. a guide to show me the way; he had lost it because of the darkness of the night. And he said "perhaps" because he could not be certain of fulfilling the promise.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا أَتَاهَا﴾ — and it was a boxthorn tree — ﴿نُودِيَ يَا مُوسَى﴾

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿إِنِّي﴾ — with kasra on the hamza, by interpreting "nūdiya" (he was called) as "qīla" (it was said), and with fatḥa on it, with the implied bāʾ — ﴿أَنَا﴾ — a tawkīd (emphasis) of the yāʾ of the speaker — ﴿رَبُّكَ فَاخْلَعْ نَعْلَيْكَ إِنَّكَ بِالْوَادِ الْمُقَدَّسِ﴾ — the purified or the blessed — ﴿طُوًى﴾ — a badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), with tanwīn and without it: fully declinable (maṣrūf) when regarded as a place, and a diptote (ghayr maṣrūf) because of femininity when regarded as a plot of land, together with its being a proper name.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿وَأَنَا اخْتَرْتُكَ﴾ — from among your people — ﴿فَاسْتَمِعْ لِمَا يُوحَى﴾ — to you from Me.

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿إِنَّنِي أَنَا اللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنَا فَاعْبُدْنِي وَأَقِمِ الصَّلَاةَ لِذِكْرِي﴾ — in it.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿إِنَّ السَّاعَةَ آتِيَةٌ أَكَادُ أُخْفِيهَا﴾ — from people, while its nearness becomes apparent to them through its signs — ﴿لِتُجْزَى﴾ — in it — ﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا تَسْعَى﴾ — in it, of good or evil.

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿فَلَا يَصُدَّنَّكَ﴾ — let him not turn you away — ﴿عَنْهَا﴾ — i.e. from believing in it — ﴿مَنْ لَا يُؤْمِنُ بِهَا وَاتَّبَعَ هَوَاهُ﴾ — in denying it — ﴿فَتَرْدَى﴾ — i.e. so that you perish, if you are turned away from it.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿وَمَا تِلْكَ﴾ — being — ﴿بِيَمِينِكَ يَا مُوسَى﴾ — the interrogative is for affirmation (taqrīr), so that He may base the miracle in it upon that.

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿قَالَ هِيَ عَصَايَ أَتَوَكَّأُ﴾ — I lean — ﴿عَلَيْهَا﴾ — when leaping and walking — ﴿وَأَهُشُّ﴾ — I beat the leaves of trees — ﴿بِهَا﴾ — so that they fall — ﴿عَلَى غَنَمِي﴾ — and they eat them — ﴿وَلِيَ فِيهَا مَآرِبُ﴾ — plural of maʾraba, with the rāʾ taking any of the three vowels, i.e. needs — ﴿أُخْرَى﴾ — such as carrying provisions and the water-skin, and driving away vermin. And in the answer he added an explanation of his needs for it.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿قَالَ أَلْقِهَا يَا مُوسَى﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿فَأَلْقَاهَا فَإِذَا هِيَ حَيَّةٌ﴾ — a huge serpent — ﴿تَسْعَى﴾ — moving on its belly quickly, like the quickness of the small snake called al-jānn, by which it is described in another verse.

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿قَالَ خُذْهَا وَلَا تَخَفْ﴾ — of it — ﴿سَنُعِيدُهَا سِيرَتَهَا﴾ — accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), i.e. to its state — ﴿الْأُولَى﴾ — so he put his hand in its mouth and it turned back into a staff, and it became clear that the place where he put it in was the place where he held it, between its two prongs. The master Mūsā was shown that so that he would not be alarmed when it turned into a serpent before Pharaoh.

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿وَاضْمُمْ يَدَكَ﴾ — the right, meaning the palm — ﴿إِلَى جَنَاحِكَ﴾ — i.e. your left side, under the upper arm up to the armpit, and bring it out — ﴿تَخْرُجْ﴾ — contrary to the brownness it had — ﴿بَيْضَاءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوءٍ﴾ — i.e. leprosy, shining like the rays of the sun, dazzling the sight — ﴿آيَةً أُخْرَى﴾ — it and "bayḍāʾ" are two ḥāls (circumstantials) from the pronoun of "takhruj".

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿لِنُرِيَكَ﴾ — by it, when you do that to make it appear — ﴿مِنْ آيَاتِنَا﴾ — the sign — ﴿الْكُبْرَى﴾ — i.e. the greatest, of your messengership. And when he wanted it to return to its first state, he pressed it to his side, as mentioned before, and brought it out.

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿اذْهَبْ﴾ — as a messenger — ﴿إِلَى فِرْعَوْنَ﴾ — and those with him. ﴿إِنَّهُ طَغَى﴾ — he has exceeded the limit in his disbelief, to the point of claiming divinity.

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿قَالَ رَبِّ اشْرَحْ لِي صَدْرِي﴾ — widen it to bear the message.

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿وَيَسِّرْ﴾ — make easy — ﴿لِي أَمْرِي﴾ — so that I may convey it.

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿وَاحْلُلْ عُقْدَةً مِنْ لِسَانِي﴾ — which arose from its being burnt by a live coal he put in his mouth when he was small.

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿يَفْقَهُوا﴾ — so that they understand — ﴿قَوْلِي﴾ — when conveying the message.

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿وَاجْعَلْ لِي وَزِيرًا﴾ — a helper in it — ﴿مِنْ أَهْلِي﴾

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿هَارُونَ﴾ — a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) — ﴿أَخِي﴾ — ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition).

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿وَأَشْرِكْهُ فِي أَمْرِي﴾ — i.e. the message. The two verbs are [read] in the imperative form and in the jussive (majzūm) imperfect form, and it is the response to the request (jawāb al-ṭalab).

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿إِنَّكَ كُنْتَ بِنَا بَصِيرًا﴾ — knowing, so You bestowed the message as a favour.

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿قَالَ قَدْ أُوتِيتَ سُؤْلَكَ يَا مُوسَى﴾ — as a favour to you.

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ مَنَنَّا عَلَيْكَ مَرَّةً أُخْرَى﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿إِذْ﴾ — causal (li-l-taʿlīl) — ﴿أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَى أُمِّكَ﴾ — in a dream or by inspiration, when she gave birth to you and feared that Pharaoh would kill you among those being born — ﴿مَا يُوحَى﴾ — concerning you; and there is substituted (badal) from it:

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿أَنِ اقْذِفِيهِ﴾ — put him — ﴿فِي التَّابُوتِ فَاقْذِفِيهِ﴾ — with the chest — ﴿فِي الْيَمِّ﴾ — the river Nile — ﴿فَلْيُلْقِهِ الْيَمُّ بِالسَّاحِلِ﴾ — i.e. its bank; and the imperative has the meaning of a statement — ﴿يَأْخُذْهُ عَدُوٌّ لِي وَعَدُوٌّ لَهُ﴾ — and he is Pharaoh. ﴿وَأَلْقَيْتُ﴾ — after they took you — ﴿عَلَيْكَ مَحَبَّةً مِنِّي﴾ — so that you would be loved among people; so Pharaoh loved you, and everyone who saw you — ﴿وَلِتُصْنَعَ عَلَى عَيْنِي﴾ — be brought up under My care and protection of you.

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿إِذْ﴾ — causal — ﴿تَمْشِي أُخْتُكَ﴾ — Maryam, to find out news of you, when they had brought wet-nurses and you would not accept the breast of any one of them — ﴿فَتَقُولُ هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَى مَنْ يَكْفُلُهُ﴾ — and she was answered, so she brought his mother and he accepted her breast — ﴿فَرَجَعْنَاكَ إِلَى أُمِّكَ كَيْ تَقَرَّ عَيْنُهَا﴾ — at meeting you — ﴿وَلَا تَحْزَنَ﴾ — then. ﴿وَقَتَلْتَ نَفْسًا﴾ — he is the Copt in Egypt, and you were distressed at having killed him, on account of Pharaoh — ﴿فَنَجَّيْنَاكَ مِنَ الْغَمِّ وَفَتَنَّاكَ فُتُونًا﴾ — We tested you by casting you into other than that and delivered you from it — ﴿فَلَبِثْتَ سِنِينَ﴾ — ten — ﴿فِي أَهْلِ مَدْيَنَ﴾ — after you came to it from Egypt, with Shuʿayb the Prophet, and after you married his daughter — ﴿ثُمَّ جِئْتَ عَلَى قَدَرٍ﴾ — in My knowledge, for the message, and that is at forty years of your age — ﴿يَا مُوسَى﴾.

celaleyn:41-41.t: ﴿وَاصْطَنَعْتُكَ﴾ — I chose you — ﴿لِنَفْسِي﴾ — for the message.

celaleyn:42-42.t: ﴿اذْهَبْ أَنْتَ وَأَخُوكَ﴾ — to the people — ﴿بِآيَاتِي﴾ — the nine — ﴿وَلَا تَنِيَا﴾ — do not slacken — ﴿فِي ذِكْرِي﴾ — with glorification and other than it.

celaleyn:43-43.t: ﴿اذْهَبَا إِلَى فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُ طَغَى﴾ — by his claiming lordship.

celaleyn:44-44.t: ﴿فَقُولَا لَهُ قَوْلًا لَيِّنًا﴾ — about his turning back from that — ﴿لَعَلَّهُ يَتَذَكَّرُ﴾ — take admonition — ﴿أَوْ يَخْشَى﴾ — Allah, and turn back. The hope is relative to the two of them, since He the Exalted knew that he would not turn back.

celaleyn:45-45.t: ﴿قَالَا رَبَّنَا إِنَّنَا نَخَافُ أَنْ يَفْرُطَ عَلَيْنَا﴾ — i.e. hasten to punish — ﴿أَوْ أَنْ يَطْغَى﴾ — against us, i.e. behave arrogantly.

celaleyn:46-46.t: ﴿قَالَ لَا تَخَافَا إِنَّنِي مَعَكُمَا﴾ — with My help — ﴿أَسْمَعُ﴾ — what he says — ﴿وَأَرَى﴾ — what he does.

celaleyn:47-47.t: ﴿فَأْتِيَاهُ فَقُولَا إِنَّا رَسُولَا رَبِّكَ فَأَرْسِلْ مَعَنَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾ — to Syria — ﴿وَلَا تُعَذِّبْهُمْ﴾ — i.e. release them from your using them in your arduous labours, such as digging, building and carrying heavy loads. ﴿قَدْ جِئْنَاكَ بِآيَةٍ﴾ — with a proof — ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾ — of our truthfulness in the message. ﴿وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى مَنِ اتَّبَعَ الْهُدَى﴾ — i.e. safety for him from punishment.

celaleyn:48-48.t: ﴿إِنَّا قَدْ أُوحِيَ إِلَيْنَا أَنَّ الْعَذَابَ عَلَى مَنْ كَذَّبَ﴾ — what we have brought — ﴿وَتَوَلَّى﴾ — turned away from it. So they came to him and said all that has been mentioned.

celaleyn:49-49.t: ﴿قَالَ فَمَنْ رَبُّكُمَا يَا مُوسَى﴾ — he confined [the address] to him because he is the principal, and in order to humiliate him (li-idhlālihi) by [reminding him of] the upbringing. [Translator's note: the text reads «لِإِذْلَالِهِ» "to humiliate him"; the commonly transmitted reading is «لِإِدْلَالِهِ» "because he presumed upon him", on account of having raised him.]

celaleyn:50-50.t: ﴿قَالَ رَبُّنَا الَّذِي أَعْطَى كُلَّ شَيْءٍ﴾ — of creation — ﴿خَلْقَهُ﴾ — the form it has, by which it is distinguished from others — ﴿ثُمَّ هَدَى﴾ — the animals among it, to their food, their drink, their mating and other than that.

celaleyn:51-51.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ — Pharaoh — ﴿فَمَا بَالُ﴾ — what is the state of — ﴿الْقُرُونِ﴾ — the nations — ﴿الْأُولَى﴾ — such as the people of Nūḥ, Hūd, Lūṭ and Ṣāliḥ, in their worship of idols?

celaleyn:52-52.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ — Mūsā — ﴿عِلْمُهَا﴾ — i.e. the knowledge of their state is preserved — ﴿عِنْدَ رَبِّي فِي كِتَابٍ﴾ — it is the Preserved Tablet; He will requite them for it on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿لَا يَضِلُّ﴾ — is not absent — ﴿رَبِّي﴾ — from anything — ﴿وَلَا يَنْسَى﴾ — my Lord does not forget anything. He is

celaleyn:53-53.t: ﴿الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمْ﴾ — among the whole of creation — ﴿الْأَرْضَ مَهْدًا﴾ — a bed — ﴿وَسَلَكَ﴾ — made easy — ﴿لَكُمْ فِيهَا سُبُلًا﴾ — roads — ﴿وَأَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً﴾ — rain. The Exalted said, completing what Mūsā described Him with, and addressing the people of Mecca: ﴿فَأَخْرَجْنَا بِهِ أَزْوَاجًا﴾ — kinds — ﴿مِنْ نَبَاتٍ شَتَّى﴾ — an adjective (ṣifa) of "azwājan", i.e. differing in colours, tastes and other things; and shattā is the plural of shatīt, like marīḍ and marḍā, from "shatta al-amr" (the matter became scattered), i.e. it became dispersed.

celaleyn:54-54.t: ﴿كُلُوا﴾ — of it — ﴿وَارْعَوْا أَنْعَامَكُمْ﴾ — in it; plural of naʿam, which are camels, cattle and sheep. One says "raʿat al-anʿām" (the livestock grazed) and "raʿaytuhā" (I grazed them). The imperative is for permission and as a reminder of the blessing, and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of "akhrajnā", i.e. permitting you to eat and to graze livestock. ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ﴾ — what is mentioned here — ﴿لَآيَاتٍ﴾ — lessons — ﴿لِأُولِي النُّهَى﴾ — for those possessed of intellects; plural of nuhya, like ghurfa and ghuraf. The intellect is called by it because it forbids (yanhā) its possessor from committing vile acts.

celaleyn:55-55.t: ﴿مِنْهَا﴾ — i.e. from the earth — ﴿خَلَقْنَاكُمْ﴾ — by creating your father Ādam from it — ﴿وَفِيهَا نُعِيدُكُمْ﴾ — buried after death — ﴿وَمِنْهَا نُخْرِجُكُمْ﴾ — at the resurrection — ﴿تَارَةً﴾ — a time — ﴿أُخْرَى﴾ — just as We brought you out at the beginning of your creation.

celaleyn:56-56.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أَرَيْنَاهُ﴾ — i.e. We made Pharaoh see — ﴿آيَاتِنَا كُلَّهَا﴾ — the nine — ﴿فَكَذَّبَ﴾ — them, and claimed that they were sorcery — ﴿وَأَبَى﴾ — to affirm the oneness of Allah the Exalted.

celaleyn:57-57.t: ﴿قَالَ أَجِئْتَنَا لِتُخْرِجَنَا مِنْ أَرْضِنَا﴾ — Egypt, so that sovereignty in it would be yours — ﴿بِسِحْرِكَ يَا مُوسَى﴾

celaleyn:58-58.t: ﴿فَلَنَأْتِيَنَّكَ بِسِحْرٍ مِثْلِهِ﴾ — to counter it — ﴿فَاجْعَلْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكَ مَوْعِدًا﴾ — for that — ﴿لَا نُخْلِفُهُ نَحْنُ وَلَا أَنْتَ مَكَانًا﴾ — accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ) "fī" — ﴿سِوًى﴾ — with kasra on its first letter, and with ḍamma [سُوًى], i.e. a middle point to which the distance is equal for one coming from either side.

celaleyn:59-59.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ — Mūsā — ﴿مَوْعِدُكُمْ يَوْمُ الزِّينَةِ﴾ — a feast day of theirs on which they adorned themselves and gathered — ﴿وَأَنْ يُحْشَرَ النَّاسُ﴾ — the people of Egypt be gathered — ﴿ضُحًى﴾ — at its forenoon, to watch what would take place.

celaleyn:60-60.t: ﴿فَتَوَلَّى فِرْعَوْنُ﴾ — turned back — ﴿فَجَمَعَ كَيْدَهُ﴾ — i.e. the people of his scheme, from among the sorcerers — ﴿ثُمَّ أَتَى﴾ — with them, at the appointed time.

celaleyn:61-61.t: ﴿قَالَ لَهُمْ مُوسَى﴾ — and they were seventy-two, each with a rope and a staff — ﴿وَيْلَكُمْ﴾ — i.e. may Allah make woe cling to you — ﴿لَا تَفْتَرُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا﴾ — by associating anyone with Him — ﴿فَيُسْحِتَكُمْ﴾ — with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the ḥāʾ, and with fatḥa on both, i.e. He will destroy you — ﴿بِعَذَابٍ﴾ — from Him. ﴿وَقَدْ خَابَ﴾ — has lost — ﴿مَنِ افْتَرَى﴾ — lied against Allah.

celaleyn:62-62.t: ﴿فَتَنَازَعُوا أَمْرَهُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ — concerning Mūsā and his brother — ﴿وَأَسَرُّوا النَّجْوَى﴾ — i.e. the talk among them about the two of them.

celaleyn:63-63.t: ﴿قَالُوا﴾ — to themselves — ﴿إِنَّ هَذَيْنِ﴾ — this is Abū ʿAmr's [reading], and for the others [هَذَانِ], which agrees with the dialect of those who use the alif in the dual in all three of its cases — ﴿لَسَاحِرَانِ يُرِيدَانِ أَنْ يُخْرِجَاكُمْ مِنْ أَرْضِكُمْ بِسِحْرِهِمَا وَيَذْهَبَا بِطَرِيقَتِكُمُ الْمُثْلَى﴾ — feminine of amthal, meaning "most noble", i.e. with your nobles, by their inclining to the two of them because of their victory.

celaleyn:64-64.t: ﴿فَاجْمَعُوا كَيْدَكُمْ﴾ — of sorcery; with the connecting hamza (hamzat waṣl) and fatḥa on the mīm, from "jamaʿa", i.e. "gather together"; and with the disjunctive hamza (hamzat qaṭʿ) and kasra on the mīm [فَأَجْمِعُوا], from "ajmaʿa": "make firm". ﴿ثُمَّ ائْتُوا صَفًّا﴾ — a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. lined up in ranks. ﴿وَقَدْ أَفْلَحَ﴾ — has succeeded — ﴿الْيَوْمَ مَنِ اسْتَعْلَى﴾ — prevailed.

celaleyn:65-65.t: ﴿قَالُوا يَا مُوسَى﴾ — choose — ﴿إِمَّا أَنْ تُلْقِيَ﴾ — your staff, i.e. first — ﴿وَإِمَّا أَنْ نَكُونَ أَوَّلَ مَنْ أَلْقَى﴾ — his staff.

celaleyn:66-66.t: ﴿قَالَ بَلْ أَلْقُوا﴾ — so they threw — ﴿فَإِذَا حِبَالُهُمْ وَعِصِيُّهُمْ﴾ — its original form is ʿuṣuwwun; the two wāws were changed into two yāʾs, and the ʿayn and the ṣād were given kasra — ﴿يُخَيَّلُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ سِحْرِهِمْ أَنَّهَا﴾ — snakes — ﴿تَسْعَى﴾ — on their bellies.

celaleyn:67-67.t: ﴿فَأَوْجَسَ﴾ — sensed — ﴿فِي نَفْسِهِ خِيفَةً مُوسَى﴾ — i.e. he feared, on account of their sorcery being of the same kind as his miracles, that his matter would become confused for the people and they would not believe in him.

celaleyn:68-68.t: ﴿قُلْنَا﴾ — to him — ﴿لَا تَخَفْ إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْأَعْلَى﴾ — over them, by victory.

celaleyn:69-69.t: ﴿وَأَلْقِ مَا فِي يَمِينِكَ﴾ — and it was his staff — ﴿تَلْقَفْ﴾ — it will swallow — ﴿مَا صَنَعُوا إِنَّمَا صَنَعُوا كَيْدُ سَاحِرٍ﴾ — i.e. of its kind — ﴿وَلَا يُفْلِحُ السَّاحِرُ حَيْثُ أَتَى﴾ — with his sorcery. So Mūsā threw his staff, and it swallowed everything they had made.

celaleyn:70-70.t: ﴿فَأُلْقِيَ السَّحَرَةُ سُجَّدًا﴾ — they fell down prostrating to Allah the Exalted. ﴿قَالُوا آمَنَّا بِرَبِّ هَارُونَ وَمُوسَى﴾

celaleyn:71-71.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ — Pharaoh — ﴿أَآمَنْتُمْ﴾ — with both hamzas pronounced fully, and with the second changed into an alif [آمَنْتُمْ] — ﴿لَهُ قَبْلَ أَنْ آذَنَ﴾ — I — ﴿لَكُمْ إِنَّهُ لَكَبِيرُكُمْ﴾ — your teacher — ﴿الَّذِي عَلَّمَكُمُ السِّحْرَ فَلَأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ مِنْ خِلَافٍ﴾ — a ḥāl (circumstantial) meaning "on opposite sides", i.e. the right hands and the left feet — ﴿وَلَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ فِي جُذُوعِ النَّخْلِ﴾ — i.e. on them — ﴿وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ أَيُّنَا﴾ — meaning himself and the Lord of Mūsā — ﴿أَشَدُّ عَذَابًا وَأَبْقَى﴾ — more lasting, for opposing him.

celaleyn:72-72.t: ﴿قَالُوا لَنْ نُؤْثِرَكَ﴾ — choose you — ﴿عَلَى مَا جَاءَنَا مِنَ الْبَيِّنَاتِ﴾ — which prove Mūsā's truthfulness — ﴿وَالَّذِي فَطَرَنَا﴾ — created us; an oath, or conjoined (maʿṭūf) to "mā". ﴿فَاقْضِ مَا أَنْتَ قَاضٍ﴾ — i.e. do what you have said. ﴿إِنَّمَا تَقْضِي هَذِهِ الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا﴾ — the accusative is by extension (ʿalā al-ittisāʿ), i.e. in it; and you will be requited for it in the Hereafter.

celaleyn:73-73.t: ﴿إِنَّا آمَنَّا بِرَبِّنَا لِيَغْفِرَ لَنَا خَطَايَانَا﴾ — of associating partners and other things — ﴿وَمَا أَكْرَهْتَنَا عَلَيْهِ مِنَ السِّحْرِ﴾ — in learning and practice, to counter Mūsā. ﴿وَاللَّهُ خَيْرٌ﴾ — than you in reward when obeyed — ﴿وَأَبْقَى﴾ — than you in punishment when disobeyed. The Exalted said:

celaleyn:74-74.t: ﴿إِنَّهُ مَنْ يَأْتِ رَبَّهُ مُجْرِمًا﴾ — a disbeliever, like Pharaoh — ﴿فَإِنَّ لَهُ جَهَنَّمَ لَا يَمُوتُ فِيهَا﴾ — so as to find rest — ﴿وَلَا يَحْيَى﴾ — a life that benefits him.

celaleyn:75-75.t: ﴿وَمَنْ يَأْتِهِ مُؤْمِنًا قَدْ عَمِلَ الصَّالِحَاتِ﴾ — the obligatory and the supererogatory — ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ لَهُمُ الدَّرَجَاتُ الْعُلَى﴾ — plural of ʿulyā, feminine of aʿlā.

celaleyn:76-76.t: ﴿جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ﴾ — i.e. of residence; an explication (bayān) of it — ﴿تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا وَذَلِكَ جَزَاءُ مَنْ تَزَكَّى﴾ — purified himself of sins.

celaleyn:77-77.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَى مُوسَى أَنْ أَسْرِ بِعِبَادِي﴾ — with the disjunctive hamza (hamzat qaṭʿ), from asrā, and with the connecting hamza (hamzat waṣl) and kasra on the nūn, from sarā — two dialects; i.e. travel with them by night from the land of Egypt — ﴿فَاضْرِبْ﴾ — make — ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ — by striking with your staff — ﴿طَرِيقًا فِي الْبَحْرِ يَبَسًا﴾ — i.e. dry. So he carried out what he was commanded, and Allah dried the ground, and they passed through it. ﴿لَا تَخَافُ دَرَكًا﴾ — i.e. that Pharaoh would overtake you — ﴿وَلَا تَخْشَى﴾ — drowning.

celaleyn:78-78.t: ﴿فَأَتْبَعَهُمْ فِرْعَوْنُ بِجُنُودِهِ﴾ — and he was with them — ﴿فَغَشِيَهُمْ مِنَ الْيَمِّ﴾ — i.e. the sea — ﴿مَا غَشِيَهُمْ﴾ — and drowned them.

celaleyn:79-79.t: ﴿وَأَضَلَّ فِرْعَوْنُ قَوْمَهُ﴾ — by calling them to worship him — ﴿وَمَا هَدَى﴾ — rather he cast them into destruction, contrary to his saying {وَمَا أَهْدِيكُمْ إِلَّا سَبِيلَ الرَّشَادِ}.

celaleyn:80-80.t: ﴿يَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ قَدْ أَنْجَيْنَاكُمْ مِنْ عَدُوِّكُمْ﴾ — Pharaoh, by drowning him — ﴿وَوَاعَدْنَاكُمْ جَانِبَ الطُّورِ الْأَيْمَنَ﴾ — so We would give Mūsā the Torah to act upon — ﴿وَنَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَنَّ وَالسَّلْوَى﴾ — they are taranjabīn (manna) and the bird al-sumānā (quail), with the mīm without shadda and with the short ending. Those addressed are the Jews present in the time of the Prophet ﷺ; they were addressed with what Allah bestowed upon their ancestors in the time of the Prophet Mūsā, as a preparation for His words, the Exalted, to them:

celaleyn:81-81.t: ﴿كُلُوا مِنْ طَيِّبَاتِ مَا رَزَقْنَاكُمْ﴾ — i.e. what has been bestowed upon you — ﴿وَلَا تَطْغَوْا فِيهِ﴾ — by being ungrateful for the blessing of it — ﴿فَيَحِلَّ عَلَيْكُمْ غَضَبِي﴾ — with kasra on the ḥāʾ, i.e. becomes due, and with ḍamma on it, i.e. descends — ﴿وَمَنْ يَحْلِلْ عَلَيْهِ غَضَبِي﴾ — with kasra on the lām and with ḍamma — ﴿فَقَدْ هَوَى﴾ — has fallen into the Fire.

celaleyn:82-82.t: ﴿وَإِنِّي لَغَفَّارٌ لِمَنْ تَابَ﴾ — from idolatry (shirk) — ﴿وَآمَنَ﴾ — affirmed the oneness of Allah — ﴿وَعَمِلَ صَالِحًا﴾ — it applies to the obligatory and the supererogatory — ﴿ثُمَّ اهْتَدَى﴾ — by persisting in what has been mentioned until his death.

celaleyn:83-83.t: ﴿وَمَا أَعْجَلَكَ عَنْ قَوْمِكَ﴾ — in coming to the appointment for receiving the Torah — ﴿يَا مُوسَى﴾

celaleyn:84-84.t: ﴿قَالَ هُمْ أُولَاءِ﴾ — i.e. near me, coming — ﴿عَلَى أَثَرِي وَعَجِلْتُ إِلَيْكَ رَبِّ لِتَرْضَى﴾ — with me, i.e. in addition to Your good pleasure. Before the answer he offered an excuse according to what he supposed, and what he supposed did not hold, because of what [follows]: [Translator's note: the text ends with «لِمَا» "because of what", which runs on into the next ayah.]

celaleyn:85-85.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ — the Exalted — ﴿فَإِنَّا قَدْ فَتَنَّا قَوْمَكَ مِنْ بَعْدِكَ﴾ — i.e. after your parting from them — ﴿وَأَضَلَّهُمُ السَّامِرِيُّ﴾ — so they worshipped the calf.

celaleyn:86-86.t: ﴿فَرَجَعَ مُوسَى إِلَى قَوْمِهِ غَضْبَانَ﴾ — on account of them — ﴿أَسِفًا﴾ — intensely grieved. ﴿قَالَ يَا قَوْمِ أَلَمْ يَعِدْكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ وَعْدًا حَسَنًا﴾ — i.e. a true one, that He would give you the Torah? ﴿أَفَطَالَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْعَهْدُ﴾ — the period of my separation from you — ﴿أَمْ أَرَدْتُمْ أَنْ يَحِلَّ﴾ — become due — ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ غَضَبٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ﴾ — through your worship of the calf — ﴿فَأَخْلَفْتُمْ مَوْعِدِي﴾ — and abandoned coming after me?

celaleyn:87-87.t: ﴿قَالُوا مَا أَخْلَفْنَا مَوْعِدَكَ بِمَلْكِنَا﴾ — with the mīm taking any of the three vowels, i.e. by our own power or choice — ﴿وَلَكِنَّا حَمَلْنَا﴾ — with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ and without shadda, and with ḍamma on it and kasra on the mīm with shadda [حُمِّلْنَا] — ﴿أَوْزَارًا﴾ — loads — ﴿مِنْ زِينَةِ الْقَوْمِ﴾ — i.e. the jewellery of Pharaoh's people, which the Children of Israel had borrowed from them on the pretext of a wedding, and it remained with them — ﴿فَقَذَفْنَاهَا﴾ — we threw it into the fire, at the command of al-Sāmirī — ﴿فَكَذَلِكَ﴾ — just as we threw — ﴿أَلْقَى السَّامِرِيُّ﴾ — what he had with him of their jewellery and of the dust he had taken from the hoofprint of Jibrīl's horse, in the way that will come.

celaleyn:88-88.t: ﴿فَأَخْرَجَ لَهُمْ عِجْلًا﴾ — which he cast from the jewellery — ﴿جَسَدًا﴾ — flesh and blood — ﴿لَهُ خُوَارٌ﴾ — i.e. an audible sound; i.e. it was transformed thus because of the dust, whose effect is life in whatever it is placed in; and he placed it in its mouth after casting it. ﴿فَقَالُوا﴾ — i.e. al-Sāmirī and his followers — ﴿هَذَا إِلَهُكُمْ وَإِلَهُ مُوسَى فَنَسِيَ﴾ — Mūsā forgot his Lord here and went off seeking Him. The Exalted said:

celaleyn:89-89.t: ﴿أَفَلَا يَرَوْنَ أَلَّا﴾ — "an" is lightened from the heavy one (mukhaffafa min al-thaqīla), and its noun is omitted, i.e. "that it does not" — ﴿يَرْجِعُ﴾ — the calf — ﴿إِلَيْهِمْ قَوْلًا﴾ — i.e. does not return an answer to them — ﴿وَلَا يَمْلِكُ لَهُمْ ضَرًّا﴾ — i.e. to ward it off — ﴿وَلَا نَفْعًا﴾ — i.e. to bring it? I.e. so how can it be taken as a god?

celaleyn:90-90.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ قَالَ لَهُمْ هَارُونُ مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ — i.e. before Mūsā returned — ﴿يَا قَوْمِ إِنَّمَا فُتِنْتُمْ بِهِ وَإِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ الرَّحْمَنُ فَاتَّبِعُونِي﴾ — in worshipping Him — ﴿وَأَطِيعُوا أَمْرِي﴾ — in it.

celaleyn:91-91.t: ﴿قَالُوا لَنْ نَبْرَحَ﴾ — we will not cease — ﴿عَلَيْهِ عَاكِفِينَ﴾ — persisting in worshipping it — ﴿حَتَّى يَرْجِعَ إِلَيْنَا مُوسَى﴾

celaleyn:92-92.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ — Mūsā, after his return — ﴿يَا هَارُونُ مَا مَنَعَكَ إِذْ رَأَيْتَهُمْ ضَلُّوا﴾ — by worshipping it,

celaleyn:93-93.t: ﴿أَلَّا تَتَّبِعَنِ﴾ — "lā" is redundant (zāʾida). ﴿أَفَعَصَيْتَ أَمْرِي﴾ — by your remaining among those who worship other than Allah the Exalted?

celaleyn:94-94.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ — Hārūn — ﴿يَا ابْنَ أُمِّ﴾ — with kasra on the mīm and with fatḥa on it [أُمَّ]; he meant "my mother", and mentioning her is more apt to soften his heart — ﴿لَا تَأْخُذْ بِلِحْيَتِي﴾ — he had seized it with his left hand — ﴿وَلَا بِرَأْسِي﴾ — he had seized his hair with his right hand, in anger. ﴿إِنِّي خَشِيتُ﴾ — if I had followed you, and a group of those who had not worshipped the calf would inevitably have followed me — ﴿أَنْ تَقُولَ فَرَّقْتَ بَيْنَ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾ — and be angry with me — ﴿وَلَمْ تَرْقُبْ﴾ — wait for — ﴿قَوْلِي﴾ — about what I saw [fit] in that.

celaleyn:95-95.t: ﴿قَالَ فَمَا خَطْبُكَ﴾ — your affair, which led to what you did — ﴿يَا سَامِرِيُّ﴾

celaleyn:96-96.t: ﴿قَالَ بَصُرْتُ بِمَا لَمْ يَبْصُرُوا بِهِ﴾ — with yāʾ and with tāʾ, i.e. I knew what they did not know — ﴿فَقَبَضْتُ قَبْضَةً مِنْ﴾ — the dust of — ﴿أَثَرِ﴾ — the hoof of the horse of — ﴿الرَّسُولِ﴾ — Jibrīl — ﴿فَنَبَذْتُهَا﴾ — I threw it into the form of the cast calf. ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ سَوَّلَتْ﴾ — made attractive — ﴿لِي نَفْسِي﴾ — and it was cast into it that I should take a handful of the dust mentioned and throw it on what has no soul, and it would come to have a soul. And I saw that your people had asked you to make a god for them, so my soul suggested to me that this calf should be their god.

celaleyn:97-97.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ — Mūsā to him — ﴿فَاذْهَبْ﴾ — from among us — ﴿فَإِنَّ لَكَ فِي الْحَيَاةِ﴾ — i.e. for the duration of your life — ﴿أَنْ تَقُولَ﴾ — to whomever you see — ﴿لَا مِسَاسَ﴾ — i.e. do not come near me. So he used to wander in the wilderness, and whenever he touched anyone or anyone touched him, they both came down with fever. ﴿وَإِنَّ لَكَ مَوْعِدًا﴾ — for your punishment — ﴿لَنْ تُخْلِفَهُ﴾ — with kasra on the lām, i.e. you will not be absent from it, and with fatḥa on it [تُخْلَفَهُ], i.e. rather you will be raised up to it. ﴿وَانْظُرْ إِلَى إِلَهِكَ الَّذِي ظَلْتَ﴾ — its original form is ẓalilta, with two lāms, the first of which has kasra; it was dropped for lightness; i.e. you continued — ﴿عَلَيْهِ عَاكِفًا﴾ — i.e. remaining in worship of it — ﴿لَنُحَرِّقَنَّهُ﴾ — with fire — ﴿ثُمَّ لَنَنْسِفَنَّهُ فِي الْيَمِّ نَسْفًا﴾ — We will scatter it in the air over the sea. And Mūsā, after slaughtering it, did what he mentioned.

celaleyn:98-98.t: ﴿إِنَّمَا إِلَهُكُمُ اللَّهُ الَّذِي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَسِعَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ عِلْمًا﴾ — a tamyīz (specification) converted from the fāʿil (agent), i.e. His knowledge encompasses everything.

celaleyn:99-99.t: ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ — i.e. just as We have narrated this story to you, O Muḥammad — ﴿نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ مِنْ أَنْبَاءِ﴾ — the reports of — ﴿مَا قَدْ سَبَقَ﴾ — of the nations — ﴿وَقَدْ آتَيْنَاكَ﴾ — We have given you — ﴿مِنْ لَدُنَّا﴾ — from Us — ﴿ذِكْرًا﴾ — a Quran.

celaleyn:100-100.t: ﴿مَنْ أَعْرَضَ عَنْهُ﴾ — and did not believe in it — ﴿فَإِنَّهُ يَحْمِلُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَمَةِ وِزْرًا﴾ — a heavy load of sin,

celaleyn:101-101.t: ﴿خَالِدِينَ فِيهِ﴾ — i.e. in the punishment of the burden. ﴿وَسَاءَ لَهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَمَةِ حِمْلًا﴾ — a tamyīz (specification) explaining the pronoun in "sāʾa", and the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being "their burden"; and the lām is for clarification (li-l-bayān). And there is substituted (badal) from "yawm al-qiyāma":

celaleyn:102-102.t: ﴿يَوْمَ يُنْفَخُ فِي الصُّورِ﴾ — the horn — the second blowing — ﴿وَنَحْشُرُ الْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾ — the disbelievers — ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ زُرْقًا﴾ — their eyes [blue], along with the blackness of their faces.

celaleyn:103-103.t: ﴿يَتَخَافَتُونَ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ — whispering to one another: ﴿إِنْ﴾ — "not" — ﴿لَبِثْتُمْ﴾ — in the world — ﴿إِلَّا عَشْرًا﴾ — nights, with their days.

celaleyn:104-104.t: ﴿نَحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يَقُولُونَ﴾ — about that, i.e. it is not as they said — ﴿إِذْ يَقُولُ أَمْثَلُهُمْ﴾ — the most balanced of them — ﴿طَرِيقَةً﴾ — in it: ﴿إِنْ لَبِثْتُمْ إِلَّا يَوْمًا﴾ — they deem their stay in the world very short because of the terrors of the Hereafter that they witness.

celaleyn:105-105.t: ﴿وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْجِبَالِ﴾ — how they will be on the Day of Resurrection — ﴿فَقُلْ﴾ — to them — ﴿يَنْسِفُهَا رَبِّي نَسْفًا﴾ — by crumbling them like flowing sand, then it is blown away by the wind.

celaleyn:107-107.t: ﴿لَا تَرَى فِيهَا عِوَجًا﴾ — a depression — ﴿وَلَا أَمْتًا﴾ — an elevation.

celaleyn:108-108.t: ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ — i.e. on the day when the mountains are blown away — ﴿يَتَّبِعُونَ﴾ — i.e. people, after rising from the graves — ﴿الدَّاعِيَ﴾ — to the place of gathering, with his voice; and he is Isrāfīl, saying: "Come to the presentation before the Most Merciful" — ﴿لَا عِوَجَ لَهُ﴾ — i.e. to their following him; i.e. they are not able not to follow. ﴿وَخَشَعَتِ﴾ — became still — ﴿الْأَصْوَاتُ لِلرَّحْمَنِ فَلَا تَسْمَعُ إِلَّا هَمْسًا﴾ — the sound of the treading of feet as they move to the place of gathering, like the sound of camels' pads as they walk.

celaleyn:109-109.t: ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ لَا تَنْفَعُ الشَّفَاعَةُ﴾ — anyone — ﴿إِلَّا مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ الرَّحْمَنُ﴾ — that intercession be made for him — ﴿وَرَضِيَ لَهُ قَوْلًا﴾ — by his saying "there is no god but Allah".

celaleyn:110-110.t: ﴿يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ — of the affairs of the Hereafter — ﴿وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ﴾ — of the affairs of this world — ﴿وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِهِ عِلْمًا﴾ — they do not know that.

celaleyn:111-111.t: ﴿وَعَنَتِ الْوُجُوهُ﴾ — submitted — ﴿لِلْحَيِّ الْقَيُّومِ﴾ — i.e. Allah. ﴿وَقَدْ خَابَ﴾ — has lost — ﴿مَنْ حَمَلَ ظُلْمًا﴾ — i.e. idolatry (shirk).

celaleyn:112-112.t: ﴿وَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِنَ الصَّالِحَاتِ﴾ — acts of obedience — ﴿وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَلَا يَخَافُ ظُلْمًا﴾ — through an increase in his bad deeds — ﴿وَلَا هَضْمًا﴾ — through a decrease in his good deeds.

celaleyn:113-113.t: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ﴾ — conjoined (maʿṭūf) to "kadhālika naquṣṣu", i.e. like the sending down of what has been mentioned — ﴿أَنْزَلْنَاهُ﴾ — i.e. the Quran — ﴿قُرْآنًا عَرَبِيًّا وَصَرَّفْنَا﴾ — We repeated — ﴿فِيهِ مِنَ الْوَعِيدِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ﴾ — idolatry — ﴿أَوْ يُحْدِثُ﴾ — the Quran — ﴿لَهُمْ ذِكْرًا﴾ — of the destruction of the nations that preceded them, so that they take heed.

celaleyn:114-114.t: ﴿فَتَعَالَى اللَّهُ الْمَلِكُ الْحَقُّ﴾ — above what the idolaters say. ﴿وَلَا تَعْجَلْ بِالْقُرْآنِ﴾ — i.e. in reciting it — ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يُقْضَى إِلَيْكَ وَحْيُهُ﴾ — i.e. before Jibrīl finishes conveying it. ﴿وَقُلْ رَبِّ زِدْنِي عِلْمًا﴾ — i.e. of the Quran; so whenever something of it was sent down to him, his knowledge increased by it.

celaleyn:115-115.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ عَهِدْنَا إِلَى آدَمَ﴾ — We enjoined him not to eat from the tree — ﴿مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ — i.e. before his eating from it — ﴿فَنَسِيَ﴾ — he abandoned Our covenant — ﴿وَلَمْ نَجِدْ لَهُ عَزْمًا﴾ — firmness and patience in refraining from what We forbade him.

celaleyn:116-116.t: ﴿وَ﴾ — remember — ﴿إِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ اسْجُدُوا لِآدَمَ فَسَجَدُوا إِلَّا إِبْلِيسَ﴾ — and he is the father of the jinn; he used to keep company with the angels and worship Allah with them — ﴿أَبَى﴾ — to prostrate to Ādam; he said, "I am better than him."

celaleyn:117-117.t: ﴿فَقُلْنَا يَا آدَمُ إِنَّ هَذَا عَدُوٌّ لَكَ وَلِزَوْجِكَ﴾ — Ḥawwāʾ, with the long vowel — ﴿فَلَا يُخْرِجَنَّكُمَا مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ فَتَشْقَى﴾ — and toil at ploughing, sowing, reaping, grinding, baking and other than that. He limited it to his toil because the man labours for his wife.

celaleyn:118-118.t: ﴿إِنَّ لَكَ أَلَّا تَجُوعَ فِيهَا وَلَا تَعْرَى﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:119-119.t: ﴿وَأَنَّكَ﴾ — with fatḥa on the hamza and with kasra on it; conjoined to the noun of "inna" and to its clause — ﴿لَا تَظْمَأُ فِيهَا﴾ — become thirsty — ﴿وَلَا تَضْحَى﴾ — the heat of the forenoon sun will not reach you, because there is no sun in Paradise.

celaleyn:120-120.t: ﴿فَوَسْوَسَ إِلَيْهِ الشَّيْطَانُ قَالَ يَا آدَمُ هَلْ أَدُلُّكَ عَلَى شَجَرَةِ الْخُلْدِ﴾ — i.e. the one whoever eats from it lives forever — ﴿وَمُلْكٍ لَا يَبْلَى﴾ — does not perish; and it is a necessary consequence of eternal life.

celaleyn:121-121.t: ﴿فَأَكَلَا﴾ — i.e. Ādam and Ḥawwāʾ — ﴿مِنْهَا فَبَدَتْ لَهُمَا سَوْآتُهُمَا﴾ — i.e. to each of them his own front private part and that of the other, and his rear, became visible; each of them is called sawʾa because its exposure distresses (yasūʾu) its owner — ﴿وَطَفِقَا يَخْصِفَانِ﴾ — they began to stick — ﴿عَلَيْهِمَا مِنْ وَرَقِ الْجَنَّةِ﴾ — to cover themselves with it. ﴿وَعَصَى آدَمُ رَبَّهُ فَغَوَى﴾ — by eating from the tree.

celaleyn:122-122.t: ﴿ثُمَّ اجْتَبَاهُ رَبُّهُ﴾ — brought him near — ﴿فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ﴾ — accepted his repentance — ﴿وَهَدَى﴾ — i.e. guided him to persevere in repentance.

celaleyn:123-123.t: ﴿قَالَ اهْبِطَا﴾ — i.e. Ādam and Ḥawwāʾ, together with the offspring you contain — ﴿مِنْهَا﴾ — from Paradise — ﴿جَمِيعًا بَعْضُكُمْ﴾ — some of the offspring — ﴿لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ﴾ — through some of them wronging others. ﴿فَإِمَّا﴾ — in it is the assimilation of the nūn of the conditional "in" into the added "mā" — ﴿يَأْتِيَنَّكُمْ مِنِّي هُدًى فَمَنِ اتَّبَعَ هُدَايَ﴾ — i.e. the Quran — ﴿فَلَا يَضِلُّ﴾ — in this world — ﴿وَلَا يَشْقَى﴾ — in the Hereafter.

celaleyn:124-124.t: ﴿وَمَنْ أَعْرَضَ عَنْ ذِكْرِي﴾ — i.e. the Quran, and did not believe in it — ﴿فَإِنَّ لَهُ مَعِيشَةً ضَنْكًا﴾ — with tanwīn; a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning "narrow"; and in a ḥadīth it is explained as the punishment of the disbeliever in his grave — ﴿وَنَحْشُرُهُ﴾ — i.e. the one who turns away from the Quran — ﴿يَوْمَ الْقِيَمَةِ أَعْمَى﴾ — blind of sight.

celaleyn:125-125.t: ﴿قَالَ رَبِّ لِمَ حَشَرْتَنِي أَعْمَى وَقَدْ كُنْتُ بَصِيرًا﴾ — in the world and at the resurrection?

celaleyn:126-126.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ — the matter is — ﴿كَذَلِكَ أَتَتْكَ آيَاتُنَا فَنَسِيتَهَا﴾ — you abandoned them and did not believe in them — ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ﴾ — like your forgetting Our signs — ﴿الْيَوْمَ تُنْسَى﴾ — you are left in the Fire.

celaleyn:127-127.t: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ﴾ — and like Our requiting of whoever turns away from the Quran — ﴿نَجْزِي مَنْ أَسْرَفَ﴾ — associated partners with Allah — ﴿وَلَمْ يُؤْمِنْ بِآيَاتِ رَبِّهِ وَلَعَذَابُ الْآخِرَةِ أَشَدُّ﴾ — than the punishment of this world and the punishment of the grave — ﴿وَأَبْقَى﴾ — more lasting.

celaleyn:128-128.t: ﴿أَفَلَمْ يَهْدِ﴾ — has it not become clear — ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ — to the disbelievers of Mecca — ﴿كَمْ﴾ — the declarative (khabariyya) [kam], a mafʿūl (object) — ﴿أَهْلَكْنَا﴾ — i.e. Our destruction of many — ﴿قَبْلَهُمْ مِنَ الْقُرُونِ﴾ — i.e. the past nations, for denying the messengers — ﴿يَمْشُونَ﴾ — a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of "lahum" — ﴿فِي مَسَاكِنِهِمْ﴾ — on their journeys to Syria and elsewhere, so that they may take heed. And what has been mentioned, namely taking [the maṣdar] "ihlāk" from its verb, which is free of a maṣdar-forming particle, out of regard for the meaning, there is nothing to prevent it. ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ﴾ — lessons — ﴿لِأُولِي النُّهَى﴾ — for those possessed of intellects.

celaleyn:129-129.t: ﴿وَلَوْلَا كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾ — to postpone the punishment from them until the Hereafter — ﴿لَكَانَ﴾ — the destruction — ﴿لِزَامًا﴾ — binding upon them in this world. ﴿وَأَجَلٌ مُسَمًّى﴾ — set for them; conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the latent (mustatir) pronoun in "kāna", and the separation by its khabar (predicate) took the place of the tawkīd (emphasis).

celaleyn:130-130.t: ﴿فَاصْبِرْ عَلَى مَا يَقُولُونَ﴾ — abrogated by the verse of fighting — ﴿وَسَبِّحْ﴾ — pray — ﴿بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ﴾ — a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. accompanied by it — ﴿قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ﴾ — the dawn prayer — ﴿وَقَبْلَ غُرُوبِهَا﴾ — the afternoon (ʿaṣr) prayer — ﴿وَمِنْ آنَاءِ اللَّيْلِ﴾ — its hours — ﴿فَسَبِّحْ﴾ — pray the sunset (maghrib) and the night (ʿishāʾ) prayers — ﴿وَأَطْرَافَ النَّهَارِ﴾ — conjoined to the position of "min ānāʾi", which is accusative; i.e. pray the noon (ẓuhr) prayer, because its time begins with the sun's passing the meridian, so it is the end of the first half and the beginning of the second half — ﴿لَعَلَّكَ تَرْضَى﴾ — with the reward you will be given.

celaleyn:131-131.t: ﴿وَلَا تَمُدَّنَّ عَيْنَيْكَ إِلَى مَا مَتَّعْنَا بِهِ أَزْوَاجًا﴾ — kinds — ﴿مِنْهُمْ زَهْرَةَ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا﴾ — its adornment and splendour — ﴿لِنَفْتِنَهُمْ فِيهِ﴾ — in that they transgress. ﴿وَرِزْقُ رَبِّكَ﴾ — in Paradise — ﴿خَيْرٌ﴾ — than what they have been given in this world — ﴿وَأَبْقَى﴾ — more lasting.

celaleyn:132-132.t: ﴿وَأْمُرْ أَهْلَكَ بِالصَّلَوةِ وَاصْطَبِرْ﴾ — be patient — ﴿عَلَيْهَا لَا نَسْأَلُكَ﴾ — We do not charge you with — ﴿رِزْقًا﴾ — for yourself or for anyone else. ﴿نَحْنُ نَرْزُقُكَ وَالْعَاقِبَةُ﴾ — Paradise — ﴿لِلتَّقْوَى﴾ — for its people.

celaleyn:133-133.t: ﴿وَقَالُوا﴾ — i.e. the idolaters — ﴿لَوْلَا﴾ — why does not — ﴿يَأْتِينَا﴾ — Muḥammad — ﴿بِآيَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّهِ﴾ — of those they propose? ﴿أَوَلَمْ تَأْتِهِمْ﴾ — with tāʾ and with yāʾ — ﴿بَيِّنَةُ﴾ — the explanation of — ﴿مَا فِي الصُّحُفِ الْأُولَى﴾ — which the Quran contains, of the reports of the past nations and their destruction for denying the messengers?

celaleyn:134-134.t: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّا أَهْلَكْنَاهُمْ بِعَذَابٍ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ﴾ — before Muḥammad the Messenger — ﴿لَقَالُوا﴾ — on the Day of Resurrection — ﴿رَبَّنَا لَوْلَا﴾ — why did You not — ﴿أَرْسَلْتَ إِلَيْنَا رَسُولًا فَنَتَّبِعَ آيَاتِكَ﴾ — sent with him — ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ نَذِلَّ﴾ — at the Resurrection — ﴿وَنَخْزَى﴾ — in Hell?

celaleyn:135-135.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ — to them — ﴿كُلٌّ﴾ — of us and of you — ﴿مُتَرَبِّصٌ﴾ — awaiting how the matter will turn out. ﴿فَتَرَبَّصُوا فَسَتَعْلَمُونَ﴾ — at the Resurrection — ﴿مَنْ أَصْحَابُ الصِّرَاطِ﴾ — the path — ﴿السَّوِيِّ﴾ — the straight — ﴿وَمَنِ اهْتَدَى﴾ — from error: we or you.

daas-irab:126-127.t: ﴿قالَ﴾ the clause is resumptive. ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾ the kāf is a preposition of comparison taking the genitive, and ذا is a demonstrative in the position of the genitive (majrūr) by the kāf; the lām is for distance and the kāf is for address; the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "الأمر كذلك". ﴿أَتَتْكَ﴾ a past verb, and the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿آياتُنا﴾ fāʿil (agent), and نا is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿فَنَسِيتَها﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction; a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined). ﴿وَكَذلِكَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; the kāf is a preposition of comparison taking the genitive and ذا is a demonstrative in the genitive; the two are attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿الْيَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿تُنْسى﴾ a passive imperfect verb, its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَكَذلِكَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; كذلك: the two are attached to an omitted naʿt of a mafʿūl muṭlaq. ﴿نَجْزِي﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent. ﴿مَنْ﴾ a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined. ﴿أَسْرَفَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil latent; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of a relative noun. ﴿وَلَمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and لم is jussive-governing. ﴿يُؤْمِنْ﴾ the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿بِآياتِ﴾ the two are attached to يؤمن. ﴿رَبِّهِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَلَعَذابُ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) and the lām is the lām of commencement (lām al-ibtidāʾ). ﴿عذاب﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿الْآخِرَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَشَدُّ﴾ khabar of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿وَأَبْقى﴾ conjoined to أشد; the clause of mubtadaʾ and khabar is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:128-129.t: ﴿أَفَلَمْ﴾ the hamza is for reproachful interrogation, the fāʾ is a conjunction, and لم is a jussive-governing particle. ﴿يَهْدِ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم; its fāʿil (agent) is the maṣdar (verbal noun) understood from أهلكنا. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) يهد. ﴿كَمْ﴾ it is the declarative (khabariyya) kam, in the position of the accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of أهلكنا. ﴿أَهْلَكْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿قَبْلَهُمْ﴾ an adverb of time, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause ﴿أَهْلَكْنا﴾ may be parsed as the fāʿil of يهد. ﴿مِنَ الْقُرُونِ﴾ the two are attached to a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted tamyīz (specification) of the declarative كم. ﴿يَمْشُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from القرون. ﴿فِي مَساكِنِهِمْ﴾ the two are attached to يمشون, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb. ﴿فِي ذلِكَ﴾ the preposition and the demonstrative are attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿لَآياتٍ﴾ the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); آيات is the postponed noun of إن, accusative (manṣūb) with the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural. ﴿لِأُولِي﴾ the two are attached to a naʿt of آيات. ﴿النُّهى﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) with an implied (muqaddar) kasra; النهى means minds (intellects). ﴿وَلَوْلا﴾ the wāw is resumptive; لولا is conditional, not jussive-governing. ﴿كَلِمَةٌ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar obligatorily omitted, its implied form being "موجودة". ﴿سَبَقَتْ﴾ the clause is a naʿt of كلمة. ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾ the two are attached to سبقت. ﴿لَكانَ﴾ the lām occurs in the apodosis of لولا, and كان is the incomplete (nāqiṣa) one, its noun a latent (mustatir) pronoun. ﴿لِزاماً﴾ khabar of كان. ﴿وَأَجَلٌ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and أجل is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to كلمة. ﴿مُسَمًّى﴾ naʿt of أجل, nominative with an implied ḍamma; the clause لكان is the apodosis of لولا and has no grammatical position, and the clause ﴿لَوْلا﴾ … etc. is resumptive.

daas-irab:130-131.t: ﴿فَاصْبِرْ﴾ the fāʾ is a particle of resumption, and اصبر is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive. ﴿عَلى﴾ a preposition. ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun; the two are attached to (mutaʿalliq) اصبر. ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is a ṣila (relative clause) with no grammatical position. ﴿وَسَبِّحْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and سبح is an imperative verb, its fāʿil latent; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to اصبر. ﴿بِحَمْدِ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "وأنت حامد". ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿قَبْلَ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿طُلُوعِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿الشَّمْسِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَقَبْلَ﴾ conjoined to قبل. ﴿غُرُوبِها﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَمِنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and من is a preposition. ﴿آناءِ﴾ a genitive noun; the two are attached to سبح. ﴿اللَّيْلِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَسَبِّحْ﴾ the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and سبح is an imperative verb, its fāʿil latent; the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَأَطْرافَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; أطراف is conjoined to what precedes. ﴿النَّهارِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لَعَلَّكَ﴾ لعل and its noun. ﴿تَرْضى﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma, its fāʿil latent; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of لعل, and the clause ﴿لَعَلَّكَ تَرْضى..﴾ is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the fāʿil of سبح. ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and لا is prohibitive. ﴿تَمُدَّنَّ﴾ an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis, in the position of the jussive by the prohibitive لا; the fāʿil is a latent pronoun. ﴿عَيْنَيْكَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) with the yāʾ because it is a dual, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِلى﴾ a preposition. ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun; the two are attached to تمدن, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿مَتَّعْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿بِهِ﴾ the two are attached to متعنا. ﴿أَزْواجاً﴾ first mafʿūl bihi; أزواجا means kinds (classes). ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective). ﴿زَهْرَةَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi of متع; this is permissible because the meaning of متع is "gave". ﴿الْحَياةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿الدُّنْيا﴾ a naʿt, genitive (majrūr) with an implied kasra; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿لِنَفْتِنَهُمْ﴾ the lām is the lām of causation (taʿlīl); نفتنهم is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied (muḍmara) أن after the lām of causation; the fāʿil is latent and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi; the lām and its genitive are attached to متعنا. ﴿فِيهِ﴾ the two are attached to نفتنهم. ﴿وَرِزْقُ﴾ the wāw is the wāw of ḥāl, and رزق is mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿خَيْرٌ﴾ khabar. ﴿وَأَبْقى﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and أبقى is conjoined to خير; it is nominative like it, with an implied ḍamma on its end, its appearance prevented by impossibility (taʿadhdhur); the clause of mubtadaʾ and khabar is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl.

daas-irab:132-133.t: ﴿وَأْمُرْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; أمر [an imperative verb], its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir). ﴿أَهْلَكَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined). بالصلاة: the two are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb وأمر. [Translator's note: the source places بالصلاة inside the analysis of ﴿أَهْلَكَ﴾ without brackets.] ﴿وَاصْطَبِرْ﴾ the clause is conjoined to وأمر. ﴿عَلَيْها﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to اصطبر. ﴿لا نَسْئَلُكَ﴾ لا is negating; نسألك is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent, and the kāf is the first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿رِزْقاً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿نَحْنُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿نَرْزُقُكَ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent, and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the khabar (predicate). ﴿وَالْعاقِبَةُ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and العاقبة is mubtadaʾ. ﴿لِلتَّقْوى﴾ the two are attached to an omitted khabar; the clause is resumptive, and the preceding clause likewise. ﴿وَقالُوا﴾ the wāw is resumptive; a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿لَوْلا﴾ a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ). ﴿يَأْتِينا﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent, and نا is mafʿūl bihi. ﴿بِآيَةٍ﴾ the two are attached to يأتينا. ﴿مِنْ رَبِّهِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of آية, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech). ﴿أَوَلَمْ﴾ the hamza is for interrogation, and the wāw conjoins to an implied, omitted [clause], its implied form being "ألم تأتهم البينات تترى وألم تأتهم بصورة خاصة ما في الصحف الأولى" (Have not the clear proofs come to them in succession, and has not there come to them, in particular, what is in the former scriptures?). ﴿لَمْ﴾ a jussive-governing particle. ﴿تَأْتِهِمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by deletion of the weak letter, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi. ﴿بَيِّنَةُ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun, badal (substitute) or muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فِي الصُّحُفِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿الْأُولى﴾ naʿt of الصحف, genitive (majrūr) like it with an implied (muqaddar) kasra on its end.

daas-irab:134-135.t: ﴿وَلَوْ﴾ the wāw is a particle of resumption, and لو is a conditional particle, not jussive-governing. ﴿أَنَّا﴾ أن, and نا is its noun. ﴿أَهْلَكْناهُمْ﴾ a past verb, fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of أن, and the clause ﴿أَنَّا أَهْلَكْناهُمْ﴾ is resumptive with no grammatical position. ﴿بِعَذابٍ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) أهلكناهم. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِهِ﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of عذاب, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿لَقالُوا﴾ the lām occurs in the apodosis of لو, and قالوا is a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. ﴿رَبَّنا﴾ the one addressed (munādā) with an omitted vocative particle; it is accusative (manṣūb), and نا is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech). ﴿لَوْلا﴾ a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ). ﴿أَرْسَلْتَ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿إِلَيْنا﴾ the two are attached to أرسلت. ﴿رَسُولًا﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فَنَتَّبِعَ﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ of causation (fāʾ al-sababiyya), and the imperfect verb is accusative by an implied (muḍmara) أن after the fāʾ of causation; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿آياتِكَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, accusative with the kasra in place of the fatḥa because it is a sound feminine plural, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِ﴾ the two are attached to نتبع. ﴿أَنْ﴾ an accusative-governing particle. ﴿نَذِلَّ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative by أن, its fāʿil latent; أن and what follows it are, as an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَنَخْزى﴾ conjoined to نذل. ﴿قُلْ﴾ the clause of the imperative verb and its fāʿil is resumptive. ﴿كُلٌّ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿مُتَرَبِّصٌ﴾ khabar; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl. ﴿فَتَرَبَّصُوا﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition); تربصوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition, its implied form being "إذا كان الأمر كذلك فتربصوا". ﴿فَسَتَعْلَمُونَ﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive, and the imperfect verb is nominative (marfūʿ) by retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿مَنْ﴾ an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ. ﴿أَصْحابُ﴾ khabar of من; the clause fills the place of the two objects of فستعلمون. ﴿الصِّراطِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿السَّوِيِّ﴾ naʿt of الصراط. ﴿وَمَنِ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and من is an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ. ﴿اهْتَدى﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil latent; the clause is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of من, and the clause ﴿مَنِ اهْتَدى﴾ is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to من أصحاب.

daas-irab:1-4.t: ﴿طه﴾ one of the disconnected letters (al-ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭaʿa) of the Qur'an, with no grammatical position. ﴿ما﴾ negative. ﴿أَنْزَلْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); it was also read نزلنا. ﴿عَلَيْكَ﴾ [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to (mutaʿalliq) أنزلنا. ﴿الْقُرْآنَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿لِتَشْقى﴾ the lām is the lām of causation (taʿlīl), and تشقى is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) an after the lām of causation; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir). الشقاء here means toil. The implied an and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of genitive by the lām, [the two being] attached to أنزلنا. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿تَذْكِرَةً﴾ mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); the exception here is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ). ﴿لِمَنْ﴾ the lām is a preposition and man is a relative noun; [the two are] attached to تذكرة. ﴿يَخْشى﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma implied (muqaddara) on the alif owing to impossibility; its fāʿil is latent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿تَنْزِيلًا﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "نزلنا". ﴿مِمَّنْ﴾ min is a preposition and man is a relative noun; [the two are] attached to تنزيلا. ﴿خَلَقَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿الْأَرْضَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَالسَّماواتِ﴾ conjoined to الأرض, and it is accusative like it; the sign of its accusative is the kasra in place of the fatḥa because it is a sound feminine plural. ﴿الْعُلى﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of السموات, and it is accusative like it by the fatḥa implied on the alif owing to impossibility.

daas-irab:5-8.t: ﴿الرَّحْمنُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿عَلَى الْعَرْشِ﴾ [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to (mutaʿalliq) استوى. ﴿اسْتَوى﴾ a past verb; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿لَهُ﴾ attached to a fronted khabar. ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun, mubtadaʾ. ﴿فِي السَّماواتِ﴾ attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined to ما في السموات. ﴿وَما بَيْنَهُما﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَما تَحْتَ﴾ the adverb is attached to the omitted ṣila of mā. ﴿الثَّرى﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr). ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive; in is conditional. ﴿تَجْهَرْ﴾ the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). ﴿بِالْقَوْلِ﴾ attached to تجهر; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿فَإِنَّهُ﴾ the fāʾ links the apodosis, and inna and its noun. ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the khabar of inna. ﴿السِّرَّ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَأَخْفى﴾ conjoined to السر, by the implied (muqaddara) fatḥa. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ. ﴿لا﴾ the lā of generic negation. ﴿إِلهَ﴾ its noun; its khabar is omitted, its implied form being "موجود". ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿هُوَ﴾ a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as badal (substitute) of the latent pronoun implied in the omitted khabar; the clause لا إله is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿لَهُ﴾ attached to a fronted khabar. ﴿الْأَسْماءُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿الْحُسْنى﴾ an adjective (ṣifa), nominative by the implied ḍamma; the clause له الأسماء is a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ.

daas-irab:9-13.t: ﴿وَهَلْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive and hal is an interrogative particle. ﴿أَتاكَ﴾ a past verb and mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿حَدِيثُ﴾ fāʿil (agent). ﴿مُوسى﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is resumptive, with no position. ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) حديث. ﴿رَأى ناراً﴾ a past verb and mafʿūl bihi; the fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَقالَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction; the clause is conjoined to the clause رأى. ﴿لِأَهْلِهِ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to قال; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿امْكُثُوا﴾ an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the deletion of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil and the alif is for separation; the clause is in the position of accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying). ﴿إِنِّي﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿آنَسْتُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause gives the reason for the command. ﴿ناراً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿لَعَلِّي﴾ لعل and its noun. ﴿آتِيكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is a latent pronoun; the kāf is mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the khabar of لعل, in the position of nominative. ﴿مِنْها﴾ attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of قبس. ﴿بِقَبَسٍ﴾ attached to the verb. ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿أَجِدُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿عَلَى النَّارِ﴾ attached to أجد. ﴿هُدىً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فَلَمَّا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction. ﴿لما﴾ an adverb meaning "when" (ḥīna). ﴿أَتاها﴾ a past verb and its object; the fāʿil is latent; the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿نُودِيَ﴾ a passive past verb; the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent pronoun; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. ﴿يا مُوسى﴾ yā is a vocative particle and موسى is the one addressed (munādā). ﴿إِنِّي﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿أَنَا﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿رَبُّكَ﴾ the khabar of أنا; the clause is the khabar of إني. ﴿فَاخْلَعْ نَعْلَيْكَ﴾ the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa fāʾ (al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa), and an imperative verb and its object; the fāʿil is a latent pronoun; the clause has no position, [being] the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. ﴿إِنَّكَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿بِالْوادِ﴾ attached to the khabar. ﴿الْمُقَدَّسِ﴾ a genitive adjective (ṣifa). ﴿طُوىً﴾ badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition); Ṭuwā is the name of the valley. ﴿وَأَنَا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and أنا is mubtadaʾ. ﴿اخْتَرْتُكَ﴾ a past verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the khabar. ﴿فَاسْتَمِعْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction; استمع is an imperative verb whose fāʿil is a latent pronoun. ﴿لِما﴾ attached to استمع. ﴿يُوحى﴾ a passive imperfect verb; the nāʾib fāʿil is a latent pronoun; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative.

daas-irab:14-16.t: ﴿إِنَّنِي﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿أَنَا﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, khabar (predicate); the clause is the khabar of inna. ﴿لا﴾ the lā of generic negation. ﴿إِلهَ﴾ its noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "موجود". ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿أَنَا﴾ badal (substitute) of the latent pronoun implied in the khabar. ﴿فَاعْبُدْنِي﴾ the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa fāʾ (al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa), and an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the yāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause has no position. The clause لا إله إلا أنا is a second khabar, and the clause ﴿وَأَقِمِ الصَّلاةَ﴾ is conjoined to فاعبدني. ﴿لِذِكْرِي﴾ [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to (mutaʿalliq) أقم. ﴿إِنَّ السَّاعَةَ آتِيَةٌ﴾ inna, its noun and its khabar; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿أَكادُ﴾ an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, one of the verbs of approximation; its noun is latent, its implied form being "أنا"; the clause is a second khabar. ﴿أُخْفِيها﴾ the clause is the khabar of أكاد. ﴿لِتُجْزى﴾ the lām is for causation (taʿlīl), and تجزى is a passive imperfect verb. ﴿كُلُّ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿نَفْسٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of genitive by the lām of causation. ﴿بِما﴾ attached to the verb تجزى. ﴿تَسْعى﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿فَلا﴾ the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa fāʾ; lā is prohibitive. ﴿يَصُدَّنَّكَ﴾ an imperfect verb indeclinable on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis, and it is in the position of jussive by the prohibitive lā; the nūn of emphasis is a particle with no grammatical position, and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi. ﴿عَنْها﴾ attached to يصدنك. ﴿مَنْ﴾ a relative noun, fāʿil. ﴿لا يُؤْمِنُ﴾ lā is negative; يؤمن is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿بِها﴾ attached to the verb; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of a relative. ﴿وَاتَّبَعَ هَواهُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; هواه is mafʿūl bihi and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَتَرْدى﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ of causation (al-sababiyya), and تردى is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) an after the fāʾ of causation; its fāʿil is a latent pronoun.

daas-irab:17-18.t: ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle. ﴿ما﴾ an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿تِلْكَ﴾ a demonstrative — the lām is for distance and the kāf is for address — in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate). ﴿بِيَمِينِكَ﴾ [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the demonstrative; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿يا مُوسى﴾ yā is for the vocative, and موسى is the one addressed (munādā), a singular proper noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the implied (muqaddar) أدعو; the vocative clause is resumptive, and likewise the clause that preceded it. ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿هِيَ عَصايَ﴾ mubtadaʾ and khabar; the yāʾ in عصاي is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying). ﴿أَتَوَكَّؤُا﴾ and ﴿أَهُشُّ﴾ two imperfect verbs, the fāʿil of each being latent in it; the clause أتوكأ is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) and the clause ﴿أَهُشُّ﴾ is conjoined to it. ﴿عَلَيْها﴾ attached to أتوكأ. ﴿بِها﴾ attached to أهش, and likewise ﴿عَلى غَنَمِي﴾. ﴿وَلِيَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; لي is attached to a fronted khabar of the postponed mubtadaʾ ﴿مَآرِبُ﴾, and ﴿فِيها﴾ is attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿أُخْرى﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of مآرب; the clause is conjoined to the preceding clause.

daas-irab:19-23.t: ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَلْقِها﴾ an imperative verb and its object; the fāʿil is latent; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying). ﴿يا مُوسى﴾ the vocative clause is also the maqūl al-qawl. ﴿فَأَلْقاها﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its object, its fāʿil being "هو"; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿فَإِذا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and إذا of surprise (al-fujāʾiyya) is an adverb of time. ﴿هِيَ حَيَّةٌ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); the clause is conjoined. ﴿تَسْعى﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of حية. ﴿قالَ﴾ the clause is resumptive. ﴿خُذْها﴾ an imperative verb and its object; its fāʿil is a latent pronoun; the clause is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of قال. ﴿وَلا تَخَفْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and lā is prohibitive; تخف is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā; the clause is conjoined. ﴿سَنُعِيدُها﴾ an imperfect verb and its object; its fāʿil is a latent pronoun; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl. ﴿سِيرَتَهَا﴾ accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), the implied form being "إلى سيرتها"; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿الْأُولى﴾ an adjective of سيرتها, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra implied on the alif maqṣūra. [Translator's note: so in the source; since سيرتها is accusative by the source's own analysis, its adjective would be accusative by the implied fatḥa.] ﴿وَاضْمُمْ يَدَكَ﴾ the clause consisting of the verb, its latent fāʿil and its object is conjoined. ﴿إِلى جَناحِكَ﴾ [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to (mutaʿalliq) اضمم. ﴿تَخْرُجْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the answer to the request; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿بَيْضاءَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿مِنْ غَيْرِ﴾ attached to بيضاء. ﴿سُوءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿آيَةً﴾ a ḥāl of the latent fāʿil of تخرج. ﴿أُخْرى﴾ an adjective of آية. ﴿لِنُرِيَكَ﴾ the lām is the lām of causation (taʿlīl), and the imperfect verb is accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) an after the lām of causation; its fāʿil is latent and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi; an and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of genitive by the lām. ﴿مِنْ آياتِنَا﴾ attached to an omitted ḥāl of الكبرى. ﴿الْكُبْرى﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. The meaning of جناحك is "your side", and the meaning of ﴿مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوءٍ﴾ is "without ugliness"; it is an allusion to leprosy (البرص), the well-known disease. That is, Allah gave our master Moses the miracle of the hand: when he brought it out from under his side it came out intensely white without leprosy — a sign among the nine signs that Allah gave our master Moses as miracles bearing witness to the truth of his message.

daas-irab:24-32.t: ﴿اذْهَبْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿إِلى فِرْعَوْنَ﴾ [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to (mutaʿalliq) اذهب; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying). ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ inna and its noun; the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿طَغى﴾ the clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna. ﴿قالَ رَبِّ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is resumptive. رب is the one addressed (munādā) with an omitted vocative particle; رب is a munādā annexed to the omitted yāʾ of the first person. ﴿اشْرَحْ﴾ a verb of supplication whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿لِي﴾ attached to اشرح. ﴿صَدْرِي﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause and what precedes it are the maqūl al-qawl. ﴿وَيَسِّرْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and يسر is a verb of supplication whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿لِي﴾ attached to يسر. ﴿أَمْرِي﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is conjoined to the clause اشرح لي صدري. ﴿وَاحْلُلْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; احلل is a verb of supplication whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿عُقْدَةً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مِنْ لِسانِي﴾ attached to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of عقدة; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿يَفْقَهُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the answer to the request, by the deletion of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil. ﴿قَوْلِي﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَاجْعَلْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and اجعل is a verb of supplication whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿لِي﴾ attached to a second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَزِيراً﴾ first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مِنْ أَهْلِي﴾ attached to an adjective of وزيرا. ﴿هارُونَ﴾ badal (substitute) of وزيرا. ﴿أَخِي﴾ badal of هارون. ﴿اشْدُدْ﴾ a verb of supplication whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿بِهِ﴾ attached to اشدد. ﴿أَزْرِي﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَأَشْرِكْهُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and the clause أشركه is conjoined to اشدد. ﴿فِي أَمْرِي﴾ attached to أشركه.

daas-irab:33-36.t: ﴿كَيْ﴾ a maṣdar-forming particle that makes the verb accusative. ﴿نُسَبِّحَكَ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the verb is accusative (manṣūb) by kay. ﴿كَثِيراً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), its implied form being "تسبيحا كثيرا"; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿وَنَذْكُرَكَ كَثِيراً﴾ the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿إِنَّكَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿كُنْتَ﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿بِنا﴾ [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to (mutaʿalliq) بصيرا. ﴿بَصِيراً﴾ the khabar (predicate) of kāna; the clause is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna. ﴿قالَ﴾ the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿قَدْ﴾ a particle of realisation (taḥqīq). ﴿أُوتِيتَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb; the tāʾ is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and it is the first object. [Translator's note: so in the source; أوتيت is a past verb.] ﴿سُؤْلَكَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the kāf is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿يا مُوسى﴾ yā is a vocative particle; موسى is the one addressed (munādā), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi of the implied (muqaddar) أدعو.

daas-irab:37-40.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, the lām occurs in the answer of an omitted oath, and qad is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq). ﴿مَنَنَّا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿عَلَيْكَ﴾ [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb مننا. ﴿مَرَّةً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿أُخْرى﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of مرة, accusative (manṣūb) by the implied (muqaddara) fatḥa; the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb attached to مننا. ﴿أَوْحَيْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿إِلى أُمِّكَ﴾ attached to أوحينا; the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿يُوحى﴾ a passive imperfect verb; the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "هو"; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative. ﴿أَنِ﴾ a particle of explanation (tafsīr), because revelation (الوحي) has the meaning of saying. ﴿اقْذِفِيهِ﴾ an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its object. ﴿فِي التَّابُوتِ﴾ attached to اقذفيه; the clause is explicative (tafsīriyya), with no position. ﴿فَاقْذِفِيهِ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and اقذفيه is an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its object. ﴿فِي الْيَمِّ﴾ attached to اقذفيه; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿فَلْيُلْقِهِ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction and the lām is the lām of command; يلقه is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the deletion of the weak letter; the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الْيَمِّ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿بِالسَّاحِلِ﴾ attached to يلقه; the clause is conjoined. ﴿يَأْخُذْهُ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the answer to the request; the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi. ﴿عَدُوٌّ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿لِي﴾ attached to عدو. ﴿وَعَدُوٌّ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and عدو is conjoined to what precedes it; the verbal clause has no grammatical position. ﴿لَهُ﴾ attached to عدو. ﴿وَأَلْقَيْتُ﴾ the wāw is resumptive. ﴿أَلْقَيْتُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿عَلَيْكَ﴾ attached to the verb. ﴿مَحَبَّةً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مِنِّي﴾ attached to an omitted adjective of محبة; the clause is resumptive. ﴿لِتُصْنَعَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, the lām is the lām of causation (taʿlīl), and a passive imperfect verb, accusative by an implied (muḍmara) an after the lām of causation. ﴿عَلى عَيْنِي﴾ attached to تصنع; the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is conjoined. ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb attached to ألقيت. ﴿تَمْشِي﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma implied on the yāʾ. ﴿أُخْتُكَ﴾ fāʿil; the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَتَقُولُ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿هَلْ﴾ an interrogative particle. ﴿أَدُلُّكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the kāf is mafʿūl bihi. ﴿عَلى مَنْ﴾ على is a preposition and man is a relative noun; both are attached to أدلكم. ﴿يَكْفُلُهُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative. ﴿فَرَجَعْناكَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and رجعناك is a past verb, its fāʿil and its object. ﴿إِلى أُمِّكَ﴾ attached to رجعناك; the clause is conjoined. ﴿كَيْ﴾ a particle that makes the verb accusative. ﴿تَقَرَّ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative by kay. ﴿عَيْنُها﴾ its fāʿil; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَلا تَحْزَنَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and lā is prohibitive, and an accusative imperfect verb; the clause is conjoined to كي تقر. [Translator's note: so in the source; since تحزن is accusative, conjoined to تقر, the lā here is negative (nāfiya), not prohibitive.] ﴿وَقَتَلْتَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿نَفْساً﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined. ﴿فَنَجَّيْناكَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is conjoined. ﴿مِنَ الْغَمِّ﴾ attached to نجيناك. ﴿وَفَتَنَّاكَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is conjoined. ﴿فُتُوناً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq. ﴿فَلَبِثْتَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿سِنِينَ﴾ an adverb of time, attached to لبثت. ﴿فِي أَهْلِ﴾ attached to لبثت. ﴿مَدْيَنَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, a diptote, what prevents it [from full declension] being its being a proper noun and feminine. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿جِئْتَ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿عَلى قَدَرٍ﴾ attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the tāʾ of the fāʿil. ﴿يا﴾ a vocative particle. ﴿مُوسى﴾ the one addressed (munādā), a singular proper noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi of the implied (muqaddar) أدعو.

daas-irab:41-42.t: ﴿وَاصْطَنَعْتُكَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object. ﴿لِنَفْسِي﴾ [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to (mutaʿalliq) اصطنعتك; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿اذْهَبْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿أَنْتَ﴾ tawkīd (emphasis) of the latent fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿أَخُوكَ﴾ conjoined to the latent fāʿil أنت; the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿بِآياتِي﴾ the bāʾ is for accompaniment (muṣāḥaba); [the two are] attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿لا﴾ prohibitive. ﴿تَنِيا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lā by the deletion of the nūn; the alif is the fāʿil. ﴿فِي ذِكْرِي﴾ attached to تنيا; the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:43-45.t: ﴿اذْهَبا﴾ an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the deletion of the nūn; the alif is the fāʿil (agent). ﴿إِلى فِرْعَوْنَ﴾ [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to (mutaʿalliq) اذهبا; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿طَغى﴾ a past verb indeclinable on the implied (muqaddara) fatḥa; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the clause ﴿إِنَّهُ طَغى﴾ is causal (taʿlīliyya). ﴿فَقُولا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and ﴿قَوْلًا﴾ is an imperative verb indeclinable on the deletion of the nūn; the alif is its fāʿil. [Translator's note: the source cites the word here as ﴿قَوْلًا﴾, but the analysis is of the imperative قُولا.] ﴿لَهُ﴾ attached to قولا. ﴿قَوْلًا﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿لَيِّناً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿لَعَلَّهُ﴾ لعل and its noun. ﴿يَتَذَكَّرُ﴾ a nominative imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar of لعل. ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿يَخْشى﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the implied ḍamma; its fāʿil is latent; the clause is conjoined. ﴿قالا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿رَبَّنا﴾ the one addressed (munādā), annexed (muḍāf); nā is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the vocative clause is in the position of accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying). ﴿إِنَّنا﴾ inna and its noun; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl. ﴿نَخافُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna. ﴿أَنْ﴾ a particle that makes the verb accusative. ﴿يَفْرُطَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an. ﴿عَلَيْنا﴾ attached to يفرط. ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿أَنْ﴾ making [the verb] accusative. ﴿يَطْغى﴾ an accusative imperfect verb; the clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:46-47.t: ﴿قالَ﴾ the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿لا﴾ prohibitive. ﴿تَخافا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the deletion of the nūn; the alif is the fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying). ﴿إِنَّنِي﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿مَعَكُما﴾ an adverb of place, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate); the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) and the mā is for the dual; the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya). ﴿أَسْمَعُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَأَرى﴾ the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿فَأْتِياهُ﴾ the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa fāʾ (al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa); ائتياه is an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. ﴿فَقُولا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and قولا is an imperative verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿رَسُولا﴾ the khabar of inna, nominative (marfūʿ) by the alif because it is a dual; the clause is in the position of accusative as the maqūl al-qawl. ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَأَرْسِلْ﴾ the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa fāʾ; أرسل is an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿مَعَنا﴾ an adverb of place, attached to أرسل. ﴿بَنِي﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) by the yāʾ because it is assimilated to the sound masculine plural. ﴿إِسْرائِيلَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the fatḥa in place of the kasra because it is a diptote; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and lā is prohibitive. ﴿تُعَذِّبْهُمْ﴾ a jussive imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the hāʾ is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined. ﴿قَدْ﴾ a particle of realisation (taḥqīq). ﴿جِئْناكَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object. ﴿بِآيَةٍ﴾ [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to the verb. ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾ attached to an adjective (ṣifa) of آية;
