His saying: ﴿وَيَذْهَبَا بِطَرِيقَتِكُمُ ٱلْمُثْلَىٰ﴾: al-ṭarīqa is the noble men. His saying (المثلى) means al-amthal: they will take away your nobles. He said al-muthlā and did not say al-muthul, like (al-asmāʾ al-ḥusnā). If you wish, you make (المُثْلَىٰ) feminine because al-ṭarīqa is feminine. The Arabs say of a people: "These are the ṭarīqa of their people" and "the ṭarāʾiq of their people", meaning their nobles; and His saying ﴿كُنَّا طَرَائِقَ قِدَداً﴾ is from that. They also say of a single person: "This is the ṭarīqa of his people" and "the naẓūra of his people" — and some of them "the naẓīra of his people" — and they say of a group, with the singular and the plural: "These are the naẓūra of their people" and "the naẓāʾir of their people".

farraa:64-64.t:
His saying: ﴿فَأَجْمِعُواْ كَيْدَكُمْ﴾: al-ijmāʿ is making firm and resolving upon [113 a] a thing. You say ajmaʿtu al-khurūja and ʿalā al-khurūji ("I resolved to go out"), like azmaʿtu. The poet said:
يا ليت شعرى والمنى لا تنفع * هل أَغدُوَنْ يوماً وأمرى مُجْمَع
(Would that I knew — and wishes do not avail — whether I shall set out one day with my affair resolved.)
He means: it has been made firm and resolved upon. Whoever reads (فأجْمَعُوا) is saying: do not leave out anything of your plotting, but bring it all.
His saying ﴿مَنِ ٱسْتَعْلَىٰ﴾: whoever prevails.

farraa:65-65.t:
His saying: ﴿إِمَّآ أَن تُلْقِيَ وَإِمَّآ أَن نَّكُونَ أَوَّلَ مَنْ أَلْقَىٰ﴾: (أَن) is in the position of the accusative, the meaning being "choose one of these two". Had it been put in the nominative, since the verb is not overt, it would have been correct, as though it were a statement, as in the poet's saying:
فسِيرا فإمَّا حاجةٌ تقضِيانها * وإمَّا مقِيلٌ صَالح وصَديق
(So travel on, you two: either there is a need you will fulfil, or a good resting-place and a friend.)
Had His saying ﴿فإمَّا مَنٌّ بَعْدُ وإمَّا فَدِاءٌ﴾ been put in the nominative, that too would have been correct, its approach being like that of His saying ﴿فَإمْساكٌ بِمَعرُوفٍ أَو تَسْريحٌ بإحْسَانٍ﴾. The accusative in His saying ﴿ إمَّا أَنْ تُلْقِىَ﴾ and in His saying ﴿فإمَّا مَنّاً بَعْدُ وإمَّا فَدِاءً﴾ is better than the nominative, because it is something that is not general — unlike what you see of the meaning of His saying ﴿فإمْسَاكٌ﴾ and ﴿فَصِيَامُ ثلاَثَةِ أيَّامٍ﴾: since the meaning there covers all people, in retaining honourably and in fasting three days in the expiation of an oath, it was like a conditional response (jazāʾ) and was put in the nominative for that reason; whereas the choosing is only a single act. The meaning of (أفلح) [Translator's note: in 20:64] is: he lived and was saved.

farraa:66-66.t: His saying: ﴿يُخَيَّلُ إِلَيْهِ مِن سِحْرِهِمْ أَنَّهَا تَسْعَىٰ﴾: (أنَّها) is in the position of the nominative. Whoever reads (تُخَيِّلُ) or (تَخَيَّلُ), it is in the position of the accusative, because the meaning is "it takes on an appearance, to them, by moving", and "it gives an impression" likewise; when you drop the bāʾ you put it in the accusative, just as you say "aradtu bi-an aqūma", whose meaning is "I wanted to stand"; when you drop the bāʾ you put it in the accusative. Allah said ﴿وَمَنْ يُرِدْ فِيهِ بإِلحَادٍ بِظُلْمٍ﴾; had you dropped the bāʾ you would have put it in the accusative and said: "wa-man yurid fīhi ilḥādan bi-ẓulmin".

farraa:69-69.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّمَا صَنَعُواْ كَيْدُ سَاحِرٍ﴾: you make (ما) take the role of alladhī: "Indeed, what they have made is the plot of sorcery"; some of them have read it ﴿كَيدُ سَاحِرٍ﴾, and all is correct. Had you put ﴿ كَيْدَ سحر﴾ in the accusative, it would have been correct, making (إنما) a single particle, like His saying ﴿إنَّما تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللّهِ أَوْثَانَا﴾.
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ يُفْلِحُ ٱلسَّاحِرُ حَيْثُ أَتَىٰ﴾: it has come in the exegesis that he is to be killed wherever he is found.

farraa:71-71.t:
His saying: ﴿فَلأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ مِّنْ خِلاَفٍ﴾: in such speech ʿan, ʿalā and bāʾ are also suitable.
His saying ﴿وَلأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ فِي جُذُوعِ ٱلنَّخْلِ﴾: (على) is suitable in place of (فى). (فى) is suitable because he is raised up in the wood along its length, so (فى) is suitable; and (عَلى) is suitable because he is raised up in it and so comes to be on it. Allah has said ﴿وَاتَّبَعُوا مَا تَتْلُو الشَّيَاطِينُ عَلَى مُلْكِ سُلَيْمان﴾, and its meaning is "in the reign of Solomon". His saying ﴿أَشَدُّ عَذَاباً وَأَبْقَىٰ﴾: He is saying: and more lasting.

farraa:72-72.t:
His saying: ﴿قَالُواْ لَن نُّؤْثِرَكَ عَلَىٰ مَا جَآءَنَا مِنَ ٱلْبَيِّنَاتِ وَٱلَّذِي فَطَرَنَا﴾: alladhī is in the position of the genitive: "and over the One who". Had they meant by their saying (والذى فطرنا) an oath by it, it would have been genitive and would have been correct, as though they said: "We will not prefer you, by Allah."
His saying ﴿فَٱقْضِ مَآ أَنتَ قَاضٍ﴾: do whatever you will. His saying ﴿إِنَّمَا تَقْضِي هَـٰذِهِ ٱلْحَيَاةَ ٱلدُّنْيَآ﴾: innamā is a single particle; for that reason you put (al-ḥayāh) in the accusative. Had a reader read (al-ḥayāh) in the nominative, it would have been permissible, making (مَا) take the role of alladhī, as though he said: "What you decree is this worldly [Translator's note: life]."

farraa:73-73.t: His saying: ﴿وَمَآ أَكْرَهْتَنَا عَلَيْهِ مِنَ ٱلسِّحْرِ﴾: mā is in the position of the accusative, referred back to the sense of al-khaṭāyā ("the sins"). It is mentioned in the exegesis that Pharaoh had forced the sorcerers [113 b] to learn sorcery.

farraa:77-77.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَّ تَخَافُ دَرَكاً وَلاَ تَخْشَىٰ﴾ is nominative as a new beginning (istiʾnāf) with lā, as He said ﴿وَأْمُرْ أَهْلَكَ بِالصَّلاَةِ وَاصْطَبِرْ عَلَيْهَا لاَ نَسْأَلُكَ رِزْقََا﴾; most of what has come in response to a command with lā is in the nominative. Ḥamza read (لا تَخَفْ دَرَكاً), putting it in the jussive as a conditional response (jazāʾ), and put (وَلاَ تَخْشَىٰ) in the nominative as a new beginning, as He said ﴿يُوَلُّوكُمُ الأَدْبَارَ ثُمَّ لاَ يُنْصَرُونَ﴾, beginning anew with thumma; this is like it. Had Ḥamza intended the jussive in His saying ﴿وَلاَ تَخْشَىٰ﴾, even though it has the yāʾ [Translator's note: i.e. the final long vowel], it would have been correct, as the poet said:
* هُزِّى إليك الجِذُع يجنيك الجَنَى *
(Shake the trunk towards you, and it will yield you fresh fruit.)
and he did not say yajnik al-janā. Another said:
هجوتَ زَبَّان ثمَّ جئتَ معتذِراً * من سَبّ زَبَّان لم تهجو ولم تَدِعِ
(You satirized Zabbān, then came apologizing for reviling Zabbān — as if you had not satirized and had not let it be.)
And another said:
أَلَمْ يَأتِيكَ والأَنباءُ تَنْمِى * بِمَا لاَقت لَبُونُ بنى زِيادِ
(Has it not reached you — and news spreads — what the milch-camels of the Banū Ziyād met with?)
He kept the yāʾ in (يأتيك) while it is in the position of the jussive, because of its being quiescent, and so that was permissible.

farraa:81-81.t: His saying: ﴿فَيَحِلَّ عَلَيْكُمْ غَضَبِي﴾: the kasra in it is dearer to me than the ḍamma, because al-ḥulūl (with yaḥullu) is what actually befalls, while yaḥillu means "becomes due"; and the exegesis has come with "becoming due", not with "befalling". All is correct, if Allah wills. Al-Kisāʾī took it in the sense of befalling. In the reading of al-Farrāʾ it is with ḍamma, like al-Kisāʾī; he was asked about it and said so [Translator's note: this sentence appears to be a transmitter's remark and reads awkwardly in the source]. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh or Ubayy, ﴿إن شاء الله﴾ ﴿وَلاَ يحُلَّنَّ عَلَيْكُمُ غَضَبِى وَمَنْ يَحْلُلْ عَلَيْه﴾, with ḍamma. As for His saying ﴿أَمْ أَرَدْتُمْ أَنْ يَحِلَّ عَلَيْكُمُ﴾, it is with kasra, and it is like the two preceding ones; had it been given ḍamma it would have been correct. When you say "ḥalla bihim al-ʿadhāb" ("the punishment descended upon them"), it is yaḥullu with ḍamma and nothing else; and when you say ʿalā, or you say "yaḥillu laka such-and-such" ("such-and-such is lawful for you"), it is with kasra.

farraa:82-82.t: His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ ٱهْتَدَىٰ﴾: he knew that there is reward and punishment for that.

farraa:84-84.t: His saying: ﴿قَالَ هُمْ أُوْلاۤءِ عَلَىٰ أَثَرِي﴾: some of the readers have read (أُولاىَ عَلَى أَثَرِى), dropping the hamza; and when the hamza is dropped it is made to resemble the possessive form, just as Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read ﴿مِلّة آباىَ إبراهيمَ﴾ and ﴿وَتَقَبَّل دُعَاىَ رَبَّنَا﴾.

farraa:87-87.t:
His saying: ﴿مَآ أَخْلَفْنَا مَوْعِدَكَ بِمَلْكِنَا﴾ with ḍamma on the mīm [Translator's note: the printed Qurʾānic text in this entry is vowelled «بِمَلْكِنَا» with fatḥa]. (This is the reading of the readers.) Had it been read bi-milkinā (and bi-malkinā), it would have been correct. The meaning of (mulkinā) in the exegesis is: we were not in control of what was right; we simply erred.
His saying ﴿وَلَـٰكِنَّا حُمِّلْنَآ أَوْزَاراً مِّن زِينَةِ ٱلْقَوْمِ﴾ means the gold, silver and iron they had taken from Pharaoh's people when the sea cast them out; "so we threw it into the fire, and al-Sāmirī did likewise, and we followed him." When the silver and the gold of what they had thrown became pure, al-Sāmirī fashioned it into a calf. He had taken a handful from the track of a horse that was under Gabriel. (Al-Sāmirī said to Moses: "It was cast into my mind that if I threw that handful on something dead it would come to life"; so he threw that handful into the nose of the bull and into its rear, and it came to life and lowed.) Al-Farrāʾ said: In the exegesis of al-Kalbī, the horse was [Translator's note: the horse of] life [Translator's note: the text reads «أن الفرس كانت الحياة»]. That is His saying ﴿وكَذَلكَ سَوَّلَتْ لِى نَفْسِى﴾: he is saying, my soul made it seem attractive to me.
Whoever reads bi-milkinā with kasra on the mīm, it is al-milk, what a man owns; you say of anything you own: "This is milk yamīnī (the property of my right hand)", of a slave and of other things that are owned. Al-malk is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of malaktuhu malkan and malakatan, like ghalabtuhu ghalban and ghalabatan. Al-mulk is sovereignty. Some of the Banū Asad say "mā lī mulk", meaning: I have nothing I own. Milk al-ṭarīq and malkuhu is its middle (wajh). The poet said:
أقامت على مَلْك الطريق فَمَلكه * لها ولمَنكوب المطايا جَوانبهُ
(She kept to the middle of the road: its middle is hers, and its sides belong to the footsore mounts.)
[114 a] Along with malk al-ṭarīq it is also said: fa-milkuhu. [Translator's note: One says:] she kept to the bulk (ʿuẓm) of the road, to the smooth part (sujuḥ) of the road, and to its course (sanan and sunan).

farraa:88-88.t: His saying: ﴿فَنَسِيَ﴾ means that Moses forgot: he missed the way and was slow in returning to them, so they took up the calf; and Allah reproached them, saying: Do they not see that the calf does not speak and has no power to harm or benefit them?

farraa:96-96.t: His saying: ﴿فَقَبَضْتُ قَبْضَةً﴾: al-qabḍa is with the whole hand, and al-qabṣa is with the fingertips. Al-Ḥasan read qabṣa with ṣād. Al-qubṣa and al-qubḍa (with ḍamma) are both the name of the earth itself [Translator's note: that is taken]; had they been read, it would have been a valid option. Similar to it, among what has been read, is ﴿إلاَّ مَنِ اغترف غُرْفة بيده﴾ and (غَرْفَةً): al-ghurfa is what is scooped up, and al-gharfa is the single act. Likewise al-ḥuswa and al-ḥaswa, al-khuṭwa and al-khaṭwa, al-ukla and al-akla: al-ukla is what is eaten and al-akla is the single time; al-khuṭwa is the distance between the feet in walking and al-khaṭwa is the single time. What has kasra is a maṣdar (of manner), as in "he has a fine way of walking (al-mishya), sitting (al-jilsa) and sitting down (al-qiʿda)".

farraa:97-97.t:
His saying: ﴿فَإِنَّ لَكَ فِي ٱلْحَيَاةِ أَن تَقُولَ لاَ مِسَاسَ﴾: that is, "I am not to be touched and I do not touch." The interpretation of that is that Moses commanded them not to eat with him, not to mix with him and not to trade with him. It is also read (لا مَسَاسِ), which is a widespread dialectal form: "lā masāsi, lā masāsi", like nazāli and naẓāri, from al-intiẓār ("waiting"). His saying ﴿الذِى ظَلْت عليه عاكفاً﴾ and ﴿ظِلْت﴾, and ﴿فَظَلتُم تفكَّهُوَن﴾ and ﴿فَظِلتم﴾: fatḥa and kasra are both permissible only because their meaning is ẓaliltum, and the first lām has been dropped. Whoever gives kasra to the ẓāʾ puts the kasra of the dropped lām on the ẓāʾ; and whoever gives fatḥa to the ẓāʾ says: it had fatḥa, so I left it with its fatḥa. Similar to it are masastu and masistu: the Arabs say "qad mastu that" and "mistuhu"; "hamamtu bi-dhālika" and "hamtu"; and "wadidtu" and "wadadtu" [Translator's note: the words «كذا فى ب» ("thus in manuscript B") stand in the text here] "that you had done that"; and "hal aḥsasta ṣāḥibaka?" and "hal aḥasta?" ("did you perceive your companion?").
His saying ﴿لَّنُحَرِّقَنَّهُ﴾ — with fire — and ﴿لَنَحرُقَنَّه﴾: we will file it down with iron, from ḥaraqtu, aḥruquhu and aḥriquhu, two dialectal forms. Al-Mufaḍḍal recited to me:
بذى فَرِقَيْنِ يوم بَنُو حَبيبٍ * نيُوبَهَمُ علينا يَحْرُقونَا
(At Dhū Fariqayn, on the day when the Banū Ḥabīb were grinding their teeth at us.)
Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us: Muḥammad narrated to us: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us: Ḥibbān ibn ʿAlī narrated to me from al-Kalbī from Abū Ṣāliḥ that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: (لنَحرُقَنَّه) means "we will surely file it down".

farraa:102-102.t: His saying: ﴿يَوْمِئِذٍ زُرْقاً﴾: it is said: We will gather them thirsty; and it is said: We will gather them blind.

farraa:103-103.t: His saying: ﴿يَتَخَافَتُونَ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾: al-takhāfut is speech kept low.

farraa:104-104.t: His saying: ﴿أَمْثَلُهُمْ طَرِيقَةً﴾: the best of them in speech, in himself and in their view: ﴿إِن لَّبِثْتُمْ إِلاَّ يَوْماً﴾ — and he lied.

farraa:105-105.t: His saying: ﴿يَنسِفُهَا رَبِّي نَسْفاً﴾: He uproots them.

farraa:106-106.t: His saying: ﴿قَاعاً صَفْصَفاً﴾: al-qāʿ is a place where water collects, and al-ṣafṣaf is the smooth ground on which there is no vegetation.

farraa:107-107.t: His saying: ﴿وَلاۤ أَمْتاً﴾: al-amt is a hillock of ground: what rises from it; and it is said: the water-courses of the valleys (without hamza), what lies low. I have heard the Arabs say: "He filled the water-skin with a filling in which there is no amt", when there is no slackness in it. And it is said: "We travelled a journey in which there was no amt", no flagging and no weakness.

farraa:108-108.t:
His saying: ﴿يَتَّبِعُونَ ٱلدَّاعِيَ﴾: they follow the voice of the caller to the Gathering. ﴿لاعِوَجَ لَهُ﴾: He is saying: they have no deviation from the caller. It was permissible for Him to say (له) because the sense refers to the caller and his voice. It is as you say in speech: "You called me with a call from which I have no deviation for you", i.e. I do not turn aside for you or from you.
His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ هَمْساً﴾: it is said: the shuffling of feet towards the place of Gathering; and it is said: it is the faint sound. It is reported of [114 b] Ibn ʿAbbās that he quoted:
وهُنَّ يمشين بنا هميساً * إن تصدق الطير نِنك لميسا
(And they walk with us with a soft tread; if the birds' omen proves true, we shall be with Lamīs.)
This is the sound of the camels' hoofs in their travel.

farraa:109-109.t:
His saying: ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ لاَّ تَنفَعُ ٱلشَّفَاعَةُ إِلاَّ مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ﴾: (من) is in the position of the accusative: intercession will not benefit anyone except one on whose behalf permission to intercede has been given.
His saying: ﴿وَرَضِيَ لَهُ قَوْلاً﴾ is like your saying "and He accepted his deed from him". A man may say: "I have accepted your deed for you" and "I have accepted it from you."

farraa:110-110.t: His saying: ﴿يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ﴾ means His angels, whom those who worshipped them worshipped. So He said: they do not know what is before them and what is behind them; He is the One who knows it. That is His saying: ﴿وَلاَ يُحِيطُونَ بِهِ عِلْماً﴾.

farraa:111-111.t:
His saying: ﴿وَعَنَتِ ٱلْوُجُوهُ لِلْحَيِّ ٱلْقَيُّومِ﴾: it is said: they toiled for Him, they worked for Him. It is also related that it is the Muslim's placing his hands, his forehead and his knees [Translator's note: on the ground] when he prostrates and bows. In the sense of the Arabic language it is a man's saying ʿanawtu laka: I have submitted to you and obeyed you. It is said: "The earth did not ʿanu with anything", i.e. it did not grow anything; and it is said "lam taʿni bi-shayʾ", the meaning being the same, just as it is said ḥathawtu ʿalayhi al-turāb and ḥathaytu al-turāb ("I strewed earth on him"). Al-ʿanwa, in the Arabs' saying "I took this thing ʿanwatan", may be by force, and may be by surrender and obedience on the part of the one from whom the thing is taken. The poet said:
فما أخذوهَا عن مودَّةٍ * ولكن بضرب المشرفىّ استقَالَهَا
(They did not take it out of affection, but by the blow of the Mashrafī sword he sought its release.)
This is in the sense of obedience and surrender without fighting [Translator's note: this is how the source applies the verse; the verse itself speaks of the sword].

farraa:112-112.t: His saying: ﴿فَلاَ يَخَافُ ظُلْماً وَلاَ هَضْماً﴾: the Arabs say: "I made a haḍm for you from my right", i.e. I reduced it. It has come from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, on the Day of the Camel, that it was said to him: "Is it haḍm or retaliation?" He said: "Whatever was done is under these two feet of mine", thereby making it unavenged. It is reduction.

farraa:113-113.t:
His saying: ﴿أَوْ يُحْدِثُ لَهُمْ ذِكْراً﴾:
honour; it is like Allah's saying ﴿وَإنَّه لَذِكْرٌ لكَ ولِقَوْمِكَ﴾, i.e. an honour. And it is said: ﴿أَوْ يُحْدِثُ لَهُمْ ذِكْراً﴾ means a punishment, i.e. they will remember the descent of the punishment they were promised.

farraa:114-114.t: His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَعْجَلْ بِٱلْقُرْآنِ مِن قَبْلِ إَن يُقْضَىٰ إِلَيْكَ وَحْيُهُ﴾: when Gabriel came to him ﷺ with the revelation, he would hasten to recite it before Gabriel had completed his recitation; so he was commanded not to hasten until Gabriel had completed his recitation. His saying ﴿فنسى﴾: he abandoned what he had been commanded.

farraa:115-115.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَمْ نَجِدْ لَهُ عَزْماً﴾: no firm resolve and no resoluteness in what he did.

farraa:117-117.t: His saying: ﴿فَلاَ يُخْرِجَنَّكُمَا مِنَ ٱلْجَنَّةِ فَتَشْقَىٰ﴾: He did not say "fa-tashqayā" (dual), because Adam is the one addressed, and his act suffices for the act of the woman. Similar to it is His saying in Qāf: ﴿عَنِ اليَميِنِ وَعَنِ الشِّمَالِ قَعِيد﴾: He made do with qaʿīd for its companion, because the meaning is known. The meaning of (فَتَشْقَىٰ) is: you will eat from the toil of your hand and your labour.

farraa:118-118.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّ لَكَ أَلاَّ تَجُوعَ فِيهَا﴾: an there is in the position of the accusative, because when inna, layta and laʿalla are followed by an adverbial phrase (ṣifa) you put what comes after it in the accusative; and anna is of that kind.

farraa:119-119.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَنَّكَ لاَ تَظْمَأُ فِيهَا﴾ is also accusative. Whoever reads ﴿وَإِنَّكَ لاَ تَظْمَأُ﴾ refers it back to His saying (إنَّ), which comes before (لك). It is also permissible to begin it anew and give it kasra without conjoining it to anything. Had you made ﴿وَأَنَّكَ لاَ تَظْمَأُ﴾ with fatḥa a new beginning, intending the nominative for it, in the sense of "and yours is that you will not thirst in it nor be exposed to the sun", it would have been correct.
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَضْحَىٰ﴾: no harmful sun will strike you. It is mentioned in some exegesis that (وَلاَ تَضْحَىٰ) means "you will not sweat", but the first is closer to being right. The poet said:
رأت رجلا أمَّا إذا الشمس أعرضت * فيَضْحَى وأمَّا بالعَشِىْ فيَخصر
(She saw a man who, when the sun shows itself broadly, is scorched by it, and in the evening is pinched with cold.)
So he has made it clear. One also says: ḍaḥītu.

farraa:121-121.t: His saying: ﴿وَطَفِقَا يَخْصِفَانِ﴾: in Arabic it is: "they set about patching" and "they began patching". Likewise His saying ﴿فطَفِق مَسْحاً بالسوق والأعناقِ﴾. (And it is said here:) they began sticking fig leaves on themselves, while it kept falling off them.

farraa:122-122.t: His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ ٱجْتَبَاهُ رَبُّهُ﴾: He chose him. ﴿فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ وَهَدَىٰ﴾: i.e. He guided him to repentance.

farraa:124-124.t:
His saying: ﴿مَعِيشَةً ضَنكاً﴾: al-ḍank is severe narrowness.
His saying: ﴿وَنَحْشُرُهُ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيامَةِ أَعْمَىٰ﴾: blind to the proof; and it is said: he comes out of his grave seeing, then becomes blind at his Gathering.

farraa:128-128.t:
His saying: ﴿أَفَلَمْ يَهْدِ لَهُمْ﴾: does it not make clear to them, if they look, ﴿كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا﴾? (كم) is in the position of the accusative; it cannot be otherwise. Similar to it in speech: "Has it not been made clear to you: whoever does good is rewarded for it?" — the clause of the speech has in it the sense of a nominative. Similar to it is your saying: "It has become clear to me: did ʿAbd Allāh stand or Zayd?" — in the interrogative there is the sense of a nominative. Likewise His saying: ﴿سَوَاءٌ عَلَيْكُمْ أَدَعَوْتُمْوهُمْ أَمْ أَنتُم صَامِتُون﴾: there is in it something in the nominative because of ﴿سَوَاءٌ عليكم﴾ which does not show with the interrogative; and had you said "Your silence and your calling are the same to you", the nominative within the clause would have become clear.
His saying: ﴿يَمْشُونَ فِي مَسَاكِنِهِمْ﴾ means the people of Mecca. They used to trade and travel in the dwellings of ʿĀd and Thamūd and pass through them. So the walking belongs to the unbelievers of the people of Mecca, (and the dwellings) to those destroyed. So He said: Do they not fear that there will befall them what befell those whose dwellings and the traces of whose punishment they saw?

farraa:129-129.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَوْلاَ كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ مِن رَّبِّكَ لَكَانَ لِزَاماً وَأَجَلٌ مُّسَمًّى﴾: He means: "Were it not for a word and an appointed term, it would have been inevitable" (brought forward and put back). It is — according to what they have mentioned — the killing that came down upon them at the battle of Badr.

farraa:130-131.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَطْرَافَ ٱلنَّهَارِ﴾: the day has only two ends (ṭarafān), and the exegetes said: (and the ends of the day) are the dawn, noon and afternoon prayers. (That is) one way: that you make noon and afternoon part of the latter end of the day, then add the dawn to them, so they become "ends". It may also refer to two prayers, and that is permissible: they would be two ends treated as a plural, as He said ﴿إنْ تَتُوبا إلَى اللّهِ فَقَدْ صَغَتْ قُلُوبُكُمَا﴾. That is the dearer of the two ways to me, because He said ﴿وَأَقِمْ الصَّلاَةَ طَرفَى النَّهَارِ وَزُلَفاً مِنَ اللَّيلِ﴾. You put aṭrāf in the accusative by referring it back to "before the rising of the sun and before its setting". If you wish, you put aṭrāf in the genitive, meaning "and glorify Him in part of the night and in the ends of the day"; but I have not heard it in recitation. It is, however, like His saying ﴿وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْهُ وَأَدبَارَ السُّجُودِ﴾, ﴿وإدبارَ السجودِ﴾ — Ḥamza read wa-idbāra al-sujūd. In the alif, fatḥa and kasra are both permissible, but kasra of the alif is good only in recitation.
His saying ﴿لَعَلَّكَ تَرْضَىٰ﴾ and ﴿تُرْضَى﴾: their meaning is the same, because when you are pleased, you have been made pleased. Ḥamza and the companions [Translator's note: the text has «وأصحال», evidently for «وأصحاب»] of ʿAbd Allāh used to read it turḍā. Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us: Muḥammad narrated to us: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us: Abū Bakr and his brother al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAyyāsh narrated to me from ʿĀṣim from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān that he read laʿallaka (turḍā, with ḍamma on the tāʾ).
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَمُدَّنَّ عَيْنَيْكَ إِلَىٰ مَا مَتَّعْنَا بِهِ أَزْوَاجاً مِّنْهُمْ﴾: He means: men among them.
His saying ﴿زَهْرَةَ ٱلْحَيَاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾: you put al-zahra in the accusative by the verb: "We gave them enjoyment of it as a splendour in [115 b] the life [Translator's note: of this world] and an adornment in it." (Zahratan), even though it is definite — the Arabs say: "I passed by him, the noble, the generous" (in the accusative). One of the Banū Faqʿas recited to me:
أبعد الذى بالسَّفح سفحِ كُواكبٍ * رهينةَ رَمْسٍ من تراب وجندل
(Is it after the one at the foot of the hill, the foot of Kuwākib, held in pledge by a grave of earth and stones…?)
He put al-rahīna in the accusative by the verb, though what governs the noun which is al-rahīna is a word of the genitive [Translator's note: the text has «وفع», evidently for «وقع»]; so this is weaker than (متَّعنا) and the like.

farraa:132-132.t: His saying: ﴿لاَ نَسْأَلُكَ رِزْقاً﴾: a wage for that. Likewise His saying ﴿وَرِزقُ رَبِّك﴾: He means: and the reward of your Lord.

farraa:134-134.t: His saying: ﴿أَنَّآ أَهْلَكْنَاهُمْ بِعَذَابٍ مِّن قَبْلِهِ﴾: before the Messenger, (they would have said): "How could we be destroyed before a messenger was sent to us?" So the hāʾ refers to Muḥammad ﷺ. And it is said that the hāʾ refers to the Revelation. Both are correct.

farraa:135-135.t:
His saying: ﴿فَسَتَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ أَصْحَابُ ٱلصِّرَاطِ ٱلسَّوِيِّ وَمَنِ ٱهْتَدَىٰ﴾: both man are in the position of the nominative. Everything like it in the Qurʾān is nominative when there is something after it that makes it nominative, as in His saying ﴿فَسَتَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ هُوَ فِى ضلالٍ مُبِينٍ﴾, and similarly ﴿لنَعْلمَ أىُّ الحِزْبَيْنِ أحْصَى﴾, and similarly ﴿أعْلَمُ مَنْ جَاءَ بِالهُدَى وَمَنْ هُوَ فِى ضَلاَلٍ مُبِين﴾. Had it been put in the accusative, it would have been correct; it would be on a par with Allah's saying ﴿اللّهُ يَعْلَمُ المُفْسِدَ مِنَ المُصْلِحِ﴾.
His saying: ﴿فَسَتَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ أَصْحَابُ ٱلصِّرَاطِ ٱلسَّوِيِّ﴾: those who did not go astray; ﴿وَمَنِ ٱهْتَدَىٰ﴾: of those who were astray and then were guided.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: The clause «تشقى» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī), and the genitive interpreted maṣdar is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أنزلنا».

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr); «تذكرة» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). The first one had to come with the lām because the agents differ: the agent of the sending down is Allah, glory be to Him, and the agent of {لِتَشْقَى} is the Messenger ﷺ; as for «تذكرةً», it fulfils the conditions for being accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi.

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: «تنزيلا»: a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted governing word, i.e.: نزلناه تنزيلا (We sent it down a sending down). The preposition and its genitive noun «ممَّن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «تنزيلا»; it is composed of the preposition «مِنْ» and the relative «مَنْ».

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The clause «استوى» is the khabar (predicate) of «الرحمن». The preposition and its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb.

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «في السماوات» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied (muqaddar) ṣila (relative clause), and the clause «له ما في السماوات» is a second khabar (predicate) of «الرحمن» in the previous verse.

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: His saying «وأَخفَى»: a noun conjoined to «السِّر», and it is an elative (afʿal tafḍīl).

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: «الله»: mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause of divine transcendence (jumlat al-tanzīh) is the khabar (predicate). «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr); «هو» is a badal (substitute) of the latent (mustatir) pronoun in the omitted khabar; the clause «له الأسماء» is a second khabar.

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: «إذْ»: an adverbial noun, badal (substitute) of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) of {حَدِيثُ}. The clause «لَعَلِّي آتيكم» is resumptive within the scope of the speech; the clause «أوْ أَجِدُ» is conjoined to the single word «آتيكم».

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: The conditional clause is resumptive, and the clause «نُودِيَ» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a pronoun referring to the maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb.

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: «أنَا» is tawkīd (emphasis) of the yāʾ in «إِنِّي», and «ربُّك» is the khabar (predicate) of «إنَّ». The clause «فاخلع» is resumptive. «طوى»: a badal (substitute) of «الوادي».

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: The clause «وأنا اختَرْتُك» is conjoined to the clause {إِنَّكَ بِالْوَادِ}. The clause «فاستمِع» is conjoined to the clause «اخترتك».

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: «أنَا» is tawkīd (emphasis) of the yāʾ; the name of Majesty is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the clause of divine transcendence (jumlat al-tanzīh) is a second khabar of «إنَّ». As for «إلا أَنَّا»: «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr), and «أنا» is a badal (substitute) of the latent (mustatir) pronoun in the omitted khabar. The clause «فاعبدني» is conjoined to the clause «إنني أنا الله».

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The clause «أكاد» is a second khabar (predicate) of «إنَّ», and the genitive interpreted maṣdar «لِتُجْزَى» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أُخفيها». The bāʾ in «بما» is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun) [Translator's note: so in the source; it is «ما» that is maṣdariyya, the bāʾ being the preposition], and the interpreted maṣdar is genitive, attached to «تجزى».

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: His saying «فلا يَصُدَّنك»: the fāʾ is resumptive, «لا» is prohibitive, and an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa in the position of the jussive; the nūn is for emphasis (tawkīd), and the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). «مَن» is a relative noun, fāʿil (agent). His saying «فَتَرْدَى»: the fāʾ is causative (sababiyya), and an imperfect verb in the accusative by a concealed «أنْ»; the interpreted maṣdar is conjoined to a maṣdar extracted (mutaṣayyad) from the preceding speech, i.e.: let there be no turning away, and then a perishing.

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: His saying «وما تلك»: the wāw is resumptive; «ما» is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); «تلك» is an interrogative noun, khabar (predicate) [Translator's note: so in the source; «تلك» is a demonstrative]; the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the demonstrative, and the clause «يا موسى» is resumptive within the context of the question.

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: The clause «أتَوَكَّأُ» is a second khabar (predicate); the clause «ولي فيها مآربُ» is conjoined to the clause «أهشُّ», and the preposition and its genitive noun «فيها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the "being established" (istiqrār) to which the khabar is attached.

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The clause «يا موسى» is resumptive within the scope of the speech.

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: The clause «فألقاها» is resumptive, and the clause «فإذا هي حيَّة» is conjoined to the clause «ألقاها»; «إذا» is the «إذا» of surprise (fujāʾiyya), and the clause «تسعَى» is a naʿt (adjective) of «حية».

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: The clause «سَنُعِيدُها» is resumptive within the scope of the speech, and His saying «سِيرَتَها» is a badal (substitute) of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) of the hāʾ.

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: The verb «تخرج» is jussive (majzūm) because it occurs as the apodosis of an implied (muqaddar) condition. «بيضاء»: a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «تخرج». The preposition and its genitive noun «من غير» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a second ḥāl of the agent of «تخرج». «آية»: the second object of an omitted verb, its implied form being: جعلناها آية (We made it a sign), and the implied clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: The interpreted maṣdar «لِنُرِيَك» is genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «جعلناها» implied in the previous verse; the preposition and its genitive noun «مِن آياتنا» is attached to an adjective of the second object implied in «لنريك», i.e.: لنريك شيئًا من آياتنا (that We may show you something of Our signs).

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: The clause «إنَّهُ طَغَى» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «فرعون».

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «لي» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «اشرح».

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «من لساني» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «عقدة».

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: «يَفْقَهُوا» is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it occurs as the apodosis of an implied (muqaddar) condition.

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «لي» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object of «اجْعَل»; the preposition and its genitive noun «منْ أَهْلي» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «وَزِيرًا».

harrat-mujtaba:30-30.t: «هَارُونَ» is a badal (substitute) of {وَزِيرًا}, and «أخي» is a badal of «هارون».

harrat-mujtaba:33-33.t: «كثيرًا»: a deputy of the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e.: تسبيحًا كثيرًا (much glorifying). His saying «كَيْ نُسَبِّحَك»: kay is a maṣdar-forming particle that puts the verb in the accusative, and the interpreted maṣdar is accusative by removal of the preposition, the lām.

harrat-mujtaba:35-35.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «بنا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:36-36.t: «سُؤْلَكَ»: the second object; the tāʾ, the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) in «أوتيت», is the first. The clause «يا مُوسَى» is parenthetical between the two conjoined items.

harrat-mujtaba:37-37.t: The wāw in «ولقد» is a conjunction; the oath clause with its response is conjoined to the preceding clause {أُوتِيتَ}, and the clause «لقد مننَّا عليك» is the answer to the oath; «مرة» is a deputy of the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

harrat-mujtaba:38-38.t: «إذْ» is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (mutaʿalliq) {مَنَنَّا}; «ما» is a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

harrat-mujtaba:39-39.t: «أن»: explicative (tafsīriyya) of the revelation in the previous verse, and the clause after it is explicative. The clause «يأخذه» is the apodosis of an implied (muqaddar) condition; the preposition and its genitive noun «لي» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «عَدُوٌّ». The clause «ألقيت» is resumptive; the preposition and its genitive noun «مني» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «مَحَبَّةً». His saying «لِتُصْنَعَ»: the wāw is a conjunction and the lām is causal (taʿlīl); the genitive interpreted maṣdar is attached to an implied verb, its implied form being: ولتصنع فعلتُ ذلك (and that you might be brought up, I did that); the implied clause «فعلتُ» is conjoined to the clause «ألقيتُ».

harrat-mujtaba:40-40.t: «إذْ»: an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (mutaʿalliq) {وَأَلْقَيْتُ}. The clause «فَرَجَعْنَاكَ» is resumptive, and the maṣdar «كَيْ تَقَرَّ» is accusative by removal of the preposition, the lām. The clause «فلبثتَ» is resumptive. «سنين» is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), accusative with yāʾ because it is treated like the sound masculine plural, attached to the verb, and likewise the preposition and its genitive noun «في أهل». «مدين» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive with fatḥa because it is a diptote, being a proper name and feminine. The preposition and its genitive noun «على قدر» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «جئت», and the clause «يا موسى» is parenthetical between the two conjoined items.

harrat-mujtaba:41-41.t: The clause «واصطنعتُك» is conjoined to the clause (وَجِئْتَ).

harrat-mujtaba:42-42.t: «أنت» is tawkīd (emphasis) of the latent (mustatir) agent. His saying «وأخوك»: a noun conjoined to the latent agent in «اذْهَبْ». The preposition and its genitive noun «بآياتي» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of «أخُوك» and what is conjoined to it.

harrat-mujtaba:43-43.t: The clause «إنه طغَى» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «فرعون».

harrat-mujtaba:45-45.t: «ربَّنا»: the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, accusative, and the pronoun «نَا» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The maṣdar «أن يفرط» is the object of «نَخافُ»; the clause «يَطغى» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative, and the maṣdar is conjoined to the preceding maṣdar.

harrat-mujtaba:46-46.t: The clause «إنني معكما» is resumptive within the scope of the speech, and the clause «أسمع» is a second khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:47-47.t: The clause «فَأَرْسِلْ» is conjoined to the clause «إنَّا رسُولا», and the clause «قد جئناك» is resumptive within the scope of the speech, as is the clause «والسلام على من اتبع». The preposition and its genitive noun «مِن ربِّك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «آية».

harrat-mujtaba:48-48.t: The interpreted maṣdar «أن العذاب ...» is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of «أُوْحِيَ».

harrat-mujtaba:49-49.t: The fāʾ in «فمن» links to an implied (muqaddar) condition, i.e.: إن أوحي إليكما فمَنْ ربكما؟ (if revelation has come to you, then who is your Lord?). The clause «فَمَنْ رَّبُّكُما» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition; the clause {إنَّا قَدْ أُوحِيَ ...} is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech verb), and the clause «يا موسى» is resumptive within the scope of the speech.

harrat-mujtaba:50-50.t: «الذي» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «رَبُّنا»; «خَلْقَهُ» is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

harrat-mujtaba:51-51.t: His saying «فما بالُ»: the fāʾ links to the apodosis of an implied (muqaddar) condition, i.e.: إن كان ربُّكم كذلك فما بال؟ (if your Lord is thus, then what is the state…?). This clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech verb). «ما» is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); «بال» is the khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:52-52.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «في كتاب» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the "being established" (istiqrār) to which the khabar (predicate) is attached, and the clause «لا يَضِلُّ» is resumptive within the scope of the speech.

harrat-mujtaba:53-53.t: «الذي»: the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: هو الذي. The preposition and its genitive noun «لكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the preposition and its genitive noun «مِن نباتٍ» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «أزواجًا»; «شَتَّى» is a second naʿt, i.e.: scattered, differing in colours and taste.

harrat-mujtaba:54-54.t: The clause «كُلُوا» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb of saying, and that saying is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «أخرجنا», i.e.: so We brought forth such-and-such, saying: eat. The preposition and its genitive noun «لأوْلي» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «آيات».

harrat-mujtaba:55-55.t: The clause «خلقناكم» is resumptive. «تارَةً» is a deputy of the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e.: We will bring you forth another bringing forth.

harrat-mujtaba:57-57.t: The clause «يا موسى» is parenthetical between the two conjoined items.

harrat-mujtaba:58-58.t: The clause «نأتينك» is the response to an implied (muqaddar) oath, and the implied oath clause is conjoined to the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech verb). The clause «فاجعلْ» is the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: إن قبلت فاجعل (if you accept, then set). «بيننا»: an adverb of place (ẓarf makān) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object. The clause «لا نُخْلِفُهُ» is a naʿt (adjective) of «مَوْعِدًا». «نَحْنُ» is tawkīd (emphasis) of the latent (mustatir) agent, and the pronoun «أنت» is conjoined to the latent pronoun in «نُخْلفه». «مكانًا» is a badal (substitute) of «موعدًا», and «سُوًى» is a naʿt.

harrat-mujtaba:59-59.t: «يَوْمُ» is the khabar (predicate), and the maṣdar «أَنْ يُحْشَرَ» is conjoined to «يومُ».

harrat-mujtaba:61-61.t: His saying «وَيْلَكُمْ»: a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an unused (muhmal) verb, and the clause «لا تفتَروا» is resumptive within the scope of the speech. His saying «فَيُسْحِتَكُمْ»: the fāʾ is causative (sababiyya), and an imperfect verb in the accusative by a concealed «أن» after the causative fāʾ; the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The interpreted maṣdar is conjoined to a maṣdar extracted (mutaṣayyad) from the preceding speech, i.e.: let there be no fabrication, and then an extirpation. The clause «وقد خاب» is resumptive within the scope of the speech.

harrat-mujtaba:63-63.t: «إنْ» is lightened (mukhaffafa) and inoperative (muhmala), with a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa). The clause «يُرِيدان» is a naʿt (adjective); the maṣdar «أَن يُخْرِجَاكُمْ» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «المثلى» is a naʿt.

harrat-mujtaba:64-64.t: «صَفًا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the wāw, and the clause «وقد أَفلحَ» is resumptive within the scope of the speech.

harrat-mujtaba:65-65.t: «إِمَّا» is a particle of choice (takhyīr), and the maṣdar «أن تلقي» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, i.e.: choose either your throwing or our being the first. The maṣdar «أن نكون» is conjoined to the preceding maṣdar. The relative noun «مَنْ» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

harrat-mujtaba:66-66.t: The clause «بل أَلْقُوا» is resumptive, and the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech verb) is implied (muqaddar), i.e.: I will not throw first. His saying «فإذا»: the fāʾ is a conjunction and «إذا» is the «إذا» of surprise (fujāʾiyya); the clause after it is conjoined to the implied clause «فَأَلْقَوْا», the implied form being: "He said: I will not throw first; rather, you throw. So they threw, and behold…". The maqūl al-qawl is implied, and the implied clause «فألقَوْا» is resumptive. The maṣdar «أنَّهَا تَسْعَى» is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).

harrat-mujtaba:67-67.t: The clause «فأَوْجَسَ» is resumptive. «خِيفَةً» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and «مُوسَى» is the fāʿil (agent) placed later.

harrat-mujtaba:68-68.t: «أنْتَ» is tawkīd (emphasis) of the kāf in «إنك», and «الأعلى» is the khabar (predicate) of inna; the clause «إنك أنت الأعلى» is resumptive within the scope of the speech.

harrat-mujtaba:69-69.t: The clause «وأَلْقِ» is conjoined to the clause {لا تَخَفْ}, and the clause «تَلْقَفْ» is the apodosis of an implied (muqaddar) condition. «إنَّ» is an abrogating particle (nāsikha); «ما» is a relative noun, its noun; «كَيْدُ» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن»; and the clause «ولا يُفْلِحُ» is conjoined to the resumptive one: «إنَِّمَا صَنَعُوا كيدُ».

harrat-mujtaba:70-70.t: The clause «فَأُلْقِي» is resumptive; «سُجَّدا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the sorcerers, and the clause «قالوا» is a second ḥāl of «السحرة».

harrat-mujtaba:71-71.t: The interpreted maṣdar «أَنْ آذَنَ» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); «أَنْ» is a maṣdar-forming particle. The clause «إنه لكبيرُكم» is resumptive; «الذي» is a naʿt (adjective). The clause «فلأقطعَن أيديَكم» is resumptive, and the clause «لأقطعن» is the response to an implied (muqaddar) oath. His saying «ولَتَعْلَمُنَّ»: the wāw is a conjunction, the lām occurs in the answer to the oath, and the verb is an imperfect, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, which was dropped because of the succession of like letters; the wāw, dropped because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, is the fāʿil (agent), and the nūn is for emphasis (tawkīd). «أَيُّنَا»: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and the pronoun is muḍāf ilayhi; «أَشَدُّ» is the khabar (predicate); «عذابا» is tamyīz (specification); «وأبقى» is a noun conjoined to «أشدّ». The clause «أيُّنَا أشد» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb of knowing, which is suspended (muʿallaq).

harrat-mujtaba:72-72.t: His saying «والذي»: the wāw is a conjunction, and the relative noun is conjoined to the preceding «ما». His saying «فاقْضِ»: the fāʾ is resumptive, and an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter. The clause «أنتَ قاضٍ» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and the clause «أنتَ قاضٍ» is the ṣila of the relative noun [Translator's note: this sentence is repeated in the source]. «هذه» is a demonstrative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «الحياةَ الدُّنيا»: a badal (substitute) and its naʿt (adjective). The clause «إنما تَقضِي» is resumptive within the scope of the speech.

harrat-mujtaba:73-73.t: His saying «وما»: the wāw is a conjunction; «ما» is a relative noun conjoined to «خَطايانا»; the preposition and its genitive noun «من السحر» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the hāʾ in «عليه», and the clause «والله خيْرٌ» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:74-74.t: The conditional clause is the khabar (predicate) of «إنَّ». «مَن» is a conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); «مُجْرِمًا»: a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «يأتِ»; the clause «لا يموت» is a ḥāl of the hāʾ in «له».

harrat-mujtaba:75-75.t: The clause «قد عمِل» is a naʿt (adjective) of «مؤمنًا», and «مؤمنًا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the hāʾ in «يَأتِهِ». The clause «فأولئك لهم..» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the clause «لهم الدرجات» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «أولئك».

harrat-mujtaba:76-76.t: «جناتٌ» is a badal (substitute) of {الدَّرَجَاتُ}; the clause «تجري» is a naʿt (adjective) of «جناتُ»; the clause «وذلك جزاء» is resumptive; «مَن» is a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

harrat-mujtaba:77-77.t: «أنْ» is explicative (tafsīriyya), and the clause after it is explicative. The clause «فاضْرِبْ» is conjoined to the clause «أَسْرِ»; the preposition and its genitive noun «في البحر» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «طريقًا»; «يَبَسًا» is a second naʿt; the clause «لا تخاف» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun of «اضربْ», i.e.: strike, not fearing.

harrat-mujtaba:78-78.t: The clause «فأَتْبَعَهُمْ» is resumptive, and the clause «فغشيهم» is conjoined to the clause «أتبعَهم»; «ما» is a relative noun, fāʿil (agent).

harrat-mujtaba:79-79.t: The clause «وأَضَلَّ» is conjoined to the clause {فَأَتْبَعَهُمْ}.

harrat-mujtaba:80-80.t: The clause «قد أنجيناكم» is the response to the vocative, resumptive; «جانب» is the second object of the appointing (muwāʿada), and «الأيمن» is a naʿt (adjective) of «جانب».

harrat-mujtaba:81-81.t: The clause «كُلُوا» is resumptive; the preposition and its genitive noun «من طيبات» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; «ما» is a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). His saying «فَيَحِلَّ»: the fāʾ is causative (sababiyya), and the interpreted maṣdar is conjoined to a maṣdar extracted (mutaṣayyad) from the preceding speech, i.e.: let there be no transgression, and then a descending of My wrath. The clause «ومَن يَحْلِلْ» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:82-82.t: The clause «وإني لَغَفَّارٌ» is resumptive, and the preposition and its genitive noun «لمن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «غفَّار».

harrat-mujtaba:83-83.t: «وما أَعْجَلَكَ»: the wāw is resumptive; «ما» is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause «أَعْجَلك» is the khabar (predicate); the clause «يا موسى» is resumptive within the context of the question.

harrat-mujtaba:84-84.t: «هُمْ أُولاءِ»: mubtadaʾ (subject), and «أُولاءِ» is a demonstrative, the object of an omitted verb, i.e.: أعني هؤلاء (I mean these). The preposition and its genitive noun «على أثَرِي» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate). The clause «أعني أولاء» is parenthetical, and the clause «رَبِّ» is parenthetical; the maṣdar «لترضى» is genitive, attached to «عَجِلْتُ».

harrat-mujtaba:85-85.t: The maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech verb) is implied (muqaddar), i.e.: do not wait for your people, for We…; the clause «فإنَّا قَد فَتَنَّا» is conjoined to the implied object of the speech, and the clause «وأضَلَّهم السَّامري» is conjoined to the clause «فتنَّا».

harrat-mujtaba:86-86.t: «غضبانَ أسفًا»: two ḥāls (circumstantials) of Moses. «يَا قَوْمِ»: the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, accusative with a fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the dropped yāʾ. The clause «فطال» is conjoined to the clause «ألم يَعِدْكم»; the clause «أَرَدتم» is conjoined to the clause «طال»; and the clause «فأخلفتم» is conjoined to the clause «أردتم».

harrat-mujtaba:87-87.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «بمَلْكِنَا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أخلف», and the clause «ولكنَّا حُمِّلْنَا» is conjoined to «ما أخلفنا». The preposition and its genitive noun «مِن زِينة» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «أَوْزَارًا»; the clause «فقذفناها» is conjoined to the clause «حُمِّلنا»; the clause «أَلْقَى» is resumptive. His saying «فكذلك»: the fāʾ is resumptive, the kāf is a deputy of the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and the demonstrative is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the implied form is: أَلْقَى السامري إلقاءً مثلَ ذلك الإلقاء (the Sāmirī threw a throwing like that throwing).

harrat-mujtaba:88-88.t: The clause «فأخرجَ» is conjoined to the clause {أَلْقَى}; «جسدا» is a naʿt (adjective), and the clause «لَهُ خُوَارٌ» is a second naʿt; the clause «فَنَسِي» is conjoined to the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech verb).

harrat-mujtaba:89-89.t: The clause «أَفَلا يَرَوْنَ» is resumptive. «أن» is lightened from the heavy one (mukhaffafa min al-thaqīla), and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); the clause «لا يَرْجِعُ» is the khabar (predicate) of «أن», and the maṣdar stands in place of the two objects of «يرون». The preposition and its genitive noun «لهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of «ضَرًّا».

harrat-mujtaba:90-90.t: The clause «ولقد قال لهم هارونُ» is resumptive, and the clause «لقد قال» is the answer to the oath. The clause «إنَّمَا فُتِنْتُم» is the response to the vocative, resumptive; the clause «وإنَّ ربَّكم الرحمنُ» is conjoined to the clause «إنما فتنتم», and the clause «فاتَّبِعُونِي» is conjoined to the clause «إن ربكم الرحمن».

harrat-mujtaba:91-91.t: «نبرحَ» is an abrogating (nāsikh) imperfect verb, accusative; «عاكفين» is the khabar (predicate) of «نبرح»; and the interpreted maṣdar (حتى أن يرجع) is genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «عاكفين».

harrat-mujtaba:92-92.t: «ما» is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause «منَعَك» is the khabar (predicate). «إذْ» is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān) attached to (mutaʿalliq) «منع»; the clause «رأيتَهم» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the clause «ضَلُّوا» is the second object.

harrat-mujtaba:93-93.t: «ألا»: an «أنْ» that puts the verb in the accusative, and a redundant (zāʾida) lā; the maṣdar is the second object of «منع», i.e.: what prevented you from following me? «منع» is transitive by itself and with «مِن», as in: منعتُه النومَ and منعتُه مِن النوم (I prevented him from sleep). The clause «تتبعن» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative, and the clause «أفعصَيت» is conjoined to the clause «تتبعن».

harrat-mujtaba:94-94.t: «يا ابْنَ أُمَّ»: yā is the vocative particle; «ابن» is the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf; «أُمَّ» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive with a kasra implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the first-person yāʾ, which was changed into an alif and then dropped for lightness. The clause «إني خشِيت» is resumptive within the scope of the speech, and the maṣdar «أن تقُول» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

harrat-mujtaba:95-95.t: The maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech verb) is implied (muqaddar), i.e.: he said: this is my brother's speech. The clause «فما خَطْبُك» is conjoined to the object of the speech; «ما» is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and «وخطبُك» is the khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:96-96.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «بما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «بَصُرْتُ»; the preposition and its genitive noun «مِن أثر» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «قبضة». His saying «وكذلك»: the wāw is resumptive, and the kāf is a deputy of the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e.: سوَّلتْ لي تسويلا مثلَ ذلك التسويل (it enticed me an enticing like that enticing); the clause «سوَّلتْ» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:97-97.t: The clause «فاذهبْ» is the apodosis of an implied (muqaddar) condition, i.e.: إن تكفر فاذهب (if you disbelieve, then go), and the clause «فإن لك..» is conjoined to the clause «اذهب». The maṣdar «أنْ تقُول» is the noun of inna; the preposition and its genitive noun «لك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate); the preposition and its genitive noun «في الحياة» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the kāf. «لا» is the lā of generic negation, with its noun, and the khabar is omitted, its implied form being: موجود (existing). The clause «لن تُخْلفَه» is a naʿt (adjective) of «موعدًا»; «عاكفًا» is the khabar of ẓalla; the clause «لَنُحَرِّقَنَّهُ» is the answer to the oath, and the oath with its response is a resumptive clause.

harrat-mujtaba:98-98.t: «إنَّمَا»: a restraining particle (kāffa) and the restrained one (makfūfa), with a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). «الذي» is a naʿt (adjective) of «إلهُكم», and the clause of divine transcendence (jumlat al-tanzīh) is the ṣila (relative clause); «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr); «هو» is a badal (substitute) of the latent (mustatir) pronoun in the omitted khabar. The clause «وَسِعَ» is resumptive, and «علمًا» is tamyīz (specification).

harrat-mujtaba:99-99.t: (كذلك نقص عليك) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The kāf is a deputy of the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and «ذلك» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), i.e.: نَقُصُّ عليك قصصًا مثل ذلك القصص (We relate to you a relating like that relating). The two preposition and its genitive nouns are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause «نقصُّ» is resumptive; «ذكرًا»: the second object.

harrat-mujtaba:100-100.t: «مَنْ» is a conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); the conditional clause is a naʿt (adjective) of {ذِكْرًا}, and the clause «فإنه يحمل» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), in the position of the jussive.

harrat-mujtaba:101-101.t: «خالدين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of {يَحْمِلُ}; it came in the plural form in consideration of the meaning of the preceding «مَن», having first been construed according to its wording, so the pronoun was made singular. The preposition and its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خالدين». His saying «وَسَاء»: the wāw is a conjunction; «ساء» is a past verb whose fāʿil is the pronoun huwa, i.e.: وساء الحمل (and evil is the burden). The preposition and its genitive noun «لَهُم» is attached to a ḥāl of «حملا»; «حملا» is tamyīz (specification), explaining the pronoun of «ساء». The one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being: وِزْرُهُم (their burden), i.e.: وساء الحِمل حِملا وِزْرُهُم (and evil as a burden is their burden). The clause «وساء» is conjoined to the single word «خالدين».

harrat-mujtaba:102-102.t: «يَوم» is a badal (substitute) of {يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ}; the preposition and its genitive noun «في الصور» is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يُنفَخ»; «زُرْقًا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «المجرمين»; and the tanwīn in «يَوْمَئِذٍ» is a compensation for a clause.

harrat-mujtaba:103-103.t: The clause «يَتخافتُون» is a second ḥāl (circumstantial) of {الْمُجْرِمِينَ}. «إنْ» is negating; «عَشْرًا» is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān) attached to (mutaʿalliq) «لَبِثتُم». The clause «إنْ لبثتم» is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech verb) of an omitted verb of saying which is a ḥāl of the wāw, the implied form being: قائلين (saying). The tāʾ was omitted from «عَشرًا» because what it specifies is the nights.

harrat-mujtaba:104-104.t: The clause «نحنُ أَعلمُ» is resumptive. The bāʾ is a preposition, «ما» is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), and the genitive maṣdar is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أعلم». «إذْ» is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to «أعلم»; «طَرِيقةً» is tamyīz (specification); «إنْ» is negating; «يومًا» is an adverb attached to the verb.

harrat-mujtaba:105-105.t: The clause «فَقُلْ» is conjoined to the clause «ويسألونك».

harrat-mujtaba:106-106.t: The clause «فَيَذَرُهَا» is conjoined to the clause {يَنْسِفُهَا}; «قاعًا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun hāʾ; «صَفْصَفًا»: a second ḥāl.

harrat-mujtaba:107-107.t: The clause «لا تَرَى» is a third ḥāl (circumstantial) of the hāʾ in {فَيَذَرُهَا}.

harrat-mujtaba:108-108.t: The clause «يتَّبعون» is resumptive; the clause «لا عِوَجَ له» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الداعي»; the clause «وخشَعتِ الأصوات» is conjoined to the clause «يتبعون»; and the clause «فلا تَسمعُ» is conjoined to the clause «خشَعت».

harrat-mujtaba:109-109.t: «يومَئذ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تنفع»; the clause «لا تنفعُ» is resumptive; «مَن» is a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

harrat-mujtaba:110-110.t: The clause «يَعلمُ» is resumptive, and the clause «ولا يحيطون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the hāʾ in «خلفهم». «علمًا» is a deputy of the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object): a maṣdar (verbal noun) synonymous with the word governing it.

harrat-mujtaba:111-111.t: The clause «وعَنَتِ الْوُجُوهُ» is resumptive, and so is the clause «وقد خاب».

harrat-mujtaba:112-112.t: The clause «ومَن يعملْ» is resumptive; the clause «وهو مؤمن» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «يعملْ». The clause «فلا يخاف» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: فهو لا يخاف (then he does not fear), and the clause «فهو لا يخاف» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the clause «فلا يخاف» cannot be the apodosis, because an imperfect verb joined with «لا» does not take the fāʾ. The preposition and its genitive noun «مِن الصالحات» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted qualified noun, i.e.: شيئًا كائنًا من الصالحات (something that is of the righteous deeds).

harrat-mujtaba:113-113.t: His saying «وكذلك»: the wāw is a conjunction, the kāf is a deputy of the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and the demonstrative is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), i.e.: أنزلناه إنزالا مثلَ ذلك الإنزالِ (We sent it down a sending down like that sending down). The clause «أنزلناه» is resumptive. His saying «قرآنًا»: a ḥāl (circumstantial); the ḥāl may be a non-derived (jāmid) noun here because it is qualified. The clause «لعلهم يتقون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:114-114.t: The clause «فَتَعَالَى الله» is conjoined to the clause {أَنْزَلْنَاهُ}; «الملك الحق» are two naʿts (adjectives) of the name of Majesty. The clause «رَبِّ زِدْنِي عِلْما» is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech verb), and «علمًا» is the second object.

harrat-mujtaba:115-115.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «لَهُ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the clause «وَلَمْ نَجِدْ» is conjoined to the clause «نَسي».

harrat-mujtaba:116-116.t: «وَإِذْ»: the wāw is resumptive, and «إذ» is the object of an implied (muqaddar) «اذْكُرْ» (remember); the clause «أَبَى» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:117-117.t: The clause «فَقُلْنَا» is resumptive. His saying «وَلِزَوْجِكَ»: conjoined to the kāf in «لك», attached to (mutaʿalliq) what that is attached to. The clause «فلا يخرجنَّكما» is conjoined to the clause «إن هذا عدو». The fāʾ in «فتشقى» is causative (sababiyya); His saying «فَتَشْقَى»: an imperfect verb in the accusative by a concealed «أن», and the interpreted maṣdar is conjoined to a maṣdar extracted (mutaṣayyad) from the preceding speech, i.e.: let there be no expelling of you both from it, and then misery for you.

harrat-mujtaba:118-118.t: The interpreted maṣdar «ألا تجوع» is the noun of inna, and the preposition and its genitive noun «لك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb.

harrat-mujtaba:119-119.t: The maṣdar «وأنك لا تظمأ» is conjoined to the preceding maṣdar, in the position of the accusative.

harrat-mujtaba:120-120.t: The clause «فَوَسْوَسَ» is resumptive; the clause «قال» is explicative of the whispering; the clause «لا يَبْلى» is a naʿt (adjective) of «مُلْكٍ».

harrat-mujtaba:121-121.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «عليهما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an implied (muqaddar) «أعني» (I mean); the clause «يخصفان» is the khabar (predicate) of «طفق»; and the clause «وعَصَى» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:122-122.t: The clause «اجْتَبَاهُ» is conjoined to the clause {وَعَصَى}.

harrat-mujtaba:123-123.t: «جميعا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «اهبطا»; the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «عَدُو»; and the clause «بعضكم لبعض عدو» is a second ḥāl of the agent of «اهْبِطَا». The clause «فإما يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مني هُدًى» is conjoined to the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech verb). The clause «مَن اتَّبَعَ هُدَايَ» is the apodosis of the first condition; the clause «لا يَضِلُّ» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being: هو, and the clause «فهو لا يضل» is the apodosis of the second condition.

harrat-mujtaba:124-124.t: The clause «ونَحْشُرُهُ» is resumptive, and His saying «أعمى» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the hāʾ in «نحشره».

harrat-mujtaba:125-125.t: «لِمَ»: the lām is a preposition, and «ما» is an interrogative noun in the position of the genitive; its alif was dropped for lightness because it is preceded by the preposition. «أعمى» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the yāʾ, and the clause «وقد كنت بصيرا» is a second ḥāl of the yāʾ in «حشرتني».

harrat-mujtaba:126-126.t: His saying «كذلك»: the kāf is a deputy of the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and the demonstrative is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), i.e.: أتتك إتيانًا مثل ذلك الإتيان (they came to you a coming like that coming). The clause «أتتك» is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech verb), and the clause «تُنْسَى» is conjoined to the clause «نسيتُها».

harrat-mujtaba:127-127.t: The clause «نَجْزِي» is conjoined to the clause {تُنْسَى}; the clause «ولَعَذَابُ الآخِرَةِ أَشَدُّ» is resumptive, and the lām is for emphasis (taʾkīd).

harrat-mujtaba:128-128.t: The fāʿil (agent) of «يَهْدِ» is implied (muqaddar), indicated by the verb, i.e.: guidance. «كم» is the predicative (khabariyya) kam, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the preposition and its genitive noun «مِنَ الْقُرُونِ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of «كم»; the clause «يمشون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the hāʾ in «لهم». The clause «أَهْلَكْنَا» is the mafʿūl bihi of «يَهْدِ», which is suspended (muʿallaq) by «كم», containing the meaning of knowing. The preposition and its genitive noun «لأولِي» is attached to a naʿt of «لآيَاتٍ».

harrat-mujtaba:129-129.t: The clause «ولَوْلا كَلِمَةٌ» is resumptive. «لولا» is a particle of impossibility because of existence (imtināʿ li-wujūd), and «كلمة» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being: موجود (existing). «لِزَامًا» is the khabar of kāna, and its noun is the pronoun of the destruction. His saying «وأَجَلٌ»: conjoined to «كلمة».

harrat-mujtaba:130-130.t: The clause «فَاصْبِرْ» is resumptive. «ما» is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), and the interpreted maṣdar is genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «اصبِرْ». The preposition and its genitive noun «بِحَمْدِ» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «سَبِّحْ». His saying «ومِن آنَاءِ الَّليْلِ»: the wāw is a conjunction, and the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to «سَبِّحْ»; the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida). «أَطْرَافَ»: a noun conjoined to the position of «مِنْ آناء» and attached to what that is attached to. The clause «لَعَلَّكَ تَرْضَى» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:131-131.t: «أزواجًا» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «زَهْرَةَ» is a badal (substitute) of «أزواجًا», on the supposition that they were made the very splendour itself. The genitive interpreted maṣdar «لِنَفْتِنَهُمْ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مَتَّعْنَا», and the clause «ورِزْقُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌ» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:132-132.t: The clause «لا نَسْأَلُكَ» is resumptive, and so is the clause «نَحْنُ نَرْزُقُكَ», and the clause «وَالْعَاقِبَةُ لِلتَّقْوَى».

harrat-mujtaba:133-133.t: «لولا» is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ); the preposition and its genitive noun «مِن ربِّهِ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «آية». The clause «لَوْلا يَأْتِينَا» is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech verb); the clause «أَوَلَمْ تَأْتِهِمْ» is resumptive; «ما» is a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

harrat-mujtaba:134-134.t: His saying «وَلَوْ أَنَّا»: the wāw is resumptive; «لو» is a particle of impossibility because of impossibility (imtināʿ li-imtināʿ), and the interpreted maṣdar is the fāʿil (agent) of an implied (muqaddar) «ثبت»; the clause «ولو ثبت أنَّا» is resumptive. The preposition and its genitive noun «من قبله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «عذاب». «لولا» is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ); the fāʾ is causative (sababiyya), and «نَتَّبِعَ» is an imperfect verb in the accusative by a concealed «أن» after the causative fāʾ; the interpreted maṣdar is conjoined to a maṣdar extracted (mutaṣayyad) from the preceding speech, i.e.: would that there were a sending from You, and then a following from us.

harrat-mujtaba:135-135.t: The tanwīn in «كُلٌّ» is a compensation for a single word, i.e.: كل أحد (every one). The clause «فَتَرَبَّصُوا» is conjoined to the clause «كُلٌّ مُتَرَبِّصٌ»; the clause «فستعلمون» is resumptive; the clause «مَنْ أصْحَابُ» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb of knowing, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative. «مَنْ» is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and «أصحاب» is its khabar (predicate); the clause «مَنِ اهْتَدَى» is conjoined to the clause «مَنْ أصْحَابُ».

mekki-muskil:12-12.t: His saying {طوى}: whoever leaves it without tanwīn, his reason is that it is deflected (maʿdūl), like عمر, and it is definite; and it is said that it is feminine, a name of the spot of land, and it is definite. Whoever gives it tanwīn makes it a name of the place, not deflected, like صُرَد. In both views it is a badal (substitute) from الْوَادي.

mekki-muskil:17-17.t: His saying {وَمَا تِلْكَ بيمينك}: تِلْكَ according to al-Zajjāj has the meaning of الَّتِي (relative noun), and بيمينك is its ṣila (relative clause). According to al-Farrāʾ it has the meaning of هَذِه, and هَذِه and تلك according to him require a ṣila like الَّتِي. Quṭrub reported from Ibn ʿAbbās that تِلْكَ has the meaning of هَذِه. مَا is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and what follows it is the khabar (predicate). The meaning of the interrogative here is to draw attention (tanbīh).

mekki-muskil:22-22.t: His saying {تخرج بَيْضَاء}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in تخرج. آية is a badal (substitute) from بَيْضَاء, likewise a ḥāl, i.e. it comes out making clear the power of Allah (exalted be His mention). It is also said that آية is accusative by an implied verb, the implied form being "We have given you another sign" (آتيناك آيَة أُخْرَى). The nominative is permissible outside the Qurʾān, on the sense "this is a sign" (هَذِه آيَة).

mekki-muskil:29-30.t: His saying {وَاجعَل لي وزيرا من أَهلِي هَارُون}: هَارُون is a badal (substitute) from وزير; and it is said to be accusative by اجعل with fronting and postponement (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr), i.e. "and make Hārūn, my brother, a minister for me" (وَاجعَل لي هَارُون أخي وزيرا).

mekki-muskil:3-3.t: His saying, the Exalted, {إِلَّا تذكرة}: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), or as a maṣdar (verbal noun). And تنزيلا is a maṣdar.

mekki-muskil:33-33.t:
His saying {نسبحك كثيرا}: كثيرا is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "that we may glorify You with much glorification" (نسبحك تسبيحا كثيرا), or a naʿt of an omitted time, its implied form being "that we may glorify You a long time" (نسبحك وقتا طَويلا).
Whoever reads with the connecting alif in اشْدُد and with fatḥa on the alif of أشركه makes it a supplication and request, so it is indeclinable (mabnī). Whoever reads with the disjunctive alif in اشْدُد and ḍamma on the alif of أشركه — and that is Ibn ʿĀmir — makes it jussive (majzūm) as the answer to اجعل [Translator's note: the source writes لأجعل], so the two alifs are the alifs of the first person. In the first reading, the first alif is a connecting alif (alif waṣl) and the second a disjunctive alif (alif qaṭʿ).

mekki-muskil:39-39.t: His saying {أَن اقذفيه فِي التابوت فاقذفيه فِي اليم}: أَن is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) from مَا. The first hāʾ in اقذفيه refers to Mūsā (peace be upon him), and the second to the chest (التابوت).

mekki-muskil:52-52.t: His saying {فِي كتاب لَا يضل رَبِّي وَلَا ينسى}: what comes after كتاب, of the two clauses, is a description (ṣifa) of it. رَبِّي is in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition, its implied form being "the Book does not stray from my Lord, nor forget" (لَا يضل الْكتاب عَن رَبِّي وَلَا ينسى). It may also be that رَبِّي is in the position of the nominative, straying and forgetting being denied of Him. We have explained this verse in the book al-Hidāya more fully than this.

mekki-muskil:58-58.t:
His saying {مَكَانا سوى}: مكان is accusative as the second object of جعل. It may not be made accusative by الْموعد, because it has been described by His saying, the Exalted,
{لَا نخلفه نَحن وَلَا أَنْت}; and nouns that govern as verbs do, when they are described or made diminutive, do not govern, because by description and diminution they leave their resemblance to verbs, since verbs are neither described nor made diminutive. So when, by description and diminution, they leave the resemblance to the verb, they are barred from governing. This is a principle on which the Basrans do not differ. Likewise, when you predicate something of maṣdars (verbal nouns) or conjoin something to them, it is not permissible to make them govern anything after that, because you would be separating the ṣila from the mawṣūl (the relative) — for what is governed is included in the ṣila of the maṣdar, whereas the khabar and the conjoined are not included in the ṣila. Nor is it good for مَكَانا in this place to be an adverb (ẓarf), because the Arabs did not treat الْموعد with adverbs as they treat the other maṣdars with them. Do you not see that He, the Exalted, said {إِن موعدهم الصُّبْح} with the nominative? Had you said إن خروجهم الصبح, nothing but the accusative would be allowed in الصبح, on the implied form "the time of the morning". And الْموعد has come as a noun of place: Allah (exalted be His mention) said {وَإِن جَهَنَّم لموعدهم أَجْمَعِينَ}, and it has been said that its meaning is "the place of their appointment".
And His saying {سوى}: it is a description (ṣifa) of مكان. But whoever reads the sīn with kasra makes it rare, because فِعَل has come as an adjective only rarely, as in هم قوم عِدًى ("they are a hostile people"). Whoever reads the sīn with ḍamma brings it on the more common pattern, because فُعَل is frequent among adjectives, e.g. رجل حُطَم, لُبَد and شُكَع, and it is frequent.

mekki-muskil:102-102.t: His saying {زرقا}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْمُجْرمين.

mekki-muskil:59-59.t:
His saying {مَوْعدكُمْ يَوْم الزِّينَة}: the nominative in يَوْم is as the khabar (predicate) of مَوْعدكُمْ, on the assumption of an omitted muḍāf, its implied form being "your appointment is the time of the day of adornment" (مَوْعدكُمْ وَقت يَوْم الزِّينَة). Al-Ḥasan read يَوْم الزِّينَة in the accusative as an adverb (ẓarf).
And His saying {وَأَن يحْشر النَّاس ضحى}: أَن is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to يَوْم, on the implied form "your appointment is the time of the day of adornment and the time of the gathering of the people". It is also said that أَن is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to الزِّينَة. Whoever reads يَوْم الزِّينَة in the accusative makes أَن in the position of the accusative, conjoined to يَوْم الزِّينَة; and it may be in the position of the nominative on the implied form "your appointment is the time of the gathering of the people", or in the position of the genitive, conjoined to الزِّينَة.

mekki-muskil:63-63.t:
His saying {إِن هَذَانِ لساحران}: whoever reads هَذَانِ in the nominative takes it according to a dialect of Banū al-Ḥārith ibn Kaʿb, who bring the dual with alif in every state. One of them said:
... تزَود منا بَين أذنَاهُ طعنة ... دَعَتْهُ هابي التُّرَاب عقيم ...
(He took from us, between his ears, a thrust as provision that called him to the dusty, barren earth.)
It is said that إِن has the meaning of نعم ("yes"); and there is remoteness (improbability) in this because of the entry of the lām into the khabar (predicate), and that occurs only in poetry, as in his saying:
... أم الْحُلَيْس لعجوز شهربه ... ترْضى من اللَّحْم بِعظم الرقبه ...
(Umm al-Ḥulays is surely an old crone, content, of meat, with the bone of the neck.)
The proper form of the speech would have been لأم الْحُلَيْس عَجُوز. Likewise the proper form of the speech in the verse, if you take إن in the meaning of نعم, would have been إِن لهذان ساحران, as you say نعم لهذان ساحران and نعم لمُحَمد رَسُول الله. And in the lām coming late together with the word إن there is some strength for [the view of] نعم.
It is said that since the vague nouns (al-mubham, i.e. demonstratives) show no inflection in the singular or in the plural, the dual was treated likewise, and the alif was brought in every state. And it is said that the hāʾ [of the pronoun] is implied with إن, its implied form being إِنَّه هَذَانِ لساحران, as you say إِنَّه زيد منطلق; and this is a good view, were it not that the entry of the lām into the khabar makes it remote.
As for whoever reads إن light (without doubling), it is a good reading, because he set the i'rab right and did not contradict the script; but the entry of the lām into the khabar opposes it according to the school of Sībawayh, because he assumes it is the one lightened from the heavy [إنّ], so that what follows it became nominative as mubtadaʾ and khabar because of the deficiency of its form, and what follows it returned to its origin; and the lām does not enter the khabar of a mubtadaʾ that has come in its original form, except in poetry, as we mentioned. But according to the school of the Kufans it is among the best of things, because they take the light إن in the meaning of مَا and the lām in the meaning of إِلَّا, so the implied form of the speech is "these two are nothing but two sorcerers" (مَا هَذَانِ إِلَّا ساحران). There is no defect in this interpretation except what they claim, that the lām comes in the meaning of إِلَّا.

mekki-muskil:66-66.t: His saying {يخيل إِلَيْهِ من سحرهم أَنَّهَا تسْعَى}: whoever reads يخيل with yāʾ makes أَن in the position of the nominative, because it is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of يُخيَّل. Whoever reads تخيل with tāʾ — and that is Ibn Dhakwān — makes أَن in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) from the latent pronoun in تخيل, and it is a substitute of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl). The like of that is permissible in the reading of whoever reads with yāʾ, on the basis that you make the verb masculine according to the meaning. It is also possible that أَن, in the reading of whoever reads with tāʾ, is in the position of the accusative on the assumption of the omission of the bāʾ [Translator's note: the source writes خذف for حذف], its implied form being "it was made to seem to him by their magic that it was moving" (تخيل اليه من سحرهم بِأَنَّهَا تسْعَى), and you make the maṣdar or إليه in the position of the nāʾib fāʿil.

mekki-muskil:67-67.t: His saying {فأوجس فِي نَفسه خيفة مُوسَى}: مُوسَى is in the position of the nominative by أوجس, and خيفة is the object of أوجس. The origin of خيفة is خوفة; then the wāw was replaced by a yāʾ and what precedes it given kasra so that the pattern فِعْلة would be sound. Mūsā only feared that the people would be led astray; and it is said that when the revelation to throw his staff was slow to come to him, he feared; and it is said rather that human nature overcame him on seeing what he was not accustomed to. And Allah knows best.

mekki-muskil:69-69.t:
His saying {وألق مَا فِي يَمِينك تلقف مَا صَنَعُوا}: whoever reads تلقف in the jussive makes it the answer to the imperative. Whoever reads it in the nominative — and that is Ibn Dhakwān — makes it nominative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from مَا, which is the staff; and it is said to be a ḥāl from the one throwing, who is Mūsā, the swallowing being attributed to him since it came about through his action and movement, as He said {وَمَا رميت إِذْ رميت وَلَكِن الله رمى}. It is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), because it only swallowed their ropes after he had thrown it.
His saying {إِنَّمَا صَنَعُوا كيد سَاحر}: مَا is the noun of إِن, with the meaning of الَّذِي, and كيد is its khabar; the hāʾ is omitted from صَنَعُوا, its implied form being "that which they have made is the trick of a sorcerer" (إِن الَّذِي صنعوه كيد سَاحر). Whoever reads كيد سحر, its meaning is "the trick of one possessing sorcery". It is permissible in ordinary speech to make كيد accusative by صنعوا and not to imply a hāʾ, on the basis that you make مَا the restraining (kāffa) particle that stops إن from governing. And it is permissible to read أَن with fatḥa, in the meaning "because what they have made…" (لِأَن مَا صَنَعُوا).

mekki-muskil:72-72.t:
His saying {إِنَّمَا تقضي هَذِه الْحَيَاة الدُّنْيَا}: مَا is the restraining (kāffa) particle that stops إن from governing, and هَذِه is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), and الْحَيَاة is a badal (substitute) from هَذِه or a naʿt (adjective), its implied form being "you will only decree in this worldly life" (انما تقضى فِي هَذِه الْحَيَاة الدُّنْيَا). It is permissible in ordinary speech to put هَذِه and الْحَيَاة in the nominative, on the basis that you make مَا have the meaning of الَّذِي, with the hāʾ omitted with تقضى, and هَذِه is the khabar of إن [Translator's note: the source has خبز ان, evidently for خبر إن], and الْحَيَاة is a badal from هَذِه or a naʿt, its implied form being "that which you decree is the matter of this worldly life" (ان الَّذِي تقضيه أَمر هَذِه الْحَيَاة الدُّنْيَا).
His saying {وَالَّذِي فطرنا}: الَّذِي is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to مَا; or, if you wish, as an oath.

mekki-muskil:73-73.t: His saying {وَمَا أكرهتنا عَلَيْهِ}: مَا is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to الْخَطَايَا; and it is said to be a negating particle. If you make مَا negating, مِن is attached to (mutaʿalliq) الخطايا; and if you make مَا have the meaning of الَّذِي, مِن is attached to أكرهتنا.

mekki-muskil:77-77.t:
His saying {لَا تخَاف دركا وَلَا تخشى}: whoever reads تخَاف in the nominative makes it a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent, who is Mūsā (peace be upon him), and the implied form is "strike for them a path in the sea, not fearing being overtaken nor dreading" (اضْرِب لَهُم طَرِيقا فِي الْبَحْر غير خَائِف دركا وَلَا خاشيا). The nominative of تخاف is strengthened by the consensus of the readers on the nominative of تخشى, which is conjoined to تخاف. It is permissible to read تخَاف in the nominative as a break (qaṭʿ, a new sentence), i.e. "you do not fear being overtaken" (أَنْت لَا تخَاف دركا). It is also said that its nominative is as a naʿt (adjective) of طريق, on the assumption of the omission of فيه ("in which"). Whoever reads تخاف in the jussive — and that is Ḥamza — makes it the answer to the imperative, which is فَاضْرب, and the implied form is "if you strike, you will not fear being overtaken by those behind you" (إِن تضرب لَا تخف دركا مِمَّن خَلفك); and وَلَا تخشى is nominative as a break, i.e. "and you do not dread drowning". It is also said that the jussive in لَا تخف is as a prohibition. Al-Farrāʾ permitted وَلَا تخشى to be in the position of the jussive with the alif retained, as the yāʾ and the wāw are retained on the assumption that the vowel has been dropped from them. But this is not permissible with the alif, because it never takes a vowel except by being changed into something else, whereas the wāw and the yāʾ take vowels without being changed.
His saying {ألم يَعدكُم ربكُم وَعدا حسنا}: الْوَعْد may have the meaning of "what is promised" (الْمَوْعُود), just as الْخلق came with the meaning of "what is created" (الْمَخْلُوق); so وَعدا on this interpretation is accusative as the second object of يعدكم, on the assumption of an omitted muḍāf, its implied form being "Did your Lord not promise you the fulfilment of a good promise?" (ألم يَعدكُم ربكُم تَمام وعد حسن). And وعد may be accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun).
