﴿قال يا ابن أم لا تأخذ بلحيتي ولا برأسي﴾: (يا ابن أم): (يا) is a vocative particle, and (ابن) is a vocative (munādā) in a genitive construct, accusative (manṣūb); (أم) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive with a kasra implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the alif that was elided for lightness, and the elided alif, converted from the yāʾ, is muḍāf ilayhi; it is also said: they are two indeclinable (mabnī) nouns because they have been compounded in the way numbers and adverbs are compounded; (لا) is prohibitive; (تأخذ) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive (لا), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you" (أنت); (بلحيتي) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تأخذ﴾; and (ولا برأسي) is conjoined to (بلحيتي).
﴿إني خشيت أن تقول فرقت بين بني إسرائيل ولم ترقب قولي﴾: (إن) is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle, and the yāʾ is a pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative as the noun of inna; the clause (خشيت) is the khabar (predicate) of inna; (أن) together with what falls within its scope is the object of (خشيت); the clause (فرقت) is the content of the speech (maqūl al-qawl); (بين) is an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿فرقت﴾; (بني إسرائيل) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (ولم ترقب قولي) is conjoined to (فرقت), the pronoun in (قولي) then referring to Moses; or it is conjoined to (خشيت), the pronoun in (قولي) then referring to Aaron.

muyesser-irab:95-95.t: ﴿قال فما خطبك يا سامري﴾: (قال) is a past verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو), referring back to Moses; the fāʾ is a conjunction or resumptive; (ما) is interrogative, a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (خطبك) is the khabar (predicate); (يا) is a vocative particle, and (سامري) is a vocative (munādā), a single proper noun; and the clause ﴿فما خطبك يا سامري﴾ is conjoined to the content of the speech (maqūl al-qawl), or resumptive with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:96-96.t:
﴿قال بصرت بما لم يبصروا به فقبضت قبضة من أثر الرسول﴾: the clause (بصرت) is the content of the speech (maqūl al-qawl), and the fāʿil (agent) of (قال) is "he", i.e. al-Sāmirī; (بما) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿بصرت﴾; the clause (لم يبصروا به) is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position; (فقبضت) is conjoined to (بصرت); (قبضة) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿من أثر﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (قبضة); (أثر) is muḍāf, and (الرسول) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), on the assumption of two omitted words, i.e.: "from the trace of the hoof of the Messenger's horse".
﴿فنبذتها وكذلك سولت لي نفسي﴾: (فنبذتها) is conjoined to (قبضت); (وكذلك): the kāf is a noun meaning "like", indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e.: "with the like of that enticement my soul enticed me"; ﴿ذلك﴾: ﴿ذا﴾ is a demonstrative in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, the lām is for distance, and the kāf is a particle of address; and (سولت لي نفسي) is a verb and its fāʿil.

muyesser-irab:97-97.t:
﴿قال فاذهب فإن لك في الحياة أن تقول لا مساس﴾: (قال) is a past verb, and its fāʿil (agent) refers back to Moses; (فاذهب): the fāʾ is a conjunction, and (اذهب) is an imperative verb whose fāʿil is "you" (أنت); (فإن): the fāʾ is a conjunction, and (إن) is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle; ﴿لك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate) of inna; (في الحياة) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); (أن) together with what follows it is the noun of inna; (لا) is the lā of generic negation; (مساس) is the noun of (لا); and the khabar is omitted.
﴿وإن لك موعدا لن تخلفه﴾: (إن) is an abrogating particle; ﴿لك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted, fronted khabar of inna; (موعدًا) is its postponed noun; (لن) is a particle of negation, accusative and future; (تخلفه) is accusative (manṣūb) by (لن); the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you" (أنت); and the hāʾ is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿وانظر إلى إلهك الذي ظلت عليه عاكفا لنحرقنه ثم لننسفنه في اليم نسفا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (انظر) is an imperative verb, and its fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "you" (أنت); (إلى إلهك) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿انظر﴾; (الذي) is a naʿt (adjective); the clause (ظلت) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (الذي), with no grammatical position; (ظلت) is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; (عليه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿عاكفًا﴾; (عاكفًا) is the khabar of (ظلت); (لنحرقنه): the lām occurs in the answer to the oath, and (نحرقنه) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is joined to the nūn of emphasis, the fāʿil being latent, its implied form being "we" (نحن), and the hāʾ a mafʿūl bihi; (ثم) is a conjunction; (لننسفنه): the lām occurs in the answer to the oath, and (ننسفنه) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa because it is joined to the nūn of emphasis; (في اليم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿ننسفنه﴾; and (نسفًا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

muyesser-irab:98-98.t:
﴿إنما إلهكم الله الذي﴾: (إنما) is the restraining (kāffa) and restrained (makfūfa) particle; (إلهكم) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (الله) is its khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; and (الذي) is a naʿt (adjective).
﴿لا﴾: the lā of generic negation.
﴿إله﴾: its noun (ism), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa in the position of the accusative.
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr).
﴿هو﴾: a badal (substitute) from the position of (لا) and its noun, because their position is nominative as a mubtadaʾ; or a badal from the pronoun latent in the omitted khabar. The clause (لا إله إلا هو) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (الذي), with no grammatical position.
﴿وسع كل شيء علما﴾: (وسع) is a past verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو); (كل شيء) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) [Translator's note: so in the source; (كل) is in fact the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of (وسع), and (شيء) is the muḍāf ilayhi]; and (علمًا) is a tamyīz (specification) converted from the fāʿil of (وسع).

muyesser-irab:99-99.t: ﴿كذلك نقص عليك من أنباء ما قد سبق وقد آتيناك من لدنا ذكرا﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning "like", indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun) of ﴿نقص﴾, i.e.: "We relate to you a relating like that relating"; ﴿ذلك﴾: ﴿ذا﴾ is a demonstrative in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the lām is for distance, and the kāf is a particle of address; (نقص) is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "we" (نحن); ﴿عليك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نقص﴾; (من أنباء) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of (نقص); (ما) is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause ﴿قد سبق﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position; ﴿وقد﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and (قد) is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); ﴿آتيناك﴾ is a past verb, ﴿نا﴾ being the fāʿil and the kāf a mafʿūl bihi; ﴿من لدنا﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was an adjective of ﴿ذكرًا﴾; and (ذكرًا) is the second mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:100-100.t: ﴿من أعرض عنه فإنه يحمل يوم القيامة وزرا﴾: (من) is conditional, in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); (أعرض) is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "he" (هو); (عنه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أعرض﴾; the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa); (إن) is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle, the hāʾ is its noun (ism), and the clause (يحمل) is its khabar (predicate), the fāʿil being latent, its implied form being "he" (هو); (يوم القيامة) is an adverb attached to ﴿يحمل﴾; (وزرًا) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause (من أعرض) is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿ذكرًا﴾.

muyesser-irab:101-101.t: ﴿خالدين فيه وساء لهم يوم القيامة حملا﴾: (خالدين) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); (فيه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (خالدين), and the pronoun refers back to the burden (الوزر); (وساء): the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) or a conjunction, and (ساء) is a past verb, one of the verbs of blame, its fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir) and specified by an indefinite, namely ﴿حملًا﴾, while the one specifically blamed (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being "their burden"; ﴿لهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an implied verb of saying, i.e.: "these words are said to them"; it is also said: it is like the lām in ﴿هيت لك﴾, i.e. for mere clarification; (يوم القيامة) is an adverb attached to ﴿ساء﴾; and (حملًا) is a tamyīz (specification).

muyesser-irab:102-102.t: ﴿يوم ينفخ في الصور ونحشر المجرمين يومئذ زرقا﴾: ﴿يوم﴾ is an adverb, a badal (substitute) from (يوم القيامة); the clause (ينفخ) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (ينفخ) is an imperfect verb in the passive (built for that whose agent is not named); ﴿في الصور﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ينفخ﴾; ﴿نحشر﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and ﴿نحشر﴾ is an imperfect verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "we" (نحن); (المجرمين) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿يومئذ﴾: (يوم) is an adverb attached to ﴿نحشر﴾, and (إذٍ) is a noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on a sukūn implied (muqaddar) because the slot is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, the tanwīn compensating for an omitted clause, the implied sense being: "and We gather the criminals on the day when the trumpet is blown"; and (زرقًا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (المجرمين).

muyesser-irab:103-103.t: ﴿يتخافتون بينهم إن لبثتم إلا عشرا﴾: the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (المجرمين), or resumptive with no grammatical position; (يتخافتون) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, because it is one of the five verbs, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (بينهم) is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يتخافتون﴾; (إن لبثتم) is a clause in the accusative by a verb of saying indicated by (يتخافتون), the saying being accusative as a ḥāl, i.e.: "saying in secret"; (إن) is negating; (لبثتم) is a verb and its fāʿil; (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); and (عشرًا) is an adverb of time.

muyesser-irab:104-104.t: ﴿نحن أعلم بما يقولون إذ يقول أمثلهم طريقة إن لبثتم إلا يوما﴾: (نحن) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (أعلم) is the khabar (predicate); (بما) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أعلم); the clause (يقولون) is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position; (إذ) is an adverb attached to ﴿أعلم﴾; the clause ﴿يقول﴾ is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (أمثلهم) is the fāʿil (agent); (طريقة) is a tamyīz (specification); (إن) is negating; (لبثتم) is a verb and its fāʿil; (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); and (يومًا) is an adverb attached to ﴿لبثتم﴾.

muyesser-irab:105-105.t: ﴿ويسألونك عن الجبال فقل ينسفها ربي نسفا﴾: the wāw is for resumption; (يسألونك) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, the wāw being the fāʿil (agent) and the kāf a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿عن الجبال﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يسألونك﴾; the clause ﴿ويسألونك عن الجبال﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿فقل﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and (قل) is an imperative verb, and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you" (أنت); the clause (ينسفها) is the content of the speech (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿ها﴾ is a fronted mafʿūl bihi; (ربي) is a postponed fāʿil; and (نسفًا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

muyesser-irab:106-106.t: ﴿فيذرها قاعا صفصفا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; (يذرها) is an imperfect verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو), i.e. Allah the Exalted; ﴿ها﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (قاعًا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the accusative pronoun, or a second mafʿūl bihi, because (يذر) is made to include the meaning of "turning into" (al-taṣyīr); and (صفصفًا) is a second ḥāl, or a badal (substitute) from the second object; it is also said: it is a naʿt (adjective) of it.

muyesser-irab:107-107.t: ﴿لا ترى فيها عوجا ولا أمتا﴾: the clause is a third ḥāl (circumstantial), or a first ḥāl; (لا) is negating; (ترى) is an imperfect verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you" (أنت); (فيها) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ترى﴾; (عوجًا) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and (ولا أمتًا) is conjoined.

muyesser-irab:108-108.t:
﴿يومئذ يتبعون الداعي لا عوج له﴾: ﴿يومئذ﴾: (يوم) is an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يتبعون﴾, or a badal (substitute) from the earlier ﴿يوم القيامة﴾; (إذٍ) is a noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on a sukūn implied (muqaddar) because the slot is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the tanwīn compensating for an omitted clause; ﴿يتبعون الداعي﴾ is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (لا) is the lā of generic negation; (عوج) is its noun (ism), indeclinable on the fatḥa; ﴿له﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of (لا); and the clause ﴿لا عوج له﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (الداعي), or an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e.: "they follow him with a following that has no crookedness", or resumptive with no grammatical position.
﴿وخشعت الأصوات للرحمن فلا تسمع إلا همسا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (خشعت الأصوات) is a verb and its fāʿil; ﴿للرحمن﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿خشعت﴾; the fāʾ is a conjunction; (لا) is negating; (تسمع) is an imperfect verb, and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو) [Translator's note: so in the source; with the second-person (تسمع) one would expect "you" (أنت)]; (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); and (همسًا) is a mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:109-109.t: ﴿يومئذ لا تنفع الشفاعة إلا من أذن له الرحمن ورضي له قولا﴾: ﴿يومئذ﴾: (يوم) is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the negated verb ﴿تنفع﴾; (إذٍ) is a noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on a sukūn implied (muqaddar) because the slot is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the tanwīn compensating for an omitted clause; (لا) is negating; (تنفع الشفاعة) is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (من) is the object of ﴿تنفع﴾; the clause ﴿أذن له الرحمن﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿من﴾, with no grammatical position; ﴿رضي له قولًا﴾ is conjoined to (أذن له); and it is also said: the accusative is as an object.

muyesser-irab:110-110.t: ﴿يعلم ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم ولا يحيطون به علما﴾: (يعلم) is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو); (ما) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (بين) is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted [word] that is the ṣila of the relative, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position; (أيديهم) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause ﴿يعلم ما...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿ما خلفهم﴾ is conjoined to ﴿ما بين أيديهم﴾; (ولا يحيطون): the wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and (يحيطون) is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; ﴿به﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿يحيطون﴾; and (علمًا) is a mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:111-111.t: ﴿وعنت الوجوه للحي القيوم وقد خاب من حمل ظلما﴾: the wāw is resumptive; (عنت الوجوه) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿وعنت الوجوه﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position; (للحي) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿عنت﴾; (القيوم) is a naʿt (adjective); the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and the clause (وقد خاب) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause; (من) is the fāʿil of (خاب); and the clause (حمل ظلمًا) is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿من﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:112-112.t: ﴿ومن يعمل من الصالحات وهو مؤمن فلا يخاف ظلما ولا هضما﴾: the wāw conjoins to (وقد خاب); (من) is conditional, a mubtadaʾ (subject); (يعمل) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (من الصالحات) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of an omitted mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e.: "deeds"; the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ﴿هو﴾ is a mubtadaʾ, and (مؤمن) is the khabar (predicate); the fāʾ connects (rābiṭa) the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (لا) is negating; (يخاف) is an imperfect verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو); (ظلمًا) is a mafʿūl bihi; (ولا هضمًا) is conjoined to ﴿ظلمًا﴾; the clause (لا يخاف) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, the implied sense being: "then he does not fear"; the clause (فهو لا يخاف) is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis; and the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of (من).

muyesser-irab:113-113.t:
﴿وكذلك أنزلناه قرآنا عربيا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿كذلك﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning "like", indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun) of ﴿أنزلناه﴾, i.e.: "with the like of that sending-down We sent it down"; ﴿ذلك﴾: ﴿ذا﴾ is a demonstrative in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the lām is for distance, and the kāf is a particle of address; ﴿أنزلناه﴾ is a past verb, ﴿نا﴾ being the fāʿil (agent) and the hāʾ a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿قرآنًا﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial); and ﴿عربيًّا﴾ is a naʿt (adjective).
﴿وصرفنا فيه من الوعيد لعلهم يتقون أو يحدث لهم ذكرا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿صرفنا﴾ is a verb and its fāʿil; ﴿فيه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿صرفنا﴾; ﴿من الوعيد﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt of an omitted object, i.e.: "We varied a threat from among the threats"; (لعل) is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle expressing hope, ﴿هم﴾ is its noun (ism), and the clause (يتقون) is its khabar (predicate); (أو) is a conjunction; (يحدث) is conjoined to (يتقون); ﴿لهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿يحدث﴾; (ذكرًا) is a mafʿūl bihi; and the fāʿil of (يحدث) is "it", i.e. the Quran.

muyesser-irab:114-114.t: ﴿فتعالى الله الملك الحق ولا تعجل بالقرآن من قبل أن يقضى إليك وحيه وقل رب زدني علما﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive; ﴿تعالى الله﴾ is a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿الملك الحق﴾ are two adjectives of (الله); the clause ﴿فتعالى الله﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position; (ولا تعجل): the wāw is a conjunction, (لا) is prohibitive, and (تعجل) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive (لا); (بالقرآن) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تعجل﴾; ﴿من قبل﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿تعجل﴾; the interpreted maṣdar from ﴿أن يقضى﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿إليك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿يقضى﴾; (يقضى) is an imperfect verb in the passive (built for that whose agent is not named), and (وحيه) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (قل) is conjoined to (لا تعجل); (رب) is a vocative (munādā) annexed to the omitted yāʾ of the first person; (زدني) is a verb of supplication, the nūn being for protection (al-wiqāya) and the yāʾ the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and (علمًا) is the second mafʿūl bihi, or a tamyīz (specification).

muyesser-irab:115-115.t: ﴿ولقد عهدنا إلى آدم من قبل فنسي ولم نجد له عزما﴾: the wāw is resumptive; the lām is the answer to the omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); (عهدنا) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (إلى آدم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿عهدنا﴾; (من قبل) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause ﴿ولقد عهدنا...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position; (فنسي) is conjoined to (عهد), i.e.: "he forgot what We had commanded him"; (ولم نجد): the wāw is a conjunction, (لم) is a particle of negation, inversion [of tense] and jussive, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "we" (نحن); and (عزمًا) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

muyesser-irab:116-116.t: ﴿وإذ قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم فسجدوا إلا إبليس أبى﴾: the wāw is resumptive; ﴿إذ﴾ is a noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, the implied sense being: "and remember when We said"; (قلنا) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause ﴿قلنا﴾ is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); (للملائكة) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قلنا﴾; (اسجدوا) is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil, the verbal clause being in the position of the accusative as the content of the speech (maqūl al-qawl); (لآدم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿اسجدوا﴾; (فسجدوا): the fāʾ is a conjunction, and (سجدوا) is a verb and its fāʿil; ﴿إلا﴾ is a particle of exception; (إبليس) is the excepted by ﴿إلا﴾, in a connected [exception] (muttaṣil) if Iblīs was originally one of the angels, and it is also said: disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), because he is not one of them; and (أبى) is a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif, the verbal clause being in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e.: "while he was rejecting the command, being arrogant towards it and disbelieving in it".

muyesser-irab:117-117.t:
﴿فقلنا يا آدم إن هذا عدو لك ولزوجك﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; (قلنا) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (يا آدم) is a vocative; the clause (إن) is the content of the speech (maqūl al-qawl); (هذا) is the noun of inna, and (عدو) is its khabar (predicate); ﴿لك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (عدو); and (ولزوجك) is conjoined to (لك).
﴿فلا يخرجنكما من الجنة فتشقى﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; (لا) is prohibitive; (يخرجنكما) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the jussive by (لا); the kāf is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and it is Iblīs; the mīm and the alif are for the dual; (فتشقى): the fāʾ is the fāʾ of causation (al-sababiyya), and (تشقى) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) an after the fāʾ of causation, the fāʿil being latent, its implied form being "you" (أنت); the interpreted maṣdar from an and the verb is conjoined to a maṣdar extracted from the preceding speech, i.e.: "let there be no expulsion of you two from it, and so a misery for you".
.

muyesser-irab:118-118.t: ﴿إن لك ألا تجوع فيها ولا تعرى﴾: (إن) is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle; ﴿لك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate) of inna; (أن) together with what falls within its scope is its postponed noun (ism); (فيها) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿تجوع﴾; and (ولا تعرى) is conjoined to ﴿لا تجوع﴾.

muyesser-irab:119-119.t: ﴿وأنك لا تظمأ فيها ولا تضحى﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (أن) is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle, the kāf is its noun (ism), and the clause ﴿لا تظمأ فيها﴾ is its khabar (predicate); ﴿لا﴾ is negating; (تظمأ) is an imperfect verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); (فيها) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); and ﴿ولا تضحى﴾ is conjoined to ﴿لا تظمأ﴾.

muyesser-irab:120-120.t: ﴿فوسوس إليه الشيطان قال يا آدم هل أدلك على شجرة الخلد وملك لا يبلى﴾: (فوسوس): the fāʾ is a conjunction, and ﴿وسوس﴾ is a past verb; (إليه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿وسوس﴾; (الشيطان) is the fāʿil (agent); ﴿قال يا آدم﴾ is a past verb and a vocative construction; (هل) is a particle of interrogation; (أدلك) is an imperfect verb, and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "I" (أنا), and the kāf is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿على شجرة الخلد﴾: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿أدلك﴾; (ملك) is conjoined to (شجرة); and the clause (لا يبلى) is a naʿt (adjective) of (ملك).

muyesser-irab:121-121.t: ﴿فأكلا منها فبدت لهما سوآتهما وطفقا يخصفان عليهما من ورق الجنة وعصى آدم ربه فغوى﴾: (فأكلا) is a past verb, and the alif is the fāʿil (agent); (منها) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أكلا﴾; (فبدت) is conjoined to (أكلا); ﴿لهما﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿بدت﴾; (سوءاتهما) is the fāʿil; (طفقا) is a past verb, one of the verbs of commencement (afʿāl al-shurūʿ), the alif being its noun (ism) and the clause (يخصفان) its khabar (predicate); ﴿عليهما﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿يخصفان﴾; and (من ورق الجنة) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of an omitted described noun, which is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e.: "leaves from the leaves of the Garden". ﴿وعصى آدم ربه﴾ is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; and (فغوى) is conjoined to (عصى).

muyesser-irab:122-122.t: ﴿ثم اجتباه ربه فتاب عليه وهدى﴾: (ثم) is a conjunction; (اجتباه) is a verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (ربه) is the fāʿil (agent); (فتاب عليه) is conjoined to (اجتباه); and (هدى) is conjoined to (تاب).

muyesser-irab:123-123.t:
﴿قال اهبطا منها جميعا بعضكم لبعض عدو﴾: (اهبطا) is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the alif is the fāʿil (agent); (منها) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿اهبطا﴾; (جميعًا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); (بعضكم) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (لبعض) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was an adjective of (عدو); (عدو) is the khabar (predicate); and the clause ﴿بعضكم لبعض عدو﴾ is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl.
﴿فإما يأتينكم مني هدى فمن اتبع هداي فلا يضل ولا يشقى﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; (إن) is conditional, and (ما) is a connective (ṣila) particle; (يأتينكم) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the kāf is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (مني) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿يأتينكم﴾; (هدى) is the fāʿil of (يأتينكم); (فمن اتبع): the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), (من) is conditional, a mubtadaʾ, and (اتبع) is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis; (هداي) is a mafʿūl bihi; the fāʾ connects the apodosis (jawāb); the clause ﴿لا يضل﴾ is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of (من); and the clause ﴿من اتبع﴾ is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis of (إن).

muyesser-irab:124-124.t:
﴿ومن أعرض عن ذكري فإن له معيشة ضنكا﴾: the wāw conjoins to the preceding apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); ﴿مَن﴾ is a conditional noun that makes [the verb] jussive, a mubtadaʾ (subject); (أعرض) is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "he" (هو); (عن ذكري) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أعرض﴾; (فإن): the fāʾ connects (rābiṭa) the apodosis, because it is a nominal clause; (إن) is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle; ﴿له﴾ is its fronted khabar (predicate); (معيشة) is its postponed noun (ism); (ضنكًا) is a naʿt (adjective); the nominal clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis; and the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of (من).
﴿ونحشره يوم القيامة أعمى﴾: ﴿ونحشره﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, with no grammatical position; (نحشر) is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the fāʿil being latent, its implied form being "we" (نحن), and the hāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (يوم القيامة) is an adverb attached to ﴿نحشره﴾; and (أعمى) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in (نحشره).

muyesser-irab:125-125.t: ﴿قال رب لم حشرتني أعمى وقد كنت بصيرا﴾: (رب) is a vocative (munādā) annexed to the omitted yāʾ of the first person; ﴿لِمَ﴾: the lām is a preposition, and the interrogative (ما) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿حشرتني﴾; (حشرتني) is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (أعمى) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); the wāw is circumstantial; (قد) is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); (كان) is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, the tāʾ being its noun (ism); and (بصيرًا) is the khabar (predicate) of kāna.

muyesser-irab:126-126.t: ﴿قال كذلك أتتك آياتنا فنسيتها وكذلك اليوم تنسى﴾: (قال) is a past verb; ﴿كذلك﴾: the kāf [Translator's note: the source repeats «الكاف» here] is a noun meaning "like", indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e.: "they came to you with a coming like that coming", or in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: "the matter is thus"; ﴿ذلك﴾: ﴿ذا﴾ is a demonstrative in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the lām is for distance, and the kāf is a particle of address; ﴿أتتك آياتنا﴾ is a verb, a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and a postponed fāʿil (agent); (فنسيتها): the fāʾ is a conjunction, and ﴿نسيتها﴾ is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; ﴿كذلك﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning "like", indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar; ﴿ذلك﴾: ﴿ذا﴾ is a demonstrative in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, the lām is for distance, and the kāf is a particle of address; and (اليوم) is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تنسى﴾.

muyesser-irab:127-127.t: ﴿وكذلك نجزي من أسرف ولم يؤمن بآيات ربه ولعذاب الآخرة أشد وأبقى﴾: ﴿كذلك﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning "like", indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), the implied sense being: "with a recompense like that We recompense"; (ذلك): ﴿ذا﴾ is a demonstrative in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the lām is for distance, and the kāf is a particle of address; ﴿نجزي﴾ is an imperfect verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "we" (نحن); ﴿من﴾ is a relative noun, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿أسرف﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿من﴾, with no grammatical position; ﴿ولم يؤمن﴾ is conjoined to (أسرف), so it falls within the scope of the ṣila; ﴿بآيات﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يؤمن﴾; ﴿ربه﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿ولعذاب﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) or a conjunction, the lām is for inception (al-ibtidāʾ), and (عذاب) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿الآخرة﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿أشد﴾ is the khabar (predicate); and ﴿وأبقى﴾ is conjoined to (أشد).

muyesser-irab:128-128.t:
﴿أفلم يهد لهم كم أهلكنا قبلهم من القرون يمشون في مساكنهم﴾: the hamza is for interrogation, and it introduces something omitted to which [the clause] is conjoined by the fāʾ, the implied sense being: "were they heedless, so that it did not become clear to them?"; the fāʿil (agent) of (يهد) is the maṣdar understood from (أهلكنا), i.e.: "has Our destroying not become clear to them?", or a pronoun referring back to Allah the Exalted, i.e.: "has Allah not made clear"; ﴿لهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يهد﴾; (كم) is the predicative (khabariyya) kam, an object placed before (أهلكنا); (من القرون) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of the tamyīz (specification) of the predicative kam, i.e.: "how many a generation from among the generations"; the clause (يمشون في مساكنهم) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object of (أهلكنا), or from the pronoun in (لهم); (في مساكنهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿يمشون﴾; and the pronoun refers back to those destroyed.
﴿إن في ذلك لآيات لأولي النهى﴾: (إن) and its fronted khabar (predicate); the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (آيات) is its postponed noun (ism); (لأولي) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt of (آيات); and (النهى) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

muyesser-irab:129-129.t: ﴿ولولا كلمة سبقت من ربك لكان لزاما وأجل مسمى﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, with no grammatical position; (لولا) is a particle of non-occurrence due to occurrence (imtināʿ li-wujūd); (كلمة) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted; the clause ﴿سبقت من ربك﴾ is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿كلمة﴾; (من ربك) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿سبقت﴾; ﴿لكان﴾: the lām occurs in the answer to (لولا), and (كان) is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, its noun (ism) being a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "it" (هو), referring back to the destruction; (لزامًا) is its khabar; and (أجل مسمى) is conjoined to (كلمة), or to the latent pronoun in ﴿كان﴾, i.e.: "the immediate destruction and an appointed term would have been binding on them, as they were binding on ʿĀd and Thamūd".

muyesser-irab:130-130.t: ﴿فاصبر على ما يقولون وسبح بحمد ربك قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل غروبها﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an omitted condition); (اصبر) is an imperative verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you" (أنت); ﴿على ما﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿اصبر﴾; the clause (يقولون) is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position; (سبح) is conjoined to (اصبر); (بحمد ربك) is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e.: "while you are praising your Lord for having enabled you to glorify Him and having helped you in it"; (قبل) is an adverb attached to (سبح); (طلوع الشمس) is muḍāf [Translator's note: so in the source («مضاف»); (طلوع) is the muḍāf ilayhi of (قبل) and is itself annexed to (الشمس)]; and (وقبل غروبها) is conjoined to (قبل طلوع الشمس).

muyesser-irab:131-131.t:
﴿ولا تمدن عينيك إلى ما متعنا به أزواجا منهم زهرة الحياة الدنيا لنفتنهم فيه﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (لا) is prohibitive; (تمدن) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is joined to the nūn of emphasis, and it is in the position of the jussive by ﴿لا﴾, its fāʿil (agent) being a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "you" (أنت); (عينيك) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (إلى ما) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تمدن﴾; the clause (متعنا) is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position; ﴿به﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿متعنا﴾, and the hāʾ is the referring pronoun (al-ʿāʾid); (أزواجًا) is the object of (متعنا); (منهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective), or it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun hāʾ; (منهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿متعنا﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source, which gives (منهم) a second, alternative attachment here]; and ﴿زهرة الحياة الدنيا﴾ has several views:
1 - a second object, if we parse ﴿أزواجًا﴾ as the first object, because the meaning of ﴿متعنا﴾ is "We gave".
2 - accusative as a ḥāl from the relative ﴿ما﴾.
3 - accusative as a badal (substitute) from ﴿أزواجًا﴾, by way of hyperbole.
4 - accusative by an implied verb indicated by ﴿متعنا﴾, its implied form being: "We made for them an adornment".
5 - accusative on account of blame (al-dhamm), i.e.: "I blame the adornment of the life of this world".
6 - accusative on account of specialisation (al-ikhtiṣāṣ).
7 - accusative as a badal from the position of ﴿به﴾.
8 - accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun in ﴿به﴾.
9 - accusative as a tamyīz (specification) of ﴿ما﴾ or of the hāʾ in ﴿به﴾.
﴿لنفتنهم﴾: the lām is for causation (taʿlīl), and (نفتنهم) is an imperfect [verb], accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) an after the lām of causation; the interpreted maṣdar from an and the verb is genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿متعنا﴾; the hāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi; and (فيه) is attached to ﴿نفتنهم﴾.
﴿ورزق ربك خير وأبقى﴾: the wāw is circumstantial; (رزق) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿ربك﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿خير﴾ is the khabar (predicate); and (أبقى) is conjoined to (خير).

muyesser-irab:132-132.t:
﴿وأمر أهلك بالصلاة واصطبر عليها لا نسألك رزقا﴾: the wāw is resumptive or a conjunction; the imperative verb is indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you" (أنت); (أهلك) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (بالصلاة) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) the imperative verb; the clause ﴿وأمر أهلك بالصلاة﴾ is conjoined, or resumptive with no grammatical position; (اصطبر) is an imperative verb, and its fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "you" (أنت); (عليها) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿اصطبر﴾; the clause (لا نسألك) is resumptive; (نسألك) is an imperfect verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; and (رزقًا) is a second mafʿūl bihi.
﴿نحن نرزقك والعاقبة للتقوى﴾: (نحن) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause (نرزقك) is the khabar (predicate); (العاقبة) is a mubtadaʾ, and (للتقوى) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar; and these two clauses are also resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:133-133.t: ﴿وقالوا لولا يأتينا بآية من ربه أولم تأتهم بينة ما في الصحف الأولى﴾: (لولا) is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ), i.e.: "why not?"; (يأتينا) is a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (بآياته) [Translator's note: so in the source; the Quranic word is (بآية)] is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يأتينا﴾; (من ربه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (آية); (أولم): the hamza is for interrogation, and the wāw conjoins to something implied that the context requires, the implied sense being: "did not clear proofs come to them in succession, and did there not come to them, in particular, the clear proof of what is in the former scriptures?"; (بينة) is the fāʿil of ﴿تأتهم﴾; (ما) is a relative, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (في الصحف) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted [word] that is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position; and (الأولى) is a naʿt of (الصحف).

muyesser-irab:134-134.t:
﴿ولو أنا أهلكناهم بعذاب من قبله لقالوا ربنا لولا أرسلت إلينا رسولا﴾: ﴿لو﴾ is conditional; (أن) is an abrogating (nāsikh), maṣdar-forming particle, and ﴿نا﴾ is a pronoun in the position of the accusative as the noun of anna; (أهلكناهم) is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿أنّا﴾ together with what follows it is the fāʿil of an omitted verb, its implied form being "it were established" (ثبت), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; (بعذاب) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أهلكناهم﴾; (من قبله) is a naʿt (adjective) of (عذاب); (لقالوا) is the answer to (لو), and the clause has no grammatical position; (ربنا) is a vocative (munādā) in a genitive construct, from which the vocative particle is omitted; (لولا) is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ); (أرسلت) is a verb and its fāʿil; (إلينا) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿أرسلت﴾; (رسولًا) is a mafʿūl bihi; and the clause is the content of the speech (maqūl al-qawl).
﴿فنتبع آياتك من قبل أن نذل ونخزى﴾: (فنتبع): the fāʾ is that of causation (al-sababiyya), and (نتبع) is accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) an in answer to the urging; the interpreted maṣdar from an and the verb is conjoined to a maṣdar extracted from the preceding speech, i.e.: "why was there not a sending from You, and so a following from us?". The fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "we" (نحن); (آياتك) is a mafʿūl bihi, accusative with the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural; ﴿من قبل﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿نتبع﴾; (أن) together with what follows it is interpreted as a maṣdar that is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and ﴿نخزى﴾ is conjoined to ﴿نذل﴾.

muyesser-irab:135-135.t: ﴿قل كل متربص فتربصوا فستعلمون من أصحاب الصراط السوي ومن اهتدى﴾: (كل) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (متربص) is the khabar (predicate); the clause is the content of the speech (maqūl al-qawl); the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an omitted condition); (تربصوا) is an imperative verb; (فستعلمون): the fāʾ is resumptive, the sīn is a particle of the future, and (تعلمون) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, the wāw being the fāʿil (agent); ﴿مَن﴾ is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ, and ﴿أصحاب الصراط السوي﴾ is the khabar; the clause ﴿فستعلمون مَن...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿من اهتدى﴾ is conjoined to (من أصحاب); and the clause ﴿من أصحاب﴾ is the object of ﴿تعلمون﴾, which is suspended (muʿallaq) from operating; or ﴿من﴾ is a relative, the object of ﴿تعلمون﴾, and (أصحاب الصراط) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e.: "they are the companions".

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: The reading of the people of Medina and of Abū ʿAmr is without imāla (inclining the vowel toward i), and the reading of the Kufans is with imāla, except ʿĀṣim, from whom there is a disagreement in transmission. Abū Jaʿfar said: According to most of the scholars of Arabic there is no justification for imāla here, for two reasons. One is that there is neither a yāʾ nor a kasra here to bring about imāla. The other reason is that the ṭāʾ is one of the letters that prevent imāla. These are two clear reasons. Some grammarians, however, chose imāla. Abū Isḥāq Ibrāhīm ibn al-Sarī said: One who gives «طه» a kasra inclines it toward kasra, because in the shortened noun (al-maqṣūr) the kasra predominates by way of imāla. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is not a proof; imāla is not permissible in many shortened nouns. But Sībawayh claimed that imāla is permissible in the letters of the alphabet, so one says «با تا ثا», because they are nouns; so a distinction is made between them and particles such as «لا», which is not given imāla because it is a particle. Abū Isḥāq said: For one who reads طه ما أَنْزَلْنا عَلَيْكَ الْقُرْآنَ لِتَشْقى, the original form according to him is «طأ», i.e. "tread the ground with both your feet in prayer"; the hamza was replaced by hāʾ, just as one says «إيّاك» and «هيّاك», and «أرقت الماء» and «هرقت الماء». He said: It may also be on the basis of replacing the hamza, so that the original is «ط» ("tread") — "O you!" — then the hāʾ was brought to clarify the vowel in the pause.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: Some grammarians say this is the lām of negation (lām al-nafy), and some say it is the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd). Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard Abū al-Ḥasan ibn Kaysān say of the like of it: it is the lām of the genitive (lām al-khafḍ), and the meaning according to him is: "We did not send down the Qurʾān to you for distress." «الشقاء» is pronounced long and short, and it has a wāw as its root letter.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: Abū Isḥāq said: It is a badal (substitute) from «يشقى», i.e. "We sent it down only as a reminder." Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a far-fetched interpretation; the closer one is that it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) or as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: تَنْزِيلًا A maṣdar (verbal noun). مِمَّنْ خَلَقَ الْأَرْضَ وَالسَّماواتِ الْعُلى According to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, the like of this cannot come except with alif and lām, and that is the view of the Kufans. He said: It is impossible to say «سقطت له ثنيّتان علييان لا سفليان» ("two upper front teeth fell out, not two lower ones"), because only the definite is intended by it; if you intend the indefinite and the preference of one thing over another, you bring «من» and say «سقطت له ثنية أعلى من كذا» ("a front tooth higher than such-and-such fell out").

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: The accusative is also permissible, as praise. Abū Isḥāq said: The genitive is also permissible, as a badal (substitute) from «من». Saʿīd ibn Masʿada said: The nominative means "He is the Most Merciful." Abū Jaʿfar said: The nominative is also permissible as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and as a badal from the latent pronoun in «خلق».

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: لَهُ ما فِي السَّماواتِ In the position of a nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). وَما بَيْنَهُما وَما تَحْتَ الثَّرى is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: وَإِنْ تَجْهَرْ بِالْقَوْلِ Jussive (majzūm) by the condition, and the apodosis is فَإِنَّهُ يَعْلَمُ السِّرَّ وَأَخْفى, i.e. "and what is more hidden than it."

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: اللَّهُ لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ Nominative as a badal (substitute) from what is in «يعلم» [i.e. its latent pronoun], or with an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), or as a mubtadaʾ. لَهُ الْأَسْماءُ الْحُسْنى Nominative as a mubtadaʾ; الْحُسْنى is its naʿt (adjective).

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: Ḥamza read فَقالَ لِأَهْلِهِ امْكُثُوا [Translator's note: i.e. «لِأَهْلِهُ» with ḍamma on the hāʾ, as the following explanation shows], and likewise in al-Qaṣaṣ. Abū Jaʿfar said: This follows the dialect of those who say «مررت بهو يا هذا»; he brought it in its original form, and it is permissible, except that Ḥamza departed from his own principle in these two places specifically.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: Because the meaning of «نودي» is "it was said to him." Al-Ḥasan, Abū Jaʿfar and Abū ʿAmr read «نودي يا موسى أنّي» with fatḥa on the hamza, meaning "he was called with (بأنّي) …," and «أنّ» is in the position of an accusative. For one who reads with kasra, the meaning according to him is: "He said: Indeed I…."

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: The people of Medina and the people of Basra read «بالواد المقدّس طوى» without tanwīn, and the people of Kufa read طُوىً with tanwīn. Abū Jaʿfar said: The proper way is to omit the tanwīn, because it is like «عمر», shifted from its pattern (maʿdūl) and definite. It may also be the name of the spot (al-buqʿa), so it is likewise a diptote. As for one who gives tanwīn, Abū Isḥāq claimed that he takes it to be the name of the place, not shifted, like «حطم» and «صرد». He said: One who says «طوى» (ṭiwan) and declines it fully makes it like «ضلع» and «معى», as the name of the place; and it may also be a diptote as the name of the spot. Abū Jaʿfar said: One who takes «طوى» in the sense of «ثنى» (twice) gives it tanwīn and nothing else, taking it from «ثنيت الشيء ثنى», i.e. it was sanctified twice. In the ḥadīth: "There is no thinā in charity," i.e. it is not doubled so as to be taken twice.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: The people of Medina, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī read وَأَنَا اخْتَرْتُكَ, and the rest of the Kufans read «وإنّا اخترناك». The meaning is the same, except that «وأنا اخترتك» is preferable here for two reasons. One is that it more closely resembles the written form; the second is that it fits better the sequence of the speech, because of His saying, Mighty and Majestic: يا مُوسى إِنِّي أَنَا رَبُّكَ, and the address proceeded in this sequence.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: وَأَقِمِ الصَّلاةَ لِذِكْرِي Abū Isḥāq said: There are two views on it. The meaning may be: "Establish prayer so that you remember Me in it," because prayer exists only with remembrance. The other view: "Establish prayer whenever you remember it," that being the time of the prayer. Abū Jaʿfar said: There is a third view: the meaning may be "Establish prayer so that I may mention you with praise." Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, Abū Rajāʾ and al-Shaʿbī read أَقِمِ الصَّلاةَ لِذِكْرِي [Translator's note: the vowelling shown is that of the standard text; the following discussion shows the variant ends in alif, i.e. «لِذِكْرَى»]. This reading has two interpretations. One is that this alif is the alif of the feminine. The other is that this alif replaces the yāʾ, as one says «يا غلاما أقبل»; this was done so that the verse-endings agree.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t:
إِنَّ السَّاعَةَ آتِيَةٌ أَكادُ أُخْفِيها A difficult verse. Abū Jaʿfar said: We have mentioned something of what has been said about it. From Saʿīd ibn Jubayr there are two transmissions. One is what al-Ḥasan ibn al-Faraj narrated to us in Gaza; he said: Yūsuf ibn ʿAdī narrated to us; he said: Muḥammad ibn Sahl al-Kūfī narrated to us, from Warqāʾ — he is Ibn Iyās — from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, that he read أَكادُ أُخْفِيها with fatḥa on the hamza [i.e. «أَخْفِيها»]; he said: "I reveal it." This transmission has no route other than this; Abū ʿUbayd transmitted it from al-Kisāʾī, from this Muḥammad ibn Sahl. Better than this chain is what Yaḥyā al-Qaṭṭān transmitted from al-Thawrī, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, that he read أَكادُ أُخْفِيها with ḍamma on the hamza. Abū Jaʿfar said: One says «خفى الشيء يخفيه» when he reveals it; and it has been reported that one says «أخفاه» when he reveals it, but that is not well known. Abū Jaʿfar said: I saw ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān, when the meaning of «أخفيها» was difficult for him, turn to this view, and he said its meaning is like the meaning of «أَخفيها», i.e. "I reveal it." Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning is not "I reveal it," especially since «أَخفيها» is an anomalous (shādhdh) reading; how could we refer the sound, widespread reading to the anomalous one? The meaning of the ḍamma reading is preferable, and the implied form is: "The Hour is coming — I almost bring it"; «آتية» indicates «آتي بها»; then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: أُخْفِيها as a new beginning. This is a sound meaning, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has hidden the Hour, which is the Day of Resurrection, and the hour in which a person dies, so that a person keeps working while the matter remains obscure to him and does not delay repentance. It was also said: the meaning is "I almost hide it," i.e. I come close to that, because when you say «كاد زيد يقوم» ("Zayd almost stood"), it may be that he stood and it may be that he did not; and it was shown that He has hidden it by evidence other than this, on this answer. It was also said: the meaning is "The Hour is coming لِتُجْزى كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِما تَسْعى," and it was said:
the meaning is "Establish prayer for My remembrance, so that every soul may be recompensed for what it strives."

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: فَلا يَصُدَّنَّكَ عَنْها i.e. from belief in it and in what it contains, مَنْ لا يُؤْمِنُ بِها وَاتَّبَعَ هَواهُ i.e. in disbelief in it. فَتَرْدى from «ردي يردى», when one perishes.

nahhas-irab:17-18.t:
وَما تِلْكَ A mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and it carries the sense of drawing attention. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that «تلك» here is an incomplete noun (ism nāqiṣ) whose ṣila (relative clause) is «بيمينك». Abū Jaʿfar said: I saw Abū Isḥāq inclining to this view and holding it; the meaning according to both of them is "And what is that which is in your right hand?" I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: I heard Abū al-ʿAbbās reject this view, saying: It is not permissible for the vague nouns [demonstratives] to take a ṣila. One says:
أَهُشُّ and «أهشّ» [Translator's note: the second form presumably «أَهِشُّ», with kasra; the source does not vowel it].

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: فَأَلْقاها فَإِذا هِيَ حَيَّةٌ A mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). The accusative is also permissible: one says «خرجت فإذا زيد جالس» and «جالسا», as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Abū Jaʿfar said: We have explained it earlier. The pause is «حيه», with hāʾ.

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: سَنُعِيدُها سِيرَتَهَا الْأُولى Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: the implied form is «إلى سيرتها» ("to its state"), like وَاخْتارَ مُوسى قَوْمَهُ [al-Aʿrāf: 155]. He said: It may also be a maṣdar (verbal noun), because the meaning of «سنعيدها» is "We shall make it go (سنسيّرها)."

nahhas-irab:22-22.t:
وَاضْمُمْ يَدَكَ إِلى جَناحِكَ Outside the Qurʾān «ضمّ» is permissible with fatḥa, kasra or ḍamma on the mīm because of the meeting of two vowelless letters. The fatḥa is best because of its lightness; the kasra is according to the base rule; and the ḍamma is by assimilation (itbāʿ). If you bring alif and lām [after it], the kasra is best; if you bring an absent (third-person) pronoun, the ḍamma is more frequent, as is making the doubling overt, because the second letter has become vowelless. «يد» has as its original form «يدي», on the pattern faʿl; this is shown by «أيد», and its diminutive is «يديّة» because it is feminine. تَخْرُجْ بَيْضاءَ Accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). It is a diptote because it contains the two alifs of the feminine, which never leave it, so their being inseparable is like a second cause; therefore it is a diptote even when indefinite. The hāʾ [tāʾ marbūṭa] differs from it, because the hāʾ can be separated from the noun. آيَةً أُخْرى Al-Akhfash said: As a badal (substitute) from «بيضاء». This is a good view, because the meaning in «بيضاء» is "made manifest." Abū Isḥāq said: The meaning is "We have given you another sign," or "We give you a sign," because when He said تَخْرُجْ بَيْضاءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوءٍ it indicated that He had given him another sign. He said:
«آية» in the nominative is also permissible, meaning "this is a sign."

nahhas-irab:24-24.t: i.e. he has transgressed all bounds in disbelief.

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: i.e. widen it and make easy for me the performance of what You have commanded me.

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: He did not say "untie every knot from my tongue"; for that reason Pharaoh said: «ولا يكاد يبين» ("and he can scarcely express himself").

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: Jussive (majzūm) because it is the answer to the request.

nahhas-irab:29-30.t: It may be by way of advancing and postponing (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr), the two being objects (mafʿūlān), with «الأخ» as a naʿt (adjective); the implied form is "and make Hārūn my brother a minister for me." «هارون» may also be a badal (substitute) from «وزير», because the definite may be substituted for the indefinite. The nominative is also permissible.

nahhas-irab:31-32.t: As a supplication. It is transmitted from al-Ḥasan and Ibn Abī Isḥāq that they read اشْدُدْ ] with fatḥa on the hamza, ḍamma on the first dāl and sukūn on the second [i.e. «أَشْدُدْ»], and وَأَشْرِكْهُ with ḍamma on the hamza and sukūn on the kāf [i.e. «وَأُشْرِكْهُ»], making the two verbs in the position of a jussive (jazm) as the answer to his saying «اجعل لي وزيرا من أهلي». [Translator's note: the bracket after «اشدد» is as in the source.] This reading is anomalous (shādhdh) and far-fetched, because the answer to the like of this is jussive only with the sense of condition and requital, so the meaning would be: "If You make for me a minister from my family, I will strengthen my back through him and I will make him share in my affair." His affair is prophethood and the mission, and this was not up to him ﷺ so that he could announce it; rather, he asks Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to make him share with him in prophethood. From Ibn ʿAbbās: «أشدد به أزري» means "strengthen me," and from him also: "my back." Abū Jaʿfar said: It is derived from «الإزار» (the waist-wrap), because it is tightened. The back is also called «أزر» because of the strength in it. «آزره» means "he strengthened him." «وزير» is not from this; it is derived only from «الوزر», which is a mountain [i.e. a refuge].

nahhas-irab:33-35.t: كَيْ نُسَبِّحَكَ كَثِيراً A naʿt (adjective) of a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "much glorification"; it may also be a naʿt of a time. Assimilation (idghām) is good, and likewise وَنَذْكُرَكَ كَثِيراً is assimilated, and likewise إِنَّكَ كُنْتَ بِنا بَصِيراً, because the two letters belong to two words. «بصيرا» means "knowing what is good for us."

nahhas-irab:39-39.t: أَنِ اقْذِفِيهِ فِي التَّابُوتِ فَاقْذِفِيهِ The pronoun refers to the chest. فَلْيُلْقِهِ الْيَمُّ بِالسَّاحِلِ An imperative. Al-Farrāʾ said: It carries the sense of requital (mujāzāt), i.e. "cast him, and the sea will throw him up." Likewise, according to him, is اتَّبِعُوا سَبِيلَنا وَلْنَحْمِلْ خَطاياكُمْ [al-ʿAnkabūt: 12]. وَلِتُصْنَعَ عَلى عَيْنِي i.e. under My knowledge of you. Assimilation (idghām) is permissible but not as good as in the first, because of the remoteness of the guttural letters.

nahhas-irab:40-40.t: ثُمَّ جِئْتَ عَلى قَدَرٍ يا مُوسى At the time when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, willed to send him.

nahhas-irab:41-41.t: i.e. I strengthened you and taught you, so that you may convey My commands and prohibitions to My servants.

nahhas-irab:42-42.t: اذْهَبْ أَنْتَ وَأَخُوكَ Conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the latent pronoun; conjoining to it is good because you have emphasised it [with «أنت»].

nahhas-irab:43-43.t: إِنَّهُ طَغى i.e. he has transgressed all bounds in disbelief.

nahhas-irab:44-44.t: لَعَلَّهُ يَتَذَكَّرُ أَوْ يَخْشى Abū Jaʿfar said: We have mentioned it.

nahhas-irab:45-45.t:
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: «يفرط» means "hasten," and he said: «يطغى» means "transgress." Abū Jaʿfar said: The implied form is:
"We fear that some matter will proceed hastily from him against us," i.e. some matter will rush out. Al-Farrāʾ said: One says «فرط منه أمر» (a matter came hastily from him). He said: «أفرط» means "went to excess," and he said: «فرّط» means "neglected." Abū Isḥāq said: Its root, in all of it, is from going ahead (al-taqdīm).

nahhas-irab:46-46.t: إِنَّنِي مَعَكُما أَسْمَعُ وَأَرى i.e. I hear his speech and see his action, and I will not leave him free to deal with you.

nahhas-irab:47-47.t: وَالسَّلامُ عَلى مَنِ اتَّبَعَ الْهُدى Abū Isḥāq said: i.e. whoever follows guidance is safe from the wrath of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and His punishment. He said: It is not a greeting; and the proof of that is that it is not the beginning of an encounter nor of an address. Zāʾida transmitted from al-Aʿmash that he read الَّذِي أَعْطى كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلْقَهُ with fatḥa on the lām [i.e. «خَلَقَهُ», as a verb]. [Translator's note: this phrase is from verse 50.]

nahhas-irab:51-52.t:
قالَ فَما بالُ الْقُرُونِ الْأُولى He said: How will they be brought to life and requited? — i.e. this is far-fetched. So Mūsā ﷺ answered him that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows them. قالَ عِلْمُها عِنْدَ رَبِّي فِي كِتابٍ There are two views on its meaning:
One is that it is a figurative representation (tamthīl majāz); the other is that it is literal, and that this is written and the angels read it and draw from it evidence of the power of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and His greatness. لا يَضِلُّ رَبِّي وَلا يَنْسى There are three views on its meaning:
Abū Isḥāq mentioned one of them, that it is a naʿt (adjective) of «كتاب», i.e. "my Lord does not lose it nor forget it." The second view is that the sentence is complete, then He began anew and said: "My Lord does not go astray," i.e. does not perish, from His saying «أإذا ضللنا في الأرض» ("When we are lost in the earth…"), "and does not forget anything." The third view, the closest to the meaning: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed that He has no need of a book; so the meaning is that knowledge of nothing at all escapes Him, nor awareness of it, and He does not forget His knowledge of it. Al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, ʿĪsā and ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read فِي كِتابٍ لا يَضِلُّ رَبِّي [Translator's note: i.e. «لا يُضِلُّ», with ḍamma on the yāʾ, as the gloss shows], i.e. "my Lord does not let it be lost nor forget it."

nahhas-irab:53-53.t: الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الْأَرْضَ مَهْداً The Kufans read مَهْداً [Translator's note: the others read «مهادا»], and «مهادا» is preferable here, because «مهدا» is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and this is not a place for a maṣdar except by omission, i.e. "possessing a cradle." وَسَلَكَ لَكُمْ فِيها سُبُلًا Figurative, i.e. He made paths for you in it. وَأَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً i.e. from its regions.

nahhas-irab:55-55.t: مِنْها خَلَقْناكُمْ i.e. from the earth. Abū Isḥāq said: Because Ādam ﷺ was created from the earth. Someone other than Abū Isḥāq said: the sperm-drop is created from dust; the apparent sense of the Qurʾān indicates this.

nahhas-irab:56-56.t: وَلَقَدْ أَرَيْناهُ آياتِنا كُلَّها The meaning is: "We showed Pharaoh all Our signs which We gave to Mūsā ﷺ." The benefit in this is that Pharaoh saw all the signs with his own eyes, not by report. فَكَذَّبَ وَأَبى to believe.

nahhas-irab:58-58.t:
فَاجْعَلْ بَيْنَنا وَبَيْنَكَ مَوْعِداً لا نُخْلِفُهُ نَحْنُ وَلا أَنْتَ مَكاناً سُوىً.
The Kufans read سُوىً with ḍamma on the sīn; the kasra is better known and more familiar. It was said: its meaning is "other than that place." The people of tafsīr hold that the meaning of «سوى» is "halfway and fair," and this is a good view. Its root is from your saying «جلس في سواء الدار», i.e. in its middle, and «في سواها». The middle of everything is its fairest part. In the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ on وَكَذلِكَ جَعَلْناكُمْ أُمَّةً وَسَطاً [al-Baqara: 143]: i.e. just. Zuhayr said: [al-Wāfir] 290-
أرونا خطّة لا ضيم فيها ... يسوّى بيننا فيها السّواء
(Show us a course with no injustice in it, in which fairness is made equal between us.)

nahhas-irab:59-59.t: قالَ مَوْعِدُكُمْ يَوْمُ الزِّينَةِ A mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). Abū Isḥāq said: The meaning is "the time of your appointment is the Day of Adornment." Al-Ḥasan read مَوْعِدُكُمْ يَوْمُ الزِّينَةِ as an adverb (ẓarf) [Translator's note: i.e. «يَوْمَ» in the accusative; the source shows the standard vowelling]. Abū Isḥāq said: i.e. it occurs on the Day of Adornment. وَأَنْ يُحْشَرَ النَّاسُ ضُحًى «أن» is in the position of a nominative — meaning, according to the reading of one who reads «يوم الزينة» as an adverb, while وَأَنْ يُحْشَرَ النَّاسُ has the sense of a maṣdar (verbal noun), so one of them cannot be conjoined to the other except by an omission, meaning "and the day on which the people are gathered." Better than this is that «أن» be in the position of a genitive, conjoined to «الزينة». «الضحى» is feminine; the Arabs form its diminutive without hāʾ, so that its diminutive will not resemble the diminutive of «ضحوة».

nahhas-irab:61-61.t:
قالَ لَهُمْ مُوسى وَيْلَكُمْ In the sense of a maṣdar (verbal noun). Abū Isḥāq said: i.e. may Allah, Mighty and Majestic, attach woe to them. He said: It may also be a muḍāf (genitive construct) in the vocative. فَيُسْحِتَكُمْ بِعَذابٍ The answer to the prohibition. The Kufans read فَيُسْحِتَكُمْ [Translator's note: the source shows a single vowelling; the two readings are «فَيَسْحَتَكُمْ» and «فَيُسْحِتَكُمْ»]. The first is the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz and this one the dialect of Banū Tamīm. Al-Farazdaq said: [al-Ṭawīl] 291-
وعضّ زمان يا ابن مروان لم يدع ... من المال إلّا مسحتا أو مجلّف
(And the bite of a time, O son of Marwān, that left of wealth nothing but what was destroyed or stripped bare.)
The meaning of لا تَفْتَرُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِباً is: "Do not say that the proofs I bring are sorcery." وَقَدْ خابَ مَنِ افْتَرى i.e. he has been disappointed of mercy and reward.

nahhas-irab:62-63.t:
قالُوا إِنْ هذانِ لَساحِرانِ There are six readings of it. The Medinans and the Kufans read «إنّ هذان لساحران»; Abū ʿAmr read «إنّ هذين لساحران», and this reading is transmitted from al-Ḥasan, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī, ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī. Al-Zuhrī, Ismāʿīl ibn Qusṭanṭīn, al-Khalīl ibn Aḥmad and ʿĀṣim, in one of the two transmissions, read إِنْ هذانِ لَساحِرانِ with «إن» lightened.
These are three readings which the community transmitted from the leading authorities. It is transmitted from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: «إن هذان إلّا ساحران». Al-Kisāʾī said: In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is «إن هذان ساحران» without lām. Al-Farrāʾ said: In the codex (ḥarf) of Ubayy it is «إن ذان إلّا ساحران». These are three further readings, to be taken as explanation (tafsīr); except that it is permissible to recite with them [Translator's note: so in the source, «إلا أنها جائز أن يقرأ بها لمخالفتها المصحف», "except that it is permissible to recite with them because they contradict the muṣḥaf"; the sense required is evidently "not permissible," and a negation has probably dropped out] because they contradict the muṣḥaf. Abū Jaʿfar said: On the first reading the scholars have six views. Among them is that «إنّ» means "yes" (naʿam), as al-Kisāʾī reported from ʿĀṣim; he said: The Arabs
use «إنّ» in the sense of "yes." Sībawayh reported that «إنّ» comes in the sense of «أجل» ("yes, indeed"). Muḥammad ibn Yazīd and Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq used to hold this view. Abū Jaʿfar said: I saw Abū Isḥāq and Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān holding it. ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān narrated to us; he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Salām al-Naysābūrī narrated to us — then I met this ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad and he narrated to me; he said: ʿUmayr ibn al-Mutawakkil narrated to us; he said: Muḥammad ibn Mūsā al-Nawfalī, of the descendants of al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, narrated to us; he said: ʿAmr ibn Jumayʿ al-Kūfī narrated to us, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from ʿAlī — that is, ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn — from his father, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him. He said: I cannot count how many times I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say on his pulpit: "إنّ الحمد لله, we praise Him and seek His help," then he would say: "I am the most eloquent of all Quraysh, and the most eloquent of them after me is Abān ibn Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ." ] [Translator's note: the bracket is as in the source.] Abū Muḥammad said: ʿUmayr said: Its i'rab according to the scholars of Arabic grammar is «إنّ الحمدَ لله» in the accusative, except that the Arabs put «إنّ» in the sense of "yes," as if he meant: "Yes, praise belongs to Allah." That is because the orators of the Jāhiliyya used to open their speeches with «نعم» ("yes"). The poet said, in the sense of "yes": [al-Kāmil] 292-
قالوا: غدرت فقلت إنّ وربّما ... نال العلى وشفى الغليل الغادر
(They said: "You have betrayed." I said: "Yes — and often the betrayer attains the heights and slakes his thirst for vengeance.")
And Ibn Qays al-Ruqayyāt said: [Majzūʾ al-Kāmil] 293-
بكر العواذل في الصّبوح ... يلمنني وألومهنّه
ويقلن شيب قد علاك ... وقد كبرت، فقلت: إنّه
(The censuring women came early at the morning draught, blaming me while I blamed them; they say: "Grey hair has come over you and you have grown old." I said: "Yes, it is so.")
On this basis it is permissible that the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, إِنْ هذانِ لَساحِرانِ be in the sense of "yes."
Abū Jaʿfar said: Dāwūd ibn al-Haytham recited to me; he said: Thaʿlab recited to me: [al-Khafīf] 294-
ليت شعري هل للمحبّ شفاء ... من جوى حبّهنّ إنّ اللّقاء
(Would that I knew: is there a cure for the lover from the burning of his love for them? Yes — the meeting.)
i.e. "yes." This is one view. Abū Zayd, al-Kisāʾī, al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ said: This is according to the dialect of Banū al-Ḥārith ibn Kaʿb. Al-Farrāʾ said: They say «رأيت الزّيدان» and «مررت بالزّيدان», and he recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 295-
فأطرق إطراق الشّجاع ولو يرى ... مساغا لناباه الشّجاع لصمّما
(He lowered his head as the serpent lowers its head; had the serpent seen an opening for its two fangs, it would have bitten deep.)
Abū al-Khaṭṭāb reported that this is the dialect of Banū Kināna. Al-Farrāʾ has another view; he said: I found the alif to be a prop (diʿāma), not the final radical of the word, so I added a nūn to it and did not change it, just as you say «الذي» and then add a nūn to it, saying «جاءني الذين عندك» and «رأيت الذين عندك». Abū Jaʿfar said: It was also said: the alif in your saying «هذان» was likened to the alif in «يفعلان», so it was not changed. Abū Isḥāq said: The early grammarians say the hāʾ here is implied, and the meaning is «إنّه هذان لساحران» ("indeed, the matter is: these two are sorcerers"). These are five views. Abū Jaʿfar said: I asked Abū al-Ḥasan ibn Kaysān about this verse, and he said: If you wish, I will answer you with the answer of the grammarians, and if you wish, I will answer you with my own view. I said: With your own view. He said: Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq asked me about it, and I said: The view I hold is that since «هذا» is said in the position of the nominative, the accusative and the genitive in one and the same state, and the dual ought not to change the singular for it, the dual was treated like the singular. He said: How fine this would be if someone had preceded you in saying it, so that one could feel at ease with it. I said: Then let the judge say it, so that one may feel at ease with it. And he smiled. Abū Jaʿfar said: The first view is the best, except that there is something in it, because one only says «نعم زيد خارج» ("Yes, Zayd is going out"), and the lām scarcely occurs here — although the grammarians have discussed this and said: the lām is intended to come first. Abū Isḥāq said: The meaning is «إنّ هذان لهما ساحران» ("Yes, these two — they are sorcerers"), then the mubtadaʾ (subject) was omitted, as the poet said: [al-Rajaz] 296-
أمّ الحليس لعجوز شهربه
(Umm al-Ḥulays is surely a decrepit old woman.)
The second view is among the best ways the verse has been interpreted, since this dialect is well known and has been reported by those whose knowledge, truthfulness and trustworthiness are approved — among them Abū Zayd al-Anṣārī, who is the one who says: "When Sībawayh says 'someone I trust told me,' he means only me"; and Abū al-Khaṭṭāb al-Akhfash, who is one of the leading masters of the language, from whom Sībawayh and others transmitted. Among the clearest things on this is the saying of Sībawayh: "Know that when you make the singular dual you add two added letters to it, the first of them being a letter of prolongation and softness, and it is the letter of inflection (ḥarf al-iʿrāb)." Abū Jaʿfar said: Sībawayh's saying "and it is the letter of inflection" requires that in principle it does not change. «إنّ هذان» came in its original form so that this would be known; Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: اسْتَحْوَذَ عَلَيْهِمُ الشَّيْطانُ [al-Mujādila: 19] and did not say «استحاذ»; it came in this way to indicate the original form, since the leading authorities transmitted it and it became clear that it is the original. This is very clear. وَيَذْهَبا بِطَرِيقَتِكُمُ الْمُثْلى The feminine of «أمثل», just as one says «الأفضل» and «الفضلى». «الطريقة» was made feminine according to the wording, even though men are meant by it; the feminine may also be according to the sense of the group.

nahhas-irab:64-64.t:
فَأَجْمِعُوا كَيْدَكُمْ is the reading of the people of the great cities, except Abū ʿAmr, who read «فاجمعوا» with the connecting hamza (waṣl) and fatḥa on the mīm, arguing from His saying, Mighty and Majestic: فَجَمَعَ كَيْدَهُ ثُمَّ أَتى [Ṭāhā: 60]. In what is reported from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd, he said: Abū ʿAmr's own argument obliges him to read contrary to this reading of his — namely the reading which most people follow. He said: Because he argued from «جمع», and His saying, Mighty and Majestic, فَجَمَعَ كَيْدَهُ has already established this, so it is unlikely that after it comes «فاجمعوا», and likely that after it comes «فأجمعوا», i.e. "resolve and be earnest"; since that had preceded, this one must differ from it in meaning.
One says: «أمر مجمع عليه» (a matter resolved upon). Abū Jaʿfar said: The justification of Abū ʿAmr's reading is: "gather every plot and every stratagem and join it with its fellow." ثُمَّ ائْتُوا صَفًّا Accusative because the verb falls on it. As for the saying of Abū ʿUbayda: he said one says «أتيت الصفّ», i.e. the place of prayer; so the meaning according to him is "come to the place where you gather on the day of the festival." Abū Isḥāq claimed that it may be accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:66-66.t:
Hārūn the reader said: The dialect of Banū Tamīm is «عصيهم» (with kasra on the ʿayn), and al-Ḥasan follows it. Abū Jaʿfar said: One who gives the ʿayn kasra makes the kasra follow the kasra, and we have mentioned it. يُخَيَّلُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ سِحْرِهِمْ أَنَّها تَسْعى Abū Isḥāq said: «أنّ» is in the position of a nominative, i.e. "their moving was made to appear to him." Al-Farrāʾ claimed that the position of «أنّ» is accusative, i.e. «بأنها», then the bāʾ was omitted. Al-Ḥasan read «تخيّل» with tāʾ. Abū ʿUbayd said: He meant the ropes. Abū Isḥāq said: One who reads with tāʾ makes «أنّ» in the position of an accusative, i.e. "they appeared to him as moving things." He said: It may also be in the position of a nominative as a badal (substitute) — a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl) — as Sībawayh reported: «ما لي بهم علم أمرهم», i.e. "I have no knowledge of their affair." He said: And he recited: [al-Rajaz] 297-
وذكرت تقتد برد مائها
(And she remembered Taqtud, the coolness of its water.)
i.e. she remembered the coolness of the water of Taqtud.

nahhas-irab:67-68.t: فَأَوْجَسَ فِي نَفْسِهِ خِيفَةً مُوسى It is said that he feared the people would be led astray when the sorcerers threw their ropes and staffs. They were far from the people, on one side; Pharaoh and his troops on another side; and Mūsā and Hārūn, Allah bless them both, on another side. So Mūsā ﷺ feared that the matter would be made confusing to the people, since they imagined that the ropes and staffs were moving and that they were snakes, and so they would fancy that the sorcerers had equalled Mūsā ﷺ in what he brought. It is also said that Mūsā ﷺ feared only because the command to throw the staff was delayed for him; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: لا تَخَفْ إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْأَعْلى, i.e. do not fear the confusion, for We shall make your matter clear so that you prevail over them with the proof.

nahhas-irab:69-69.t:
وَأَلْقِ ما فِي يَمِينِكَ تَلْقَفْ ما صَنَعُوا So he threw the staff, and it swallowed up their ropes and staffs, which were the load of three hundred camels; then it returned to being a staff, and no one knows where the ropes and staffs went except Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Abū Isḥāq said: The original form of «خيفة» is «خوفة»; the wāw was replaced by yāʾ because of the kasra before it.
He said: تَلْقَفْ ما صَنَعُوا in the nominative is also permissible [i.e. «تلقفُ»], being an imperfect verb in the position of an anticipated ḥāl (circumstantial).
He said: «أنّ ما صنعوا» with fatḥa on the hamza is also permissible, i.e. "because what…." كَيْدُ ساحِرٍ in the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ», with «ما» in the sense of «الذي»; the accusative [«كيدَ»] is on the basis that «ما» is the restraining «ما» (kāffa). The Kufans except ʿĀṣim read «كيد سحر», annexing the type to the genus, as you say «ثوب خزّ» ("a garment of silk").

nahhas-irab:71-71.t: إِنَّهُ لَكَبِيرُكُمُ الَّذِي عَلَّمَكُمُ السِّحْرَ The pronoun refers back to Mūsā ﷺ. Pharaoh used this as a ruse to confuse the people, saying to the sorcerers: "Mūsā is your chief," i.e. he is more skilled in sorcery than you, and he colluded with you in this and taught it to you. So he cut off their hands and feet on opposite sides and crucified them until they died. وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ أَيُّنا أَشَدُّ عَذاباً وَأَبْقى Abū Isḥāq said: «أيّ» is nominative because its form is the form of interrogation, so what precedes it does not act on it, since that is a statement.

nahhas-irab:72-72.t:
Abū Isḥāq said: «الذي» is in the position of a genitive by conjunction. The meaning is: "We will not prefer you over the clear proofs that have come to us, nor over Allah, Mighty and Majestic." He said: It may also be in the position of a genitive as an oath.
فَاقْضِ ما أَنْتَ قاضٍ The yāʾ is dropped in connected speech because it is vowelless and the tanwīn is vowelless; and it is dropped in the pause to indicate that in connected speech it is without yāʾ. Sībawayh chose to retain it in the pause, because the cause — the meeting of two vowelless letters — has gone. إِنَّما تَقْضِي هذِهِ الْحَياةَ الدُّنْيا Accusative as an adverb (ẓarf). The meaning is: "You only decide in the enjoyment of this worldly life." Al-Farrāʾ allowed the nominative, taking «ما» in the sense of «الذي».

nahhas-irab:73-73.t: «ما» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to «الخطايا». It was also said: it has no position and is negating, i.e. "that He may forgive us our sins of sorcery, and you did not compel us to it." The first is preferable.

nahhas-irab:74-74.t: إِنَّهُ مَنْ يَأْتِ رَبَّهُ مُجْرِماً The hāʾ is an allusion to the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ».

nahhas-irab:77-77.t:
«أَنْ أَسْرِ» from «أسرى», and «أنِ اسْرِ» from «سرى»: two eloquent dialects. فَاضْرِبْ لَهُمْ طَرِيقاً فِي الْبَحْرِ يَبَساً لا تَخافُ دَرَكاً is the reading of the people of the two Sanctuaries, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī; al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read «لا تخف دركا». The first reading is clearer, because after it comes وَلا تَخْشى, agreed upon without jussive. The first reading has three interpretations: it may be in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial); in the position of a naʿt (adjective) of «طريق», with an omission in it [i.e. "in which you do not fear"]; or cut off from what precedes [i.e. resumptive]. The second reading has two interpretations: one is the jussive of prohibition, and the other is the jussive as the answer to the imperative, namely «فاضرب». As for وَلا تَخْشى when you make «لا تخف» jussive, the grammarians have two interpretations of it. One — and it is the only one permissible — is that it is cut off from the first, like يُوَلُّوكُمُ الْأَدْبارَ ثُمَّ لا يُنْصَرُونَ [Āl ʿImrān: 111]. The other interpretation — al-Farrāʾ mentioned it ] [Translator's note: the bracket is as in the source] — is that «ولا تخشى» is intended as jussive while the yāʾ [i.e. the final letter] is retained in it; he claimed it is as the poet said: [al-Basīṭ] 298-
هجوت زبّان ثمّ جئت معتذرا ... من سبّ زبّان لم تهجو ولم تدع
(You satirised Zabbān, then came apologising for reviling Zabbān — you neither satirised nor left it alone.)
And he recited: [al-Wāfir] 299-
ألم يأتيك والأنباء تنمى ... بما لاقت لبون بني زياد
(Has it not reached you — and news spreads — what befell the milch-camels of Banū Ziyād?)
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is among the ugliest of errors — to interpret the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, by anomalies of poetry. Moreover, the poetry he brought does not resemble the verse at all, because the wāw and the yāʾ differ from the alif, since they can take a vowel and the alif cannot; so the poet, when compelled, may suppose them to be voweled and then drop the vowel for the jussive, but this is impossible with the alif. Moreover, there is no metrical necessity in the two verses requiring this, because if they are transmitted with the wāw and the yāʾ dropped, they are sound metre of al-Basīṭ and al-Wāfir; al-Khalīl calls the first maṭwī and the second manqūṣ.

nahhas-irab:78-78.t: In the sense of magnifying [the event] and knowledge of the matter.

nahhas-irab:79-79.t: i.e. he led them away from right guidance, and did not guide them to any good or salvation, because he reckoned that Mūsā ﷺ and those who followed him could not escape him, since the sea was before them. When Mūsā ﷺ struck the sea with his staff, twelve paths split open in it, with the water standing between the paths like mountains, and each tribe took a path.
