Ibn Masʿūd, Qatāda, al-Aʿmash (with a difference reported from him), Abū Ḥaywa, Ibn Abī ʿAbla and Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar [read it] with kasra on the ẓāʾ. From Ibn Yaʿmar ḍamma was also reported. Ubayy and al-Aʿmash in the other transmission read «ظَلِلْتَ» with two lāms, the first with kasra.
As for the reading of the majority, in it one of the two like letters is dropped, and the ẓāʾ is kept with its own vowel; it was dropped only for lightness. Sībawayh counted it among the irregular (shādhdh), meaning irregular in analogy, not in usage, and he counted other words with it, such as «مَسْتُ» and «أَحَسْتُ», as in the verse: 3317 - «. . . . . . . أَحَسْنَ به فهنَّ إليه شُوْسُ» (they sensed him, and they are looking sideways at him). Ibn al-Anbārī counted «هَمْتُ» for «هَمَمْتُ». This dropping occurs only when the lām of the verb has sukūn. Some later scholars mentioned that this dropping is analogical in every verb whose ʿayn and lām are doubled and whose lām has sukūn, and that is in the dialect of Sulaym.
What I say is: whenever the doubling mentioned meets a kasra, as in «ظَلِلْتُ» and «مَسِسْتُ», the dropping is analogical. Does ḍamma take the place of kasra in this? The apparent answer is that it does, indeed all the more, because ḍamma is heavier than kasra, as in «غُضْنَ يا نسوةُ», i.e. «أغْضُضْنَ أبصارَكُنَّ» ("lower your gazes, women"); Jamāl al-Dīn Ibn Mālik mentioned it. As for fatḥa, the dropping in it is weak, as in «قَرْن يا نسوةُ في المنزل» ('stay, women, in the house'), and of this, in one of the two explanations of the reading of {وَقَرْنَ فِي بُيُوتِكُنَّ} [al-Aḥzāb: 33], as will come, God willing.
As for the kasra, its explanation is that he moved the kasra of the lām to the fāʾ (first radical) after stripping that of its own vowel, to point to it. As for the ḍamma, it may be that a dialect exists on the pattern «فَعَل يفعُل» with fatḥa on the ʿayn in the past and ḍamma in the imperfect, and then it was moved as explained for the kasra. As for «ظَلِلْت» with two lāms, this is the original, and it alerts to the others. And {عاكفاً} is the khabar of «ظَلَّ».
His saying: {لَّنُحَرِّقَنَّهُ}: the response to an omitted oath, i.e. "By Allah, we shall surely burn it". The majority read it with ḍamma on the nūn and kasra on the doubled rāʾ, from «حَرَّقه يُحرِّقُه» with intensification. There are two interpretations of it. The clearer is that it is from «حَرَّقه بالنار» (burned it with fire). The second: that it is from «حَرَق نابُ البعير», when one of the camel's tusks gnashes against another; the sound heard from it is called «الصَّريف». The meaning: "we shall file it down with a file, a filing by which we destroy it, as the camel does with its tusks, one on another."
al-Ḥasan, Qatāda and Abū Jaʿfar read «لَنُحْرِقَنَّه» with ḍamma on the nūn, sukūn on the ḥāʾ and kasra on the rāʾ, from «أحرق» (four-letter verb). Ibn ʿAbbās, Ḥumayd, ʿĪsā and Abū Jaʿfar read «لَنَحْرُقَنَّه» likewise except that he gave the rāʾ ḍamma. It may be that «أَحْرق» and «حرَّق» have one meaning, like «أَنْزل» and «نزَّل». As for the last reading, it means "we shall file it down with a file".
His saying: {لَنَنسِفَنَّهُ}: The majority read fatḥa on the first nūn, sukūn on the second, and a light kasra on the sīn. ʿĪsā read the sīn with ḍamma. Ibn Miqsam read the first nūn with ḍamma, the second with fatḥa, and the sīn with kasra and shadda. «النَّسْف» is scattering and winnowing; it is also said: uprooting something from its base. It is said «نَسَفَه يَنْسِفُه» with kasra on the sīn, and with ḍamma, in the imperfect, and on this rest the two readings. The shadda is for intensification.

semin-durr:98-98.t:
His saying: {وَسِعَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ عِلْماً}: The majority read the sīn with kasra, light. In this reading «عِلْماً» is a tamyīz (specification) transferred from the agent, since the original is «وَسِعَ عِلْمُه كلَّ شيءٍ». Mujāhid and Qatāda read the sīn with fatḥa and shadda. In the accusative of «علماً» in that case [there are two views]. One: that it is a direct object. al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its explanation is that «وَسِع» is transitive to one object, and «عِلْماً» is accusative as tamyīz, being the agent in meaning. When it was intensified, it was transferred to transitivity with two objects, so both are put in the accusative as objects, because the specifier is an agent in meaning, just as you say of «خاف زيد عمراً»: «خَوَّفْت زيداً عمراً»; thus by the transfer you return what was an agent to being an object." Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "The meaning is: He gave everything knowledge", so he made it include the sense of «أعطى». What al-Zamakhsharī said is preferable.
The second view: that it is also a tamyīz, as in the light reading. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "There is also another possibility: that it means 'He magnified the creation of everything', such as the earth and the heaven, and that is in the sense of «بَسَط» (spread out), so «علماً» would be a tamyīz." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "He widened the creation of things and multiplied them by origination."

semin-durr:99-99.t: His saying: {كذلك نَقُصُّ}: The kāf is either an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, or a ḥāl of the pronoun of that implied maṣdar. The implied form: "We relate, like Our relating of this strange report." «من أنباءِ» is an adjective of an omitted element which is the object of «نَقُصُّ», i.e. "We relate a report from among the reports of".

semin-durr:100-100.t: His saying: {مَّنْ أَعْرَضَ}: «مَنْ» may be conditional or relative. The conditional sentence, or the predicative sentence resembling it, is in the position of accusative as an adjective of «ذِكْراً».

semin-durr:101-101.t:
His saying: {خَالِدِينَ}: a ḥāl of the agent of «يَحْمِلُ». If it is asked: how can a plural occur as a ḥāl of a singular? The answer is that it was carried over onto the wording of «مَنْ», so the pronoun is singular in «أَعْرَضَ», «فإنَّه» and «يَحْمِلُ», and onto its meaning, so it is plural in «خالدين» and «لهم». The pronoun in «فيه» refers to «وِزْراً». What is meant is the punishment caused by the burden, which is the sin, so the cause is put in the place of the caused.
Dāwūd ibn Rufayʿ read «يُحَمَّلُ» with doubling, in the passive, and what stands in place of the agent is the pronoun of «مَنْ»; «وِزْراً» is a second object.
His saying: {وَسَآءَ}: this is the «ساء» that means «بِئْس». Its agent is latent in it, referring to «حِمْلاً», accusative as tamyīz, because in this chapter the pronoun is explained by what follows it. The implied form: «وساء الحِمْل حِمْلاً». The specific object of blame is omitted, its implied form being: «وساء الحِمْل حِمْلاً وِزْرُهم». It is not permissible for the agent of «بِئْس» to be the pronoun of «الوِزْر», because the condition of the pronoun in this chapter is that it refer to the tamyīz itself. If you say: why do you reject that «ساء» contains the pronoun of «الوِزْر»? I say: it is not valid that «ساء», whose rule is that of «بِئْس», contain the pronoun of a specific, non-vague thing. Nor is it permissible that «ساء» here mean «أهمَّ» and «أحزنَ» (distressed, grieved), so as to be conjugated like other verbs. al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is enough to turn you away from it that the speech of Allah the Exalted would come to [your saying]: 'and the burden grieved them on the Day of Resurrection as a load', after you extricate yourself from the burden of this lām and of this accusative." End of quotation.
The lām in «لهم» is attached to an omitted element by way of clarification, like the one in {هَيْتَ لَكَ} [Yūsuf: 23].

semin-durr:102-102.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَ يُنفَخُ}: «يومَ» is a badal of «يومَ القيامة», or an explication of it, or it is accusative by an implied verb, or the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ. It is built on fatḥa according to the Kufans, like the reading of {هذا يَوْمَ يَنفَعُ} [al-Māʾida: 119], which has been discussed.
Abū ʿAmr read «نَنْفُخُ», active, with the nūn of majesty; the act is attributed to the one who commands it, out of veneration for the one commanded, who is the angel Isrāfīl. The rest read it with a yāʾ with ḍamma and fatḥa on the fāʾ, in the passive, and what stands in place of the agent is the preposition and its genitive noun after it. The majority read the wāw with sukūn. al-Ḥasan and Ibn ʿĀmir in one transmission read it with fatḥa, as the plural of «صُوْرَة», like «غُرَف» plural of «غُرْفَة». «الصور» was discussed in al-Anʿām.
«يَنْفُخُ» and «يَحْشُر» have also been read with a yāʾ with fatḥa, in the active, the agent being Allah the Exalted or the angel. al-Ḥasan, Ṭalḥa and Ḥumayd read «يُنْفَخ» like the majority, and «يَحْشر» with a yāʾ with fatḥa, in the active; the agent, as before, is the pronoun of the Creator or of the angel. It was also reported from al-Ḥasan «ويُحْشَر», in the passive, with «المجرمون» nominative by it. «زُرْقاً» is a ḥāl of «المجرمين»; what is meant is blueness of the eyes. The ḥāl came here with a quality resembling the inseparable, though its basis is non-inseparability; had you said in speech «جاءني زيدٌ أزرقَ العينِ» it would not be permissible except by interpretation.

semin-durr:103-103.t:
His saying: {يَتَخَافَتُونَ}: it may be resumptive (mustaʾnaf), or a second ḥāl of «المجرمين», or a ḥāl of the latent pronoun in «زرقاً», in which case it is a nested ḥāl, being a ḥāl from a ḥāl. The meaning of «يتخافتون» is: they speak secretly among themselves.
His saying {إِن لَّبِثْتُمْ إِلاَّ} is the object of the secret speaking. His saying {إِلاَّ عَشْراً}: nights may be meant, in which case dropping the tāʾ from the number is analogical; or days may be meant, in which case it is asked: why was the tāʾ dropped? It was said: if the counted noun is not mentioned in the number for the masculine, the tāʾ and its absence are both permissible. It is heard in their speech «صُمْنا من الشهر خمساً» ('we fasted five of the month'), though what is fasted is only the days, not the nights. In the ḥadīth: «مَنْ صامَ رمضانَ وأتبعه بسِتٍّ من شوال» ('whoever fasted Ramadan and followed it with six of Shawwāl'). The dropping is good here because it is the end of a verse and a pause.

semin-durr:104-104.t: His saying: {إِذْ يَقُولُ}: accusative by «أعلمُ», and «طريقةً» is accusative as tamyīz. [Translator's note: the source text reads «وطريقةً "نصبٌ» with a stray quotation mark, apparently a garbled reference to {أَمْثَلُهُمْ طَرِيقَةً}; translated as written.]

semin-durr:106-106.t:
His saying: {فَيَذَرُهَا}: there are two views about this pronoun. One: that it is the pronoun of «الأرض», implied because it is indicated. The second: the pronoun of «الجبال», on the basis of an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "He leaves their bases and settled places". «نَذَرُ» may mean "He leaves it empty", in which case «قاعاً» is a ḥāl; or it may mean the "making" sense of «يترك», in which case it takes two objects and «قاعاً» is the second.
About «القاع» there are statements. It is said: it is a pool of standing water, and its meaning does not suit here. The second: that it is the uncovered part of the earth; so said Makkī. The third: that it is the level place, and of this is the saying of Ḍirār ibn al-Khaṭṭāb: 3318 - «لَتَكُوْنَنَّ بالبطاحِ قُرَيْشٌ ... فَقْعَةَ القاع في أَكُفِّ الإِماءِ» (Quraysh in the valley-beds will be like a desert truffle of the plain in the hands of slave girls). The fourth: that it is land in which there is no plant and no building.
«الصَّفْصَف» is smooth land; it is also said: level land, so the two are close to synonyms. The plural of «القاع» is «أقْوع», «أَقْواع» and «قِيْعان».

semin-durr:107-107.t:
His saying: {لاَّ ترى فِيهَا عِوَجاً}: this sentence may be resumptive, or a ḥāl of «الجبال», or an adjective of the preceding ḥāl, which is «قاعاً» on one of the two interpretations, or an adjective of the second object on the other interpretation.
«العِوَج» has been discussed. al-Zamakhsharī said here: "If you say: they have distinguished between «العَوَج» and «العِوَج»; they said: «العِوَج» with kasra is for abstract things (maʿānī), and with fatḥa for concrete things (aʿyān), and the earth is a concrete thing, so how is kasra of the ʿayn valid in it? I say: the choice of this word has a fine and wonderful effect in describing the earth as level and smooth and negating crookedness from it in the most emphatic way. That is, if you took a piece of land and levelled it, and were thorough in levelling it by your eye and the eyes of the sighted, and you all agreed that no crookedness at all remained in it, and then you sought the opinion of the surveyor and ordered him to test its levelness by geometric measures, he would stumble on crookedness in more than one place, not perceived by the sense of sight but by geometric measure. So Allah the Exalted negated that crookedness which is too fine and subtle to be perceived, except by the measure known to the person of geometric calculation. And since that crookedness is not perceived except by measure and not by sensation, it was joined to abstract things, so «عِوج» was said of it with kasra."
«الأمْت» is slight protrusion. It is said: "He stretched his rope until there was no amt in it." It is also said: «الأمْت» is the mound, which is close to the first. It is also said: the cracks in the ground. It is also said: the hillocks.

semin-durr:108-108.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَئِذٍ}: accusative by «يَتَّبِعُون». It is also said: a badal of {يَوْمَ القيامة}; so said al-Zamakhsharī. There is room for objection in it because of the long separation. Also «يَتَّبِعُون» would remain unconnected with what precedes it, and the meaning would be lost by it. The implied form: "the day when the mountains are blown away".
His saying: {لاَ عِوَجَ لَهُ}: the sentence may be resumptive, or a ḥāl of «الداعي». The sentence may also be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, its implied form being: "they follow him with a following that has no crookedness". Regarding the pronoun in «له» there are several views, the clearest being that it refers to «الداعي», i.e. there is no crookedness in his call, but he makes all of them hear, not inclining to some people over others. It is also said: it refers to that omitted maṣdar, i.e. no crookedness in that following. The third: that there is a reversal (qalb) in the speech, the implied form being «لا عِوَجَ لهم عنه» ('they have no turning away from him').
His saying: {إِلاَّ هَمْساً}: a direct object, and it is a "voided" exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh). «الهَمْس» is the faint sound. It is said: it is moving the lips without speech. al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is the faint murmur (rikz); from it are the voiceless letters (al-ḥurūf al-mahmūsa)." It is also said: it is what is heard of the fall of feet on the ground. From it «هَمَسَتِ الإبلُ», when that is heard from the fall of their hooves on the ground. He said: 3319 - «وهُنَّ يَمْشِيْنَ بنا هَمِيْسا ...» (and they walk with us at a hushed pace . . .).

semin-durr:109-109.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَئِذٍ}: a badal of what preceded, or accusative by what follows «لا», according to those who allow that. The implied form: "on the day when they follow, intercession will not benefit".
His saying: {إِلاَّ مَنْ أَذِنَ}: there are several views. One: that it is accusative as a direct object, and the governing word is «تَنْفَعُ»; «مَنْ» then refers to the one interceded for. The second: that it is in the position of nominative as a badal of «الشفاعة», and an omitted muḍāf is needed, implied as: "except the intercession of him for whom permission was given". The third: that it is accusative as an exception from «الشفاعة», with the omitted muḍāf implied, and on this it is a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil). It may be a disconnected exception (munqaṭiʿ) if you imply nothing, and then it may be accusative, which is the dialect of the Ḥijāz, or nominative, which is the dialect of Tamīm. All these views are clear from what preceded, so I shall not lengthen with establishing them. «له» in the two places is for cause, like His saying {وَقَالَ الذين كَفَرُواْ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ} [al-Aḥqāf: 11], i.e. on account of him and on account of them.

semin-durr:111-111.t:
His saying: {وَعَنَتِ الوجوه}: It is said «عَنا يَعْنُو» when one is humbled and submits, and «أَعْناه غيرُه», i.e. someone else humbled him. From it comes «العُنَاة», plural of «عانٍ», which is the captive. He said: 3320 - «فيا رُبَّ مَكْروبٍ كرَرْتُ وراءَه ... وعانٍ فَكَكْتُ الغُلَّ عنه فَفَدَّاني» (How many a distressed one have I charged after, and how many a captive have I freed from his shackle, and he ransomed me). Umayya ibn Abī l-Ṣalt said: 3321 - «مَلِيكٌ على عَرْشِ السماء مُهَيْمِنٌ ... لِعِزَّته تَعْنُوا الوجوهُ وتَسْجُد» (A King on the throne of heaven, the Overseer; before His might faces submit and prostrate). In the ḥadīth: «فإنَّهنَّ عَوانٍ» ('for they are captives').
His saying: {وَقَدْ خَابَ}: this sentence may be resumptive, or a ḥāl, or parenthetical (iʿtirāḍ). al-Zamakhsharī said: "«وقد خابَ» and what follows is parenthetical, like your saying 'they failed and lost', for everyone who does wrong is a failure and a loser." By parenthesis here he means that he restricted «الوجوه» to the faces of the disobedient, so that the sentence entered between the disobedient and {وَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِنَ الصالحات}; this, in his view, is the counterpart of «وعَنَتِ الوجوهُ», and for this reason it is parenthetical. As for Ibn ʿAṭiyya, he made «الوجوه» general, and therefore made «وقد خابَ مَنْ حَمَل ظلماً» a balance for His saying {وَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِنَ الصالحات} to the end.

semin-durr:112-112.t:
His saying: {وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ}: a ḥāl sentence. His saying {فَلاَ يَخَافُ}: Ibn Kathīr read it jussive, as a prohibition. The rest read it nominative, as a negation and resumption, i.e. "so he does not fear".
«الهَضْم» is diminution. The Arabs say «هَضَمْتُ لزيدٍ مِنْ حقي», i.e. I reduced something of my right for Zayd; of it is «هَضِيم الكَشْحَيْن», i.e. slender in both flanks. Of it also is {طَلْعُهَا هَضِيمٌ} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 148], i.e. fine and packed, as though some of it wrongs another and so reduces its right. A man is «هضيم» and «مُهْتَضَم», i.e. wronged. «هَضَمْتُه», «اهْتَضَمْتُه» and «تَهَضَّمْتُه» all have one meaning. al-Mutawakkil al-Laythī said: 3322 - «إنَّ الأذِلَّةَ واللِّئامَ لَمَعْشَرٌ ... مَوْلاهُمُ المُتَهَضِّمُ المظلومُ» (The abject and the base are a company whose client is the oppressed, the wronged).
It is said that wrong (ẓulm) and diminution (haḍm) are close. Judge al-Māwardī distinguished between them, saying: "Ẓulm is withholding the whole of the right, and haḍm is withholding part of it."

semin-durr:113-113.t:
His saying: {وكذلك أَنزَلْنَاهُ}: a conjunction (nasaq) on {كذلك نَقُصُّ}. al-Zamakhsharī said: "And like that sending down; just as We sent down upon you these verses, We sent down the Qurʾān as a whole in this manner." Another said: "The meaning: just as We decreed these matters and made them truly lie in wait for the servants, so We warned these people about it and sent it down as a Qurʾān."
His saying: {مِنَ الوعيد}: an adjective of an omitted object, i.e. "We have set out in the Qurʾān a threat from among the threats", the genus being meant. «من» may be redundant according to the view of al-Akhfash regarding the direct object; the implied form: "We set out the threat in it".
al-Ḥasan read «أو يُحْدِثْ» like the group, except that he put sukūn on the lām of the verb. ʿAbd Allāh (Ibn Masʿūd), al-Ḥasan also in one transmission, Mujāhid and Abū Ḥaywa read «نُحْدِثْ» with nūn, also with sukūn on the lām. It was explained by treating the connected reading (waṣl) as the pause (waqf), or by putting sukūn on the verb as a dislike of the vowel, like the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays: 3323 - «فاليومَ أشرَبْ غيرَ مُسْتَحْقِبٍ ... . . .» (Today I drink, not laden with guilt . . .), and the saying of Jarīr: 3324 - «. . . . . . . . . ... أو نهرُ تيرى فلا تَعْرِفْكُمُ النَّفَرُ» (. . . or the river of Tīrā, so the tribe will not know you). Abū ʿAmr, as already said, did this with the rāʾ in particular, as in {يَنصُرُكُم} [Āl ʿImrān: 160].
«تُحْدِثُ» has also been read with the addressee's tāʾ, i.e. "you bring about".

semin-durr:114-114.t: His saying: {يقضى إِلَيْكَ وَحْيُهُ}: The majority read «يقضى» in the passive with «وَحْيُه» nominative as standing in place of the agent. al-Jaḥdarī, Abū Ḥaywa and al-Ḥasan, and it is the reading of ʿAbd Allāh (Ibn Masʿūd), read «نَقْضي» with the nūn of majesty in the active, «وَحْيَه» being a direct object. al-Aʿmash read likewise except that he put sukūn on the lām of the verb, disliking the vowel even though it is light on a weak letter. Instances of this have preceded in the reading of {مِنْ أَوْسَطِ مَا تُطْعِمُونَ أَهْلِيكُمْ} [al-Māʾida: 89].

semin-durr:115-115.t:
al-Yamānī read «فَنُسِي» with ḍamma on the nūn and shadda on the sīn, meaning: Satan made him forget.
His saying: {وَلَمْ نَجِدْ لَهُ عَزْماً}: «وجد» may be of knowing, so that it takes two objects, which are «له عَزْما»; or it may mean "to come upon", so that it takes one, which is «عَزْما». «له» is attached to the finding, or to an omitted element as a ḥāl of «عَزْما», since originally it is its adjective, put before it.

semin-durr:116-116.t: His saying: {أبى}: a resumptive sentence, because it is the answer to an implied question, i.e. "What prevented him from prostrating?", and it is answered that he refused and was arrogant. The object of refusal may be intended; in the other verse it is stated explicitly, in His saying {أبى أَن يَكُونَ مَعَ الساجدين} [al-Ḥijr: 31]. Omitting it here is made good by the verb being at the head of a verse-ending. It may also be that none is intended at all, and that the meaning is: "he is of the people of refusal and disobedience", without regard to what the refusal is attached to.

semin-durr:117-117.t: His saying: {فتشقى}: accusative by an implied «أَنْ» in the response to a prohibition. The prohibition is in form addressed to Iblīs, but the two of them (Adam and his wife) are meant, i.e. "do not engage in the causes of expulsion so that misery comes to you both", which is toil and worldly hardship in particular. It may be nominative as resumptive, i.e. "so you will be miserable"; so the Shaykh implied it. This is remote or impossible, since the aim is not to report that he will be miserable, but that if the expulsion of the two of them by Iblīs occurs, what was mentioned results. He attributed misery to him (Adam) and not to her because affairs are bound to the heads of men. What made that good was its being at the head of a verse-ending.

semin-durr:118-118.t: His saying: {إِنَّ لَكَ أَلاَّ تَجُوعَ}: in the position of accusative as the ism of «إنَّ»; the khabar is «لك». The implied form: "You have the absence of hunger and nakedness." So «تعرى» is accusative by implication, a conjunction on «تجوعَ». «العُرْي» is the skin's being stripped of something that protects it. It is said «عَرِي يعرى عُرِيَّاً». The poet said: 3325 - «وإنْ يَعْرَيْنَ إن كُسِيَ الجَواري ... فَتَنْبُو العينُ عن كَرَمٍ عِجافِ» (And if they go bare while the slave-girls are clothed, the eye turns away from noble, lean ones).

semin-durr:119-119.t:
His saying: {وَأَنَّكَ لاَ تَظْمَأُ}: Nāfiʿ and Abū Bakr read «وإنك» with kasra on the hamza; the rest read it with fatḥa. For one who read it with kasra, it may be resumptive, or a conjunction on the first «إنَّ». For one who read it with fatḥa, it is because he conjoined an interpreted maṣdar to the ism of the first «إنَّ». The khabar is the preceding «لك». The implied form: "You have the absence of hunger, the absence of nakedness, the absence of thirst and the absence of the midday sun." It is permissible for «أنَّ» with fatḥa to be the ism of «إنَّ» with kasra because of the separation between them; had it not been for that, it would not be permissible. If you said «إنَّ أنَّ زيداً قائم حَقٌّ» it would not be permissible, but when they are separated it is permissible. You say «إنَّ عندي أن زيداً قائم», where «عندي» is the khabar put before the ism, which is «أنَّ» and what is in its interpretation, because it is an adverbial; and the verse belongs to this type, the implied form being: «وإنَّ لك أنَّك لا تظمأ». al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: «إنَّ» does not enter «أنَّ», so one does not say «إنَّ أنَّ زيداً منطلق»; and the wāw stands in for «أنَّ» and takes its place, so why did it enter it? I say: the wāw was not set up to be always a substitute for «أنَّ»; it is a substitute for every governing element. Since it is not a particle set up for verification alone like «إنَّ», their combination is not barred, as the combination of «إنَّ» and «أنَّ» is barred."
«ضحى يَضْحَى» means to come out to the sun. ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa said: 3326 - «رَأَتْ رجلاً أَيْما إذا الشمسُ عارَضَتْ ... فيضحى وأيْما بالعَشِيِّ فَيَخْصَرُ» (She saw a man who, when the sun faces him, is exposed to it, and in the evening is chilled).
al-Zamakhsharī mentioned here a fine point in that the Exalted mentioned these things in negative wording without mentioning their opposites in affirmative wording, such as: "You have satiety, clothing, quenched thirst and shelter in the shade." He said: "He mentioned them in negative wording for their opposites, which are hunger, nakedness, thirst and exposure to the sun, so that the names of the kinds of misery of which He warned him would strike his ear, so that he would shun the cause that leads into them, out of aversion to them."

semin-durr:120-120.t: His saying: {فَوَسْوَسَ إِلَيْهِ}: «وَسْوَسَ إليه» means he conveyed the whispering to him. As for «وَسْوس له», its meaning is "for his sake". al-Zamakhsharī: "If you say: how is «وَسْوس» made transitive sometimes by lām, in His saying {فَوَسْوَسَ لَهُمَا الشيطان} [al-Aʿrāf: 20], and at other times by «إلى»? I say: Satan's whispering is like the wailing of the bereaved woman and the clucking of the hen, in that they are imitations of sounds, so their rule is that of a sound or a tinkle. From it is the whispering of one with delirium (al-mubarsam), and he is «مُوَسْوِس» with kasra; fatḥa is a mistake. Ibn al-Aʿrābī recited: 3327 - «وَسْوَسَ يَدْعو مُخْلِصاً رَبَّ الفَلَقْ» (He whispered, calling sincerely upon the Lord of the Daybreak). When you say «وَسْوَسَ له» its meaning is "for his sake", as in 3328 - «أجْرِسْ لها يا ابنَ أبي كِباشِ» (Make a sound for her, O son of Abū Kibāsh). The meaning of «وَسْوس إليه»: he conveyed the whispering to him, being in the sense of 'he mentioned to him'. And it may mean 'for his sake'."

semin-durr:121-121.t: His saying: {فغوى}: The majority read the wāw with fatḥa followed by an alif. Its explanation is clear. It is also said: its meaning is "he suffered indigestion" (bashima), from their saying «غَوِي البعير» with kasra on the wāw and the yāʾ, when that befalls it. Abū l-Baqāʾ reported this as a reading, and they explained it by this meaning. al-Zamakhsharī said: "From some of them: «فَغَوِيَ», meaning he suffered indigestion from eating much. Even if this is sound in the dialect of those who turn a yāʾ whose preceding letter has kasra into alif, saying of «فَنِي» and «بَقِي»: «فَنا» and «بَقا» (these are Banū Ṭayyiʾ), it is a vile explanation." I say: it seems he was not aware that it had been read with kasra on the wāw; had he been aware of it he would have rejected it. The one who says this has fled from ascribing error (ghayy) to Adam, peace be upon him.

semin-durr:124-124.t:
His saying: {ضَنكاً}: an adjective of «معيشة»; its origin is a maṣdar, and therefore it is not made feminine. It applies to singular, dual and plural with one wording.
The majority read «ضَنْكاً» with tanwīn in connected reading and its replacement by alif in pause, like all declinable words. A group read «ضنكى» with alif, like «سكرى». There are two possibilities for this alif. One: that it is a replacement for the tanwīn, with the connected reading treated as the pause, like parallels that have passed; the rest of them will come, God willing. The second: that it is the alif of feminine marking, the maṣdar being built on «فَعْلى» like «دعوى».
«الضَّنْك» is narrowness and hardship. It is said «ضَنُكَ عيشُه يَضْنُك ضَنَاكة وضَنْكاً». A woman is «ضِناك» when her body is fleshy, as though they imagined the narrowness of her skin by it.
The majority read «ونَحْشُرُه» with nūn and the verb nominative as resumptive. Abān ibn Taghlib, with others, put sukūn on the rāʾ. This allows two explanations. One: that the verb is jussive, conjoined to the position of the apodosis of the condition, which is the sentence {فَإِنَّ لَهُ مَعِيشَةً}, for its position is jussive; so it is like the reading of {مَن يُضْلِلِ الله فَلاَ هَادِيَ لَهُ وَيَذَرْهُمْ} [al-Aʿrāf: 186] with sukūn on the rāʾ. The second: that the sukūn is a sukūn of lightening, like {يَأْمُرْكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 67] and its like.
A group read it with the third-person yāʾ, the subject being Allah the Exalted or the angel. Abān ibn Taghlib in one transmission read «ونَحْشُرهْ» with sukūn on the hāʾ in connected reading. Its explanation is either by the dialect of Banū ʿUqayl and Banū Kilāb, or by treating the connected reading as the pause. «أعمى» is accusative as a ḥāl.

semin-durr:125-125.t: His saying: {وَقَدْ كُنتُ بَصِيراً}: a ḥāl sentence from the object of «حَشَرْتني». Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr gave the yāʾ of «حَشَرْتني» fatḥa before the hamza.

semin-durr:126-126.t: His saying: {كذلك أَتَتْكَ}: Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "«كذلك» is in the position of accusative, i.e. 'a gathering like that', or 'We did the like of that', or 'a coming like that', or 'a recompense like your turning away', or 'forgetting'." In some of these views that he stated the kāf is accusative as a maṣdar, and in others accusative as a direct object. al-Zamakhsharī mentioned only the direct object, saying: "i.e. you did the like of that; then it is explained that Our signs came to you clear and luminous, yet you did not look at them with the eye of one who takes heed."

semin-durr:127-127.t: The Exalted's saying: {وكذلك نَجْزِي مَنْ أَسْرَفَ}: i.e. "and like that recompense We recompense him who transgressed".

semin-durr:128-128.t:
His saying: {أَفَلَمْ يَهْدِ لَهُمْ}: regarding the agent of «يَهْدِ» there are several views. One: that it is the pronoun of the Creator the Exalted. «يَهْدي» means "to make clear". The object of «يهدي» is omitted, its implied form being: "Has Allah not made clear to them the lessons and what He did to the denying nations?" Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "As to its agent there are two views, one of which is the pronoun of the name of Allah the Exalted, and he suspended «بَيَّن» here when it has the meaning of «اعلمْ», as He suspended it in His saying {وَتَبَيَّنَ لَكُمْ كَيْفَ فَعَلْنَا بِهِمْ} [Ibrāhīm: 45]." The Shaykh said: "«كم» here is informative (khabariyya), so the governing verb is not suspended from it." al-Zamakhsharī said: "It may contain the pronoun of Allah or of the Messenger, and the reading with nūn indicates this."
The second view: that the agent is a latent pronoun explained by what indicates it from the speech that follows. al-Ḥūfī said: "«كم أَهْلكنا» indicates the destruction of the generations. The implied form: 'Has the destruction of those We destroyed of the generations, and the effacing of their traces, not become clear to them, that they might take warning?'" Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "The agent is what is indicated by His saying {أَهْلَكْنَا}, i.e. 'Our destroying', and the sentence explains it."
The third view: that the agent is the following sentence itself. al-Zamakhsharī said: "The agent of «لم يَهْدِ» is the sentence after it, meaning: 'Has this not guided them, in its sense and content?' Its parallel is His saying {وَتَرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ فِي الآخرين سَلاَمٌ على نُوحٍ فِي العالمين} [al-Ṣāffāt: 79], i.e. We left upon him this speech." The Shaykh said: "That a sentence is the agent of «يَهْدِ» is the Kufan school. As for his comparing and likening it to {وَتَرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ فِي الآخرين سَلاَمٌ على نُوحٍ فِي العالمين}, «تركْنا» there has the sense of speech, so the sentence is quoted by it, as though it were said: 'We said upon him' and 'We applied to him this expression'; and a sentence is quoted by the sense of saying as it is quoted by saying."
The fourth view: that it is the pronoun of the Messenger ﷺ, because he is the one who makes clear to them, by what is revealed to him, the reports of past nations and bygone generations. This view was reported earlier from Abū l-Qāsim al-Zamakhsharī.
The fifth view: that the agent is omitted. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said, quoting others: "The agent is implied, its implied form being: guidance, or the matter, or looking and taking heed." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This, to my mind, is the best of the implications."
The Shaykh said: "It is the saying of al-Mubarrad, and it is not good, since it contains omission of the agent, which the Basrans do not permit; its improvement is to say: the agent is a latent pronoun, implied as 'yahdi huwa', i.e. the guidance." I say: this saying does not say the agent is omitted, but that it is implied («مقدر»), and the word «مقدر» is often used for the latent pronoun. As for the object of «يَهْدِ», there are two views: one, that it is omitted; the second, that it is the sentence of «كم» and what is within its scope, because it suspends it, so it fills the place of its object.
The sixth view: that the agent is «كم»; so said al-Ḥūfī, and he (al-Ḥūfī) rejected it in whoever said it, because «كم» is interrogative and what precedes it does not govern in it. The Shaykh said: "It is not interrogative here but informative." The Shaykh preferred that the agent be the pronoun referring to Allah the Exalted, saying: "The best of the explanations is that the agent be a pronoun referring to Allah the Exalted, as though He said: 'Has Allah not made clear?' The object of «يُبَيِّن» is omitted, i.e. the lessons through the destruction of the earlier generations. Then He said {كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا}, i.e. 'many We destroyed', so «كم» is an object of «أهلكنا», and the sentence is as though it explains the object omitted for «يَهْدِ»."
His saying: {مِّنَ القرون}: in the position of accusative as an adjective of «كم», because it is indefinite. Making it a ḥāl from an indefinite is weak. It is not permissible for it to be a tamyīz according to the rules of the Basrans, and «من» enters it as it enters other specifiers, because it is definite.
The majority read «يَهْدِ» with the third-person yāʾ. The discussion of its agent has preceded. Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read it with the nūn that signals veneration, which supports the agent in the majority reading being the pronoun of Allah the Exalted.
His saying: {يَمْشُونَ}: a ḥāl of «القرون» or of the object of «أهلكنا». On these two the pronoun refers to the destroyed generations. Its meaning: "We destroyed them while they were in a state of security, walking about and moving in their needs", like His saying {أَخَذْنَاهُمْ بَغْتَةً} [al-Anʿām: 44]. It may be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «لهم». The pronoun in «يَمْشُون» on this refers to whom the pronoun in «لهم» refers, namely the idolaters contemporary with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The governing word in it is «يَهْدِ». The meaning: that you walk in the dwellings of past nations and move about in their lands, so you should take heed lest there befall you what befell them. Ibn al-Sumayfiʿ read «يُمَشَّوْن» in the passive with doubling; since it became transitive by doubling, building it in the passive was permissible.

semin-durr:129-129.t:
His saying: {وَأَجَلٌ مُّسَمًّى}: there are two views on its nominative. The clearer: that it is conjoined to «كلمةٌ», i.e. "and had it not been for a fixed term, the punishment would have been binding on them".
The second, which al-Zamakhsharī allowed: that it is nominative, conjoined to the latent pronoun. The pronoun refers to the immediate seizure, indicated by the context. The separation by the genitive phrase stands in the place of emphasis. The implied form: "Had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, the immediate seizure and a fixed term would have been binding on them, as the two were binding on ʿĀd and Thamūd, and the fixed term would not have been alone without the immediate seizure."
I say: he made the ism of «كان» refer to what the context indicates, except that a problem arises for him: he allowed two views for «لزام». One: that it is the maṣdar of «لازَمَ», like «الخِصام», and there is no problem on this. The second: that it is an adjective of the pattern «فِعال» meaning «مُفْعِل», i.e. "making binding", as though it were an instrument of adherence because of the excess of its adherence, as they said «لِزازُ خَصْمٍ». On this it would be said that it should agree in the dual, saying «لِزَامَيْنِ», unlike its being a maṣdar, which is singular in every case.
Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed that «لزاماً» be the plural of «لازم», like «قِيام» plural of «قائم».

semin-durr:130-130.t:
His saying: {بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ}: a ḥāl, i.e. "while you are praising Him".
His saying {وَمِنْ آنَآءِ الليل}: attached to the second «سَبِّحْ». What concerns this fāʾ has been discussed.
His saying: {وَأَطْرَافَ}: the majority read it accusative. There are two views on it. One: that it is conjoined to the position of {وَمِنْ آنَآءِ الليل}. The second: that it is conjoined to «قبلَ». al-Ḥasan and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read «وأطرافِ» genitive, conjoined to «آناءِ الليل». His saying here «أطرافَ», and in Hūd {طَرَفَيِ النهار} [verse 114]: it is said that this is putting the plural in place of the dual, as in the saying: 3329 - «ظَرْاهما مثلُ ظُهورِ التُّرْسَيْنْ» (the two of them, their upper sides are like the backs of two shields). It is also said that it is in its true sense, and that what is meant by «الأطراف» is the hours.
His saying: {ترضى}: al-Kisāʾī and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read «تُرْضَى» in the passive. The rest read it in the active, and on this is {وَلَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فترضى} [al-Ḍuḥā: 5].

semin-durr:131-131.t:
His saying: {أَزْوَاجاً}: there are two views on its accusative. One: that it is accusative as a direct object, and that is clear. The second: that it is accusative as a ḥāl from the hāʾ in «به». He took into account the wording of «ما» once and its meaning another time, and therefore he made it plural. al-Zamakhsharī said: "...and the verb falls on «منهم»." al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is as though it were said: 'to that which We gave enjoyment of, namely kinds of some of them, and people from among them.'"
His saying: {زَهْرَةَ}: nine views on its accusative. One: that it is a second object, because «مَتَّعْنا» is made to include the sense of «أَعْطَيْنا»; so «أزواجاً» is the first object and «زهرةَ» the second. The second: that it is a badal of «أَزْواجاً», either with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "possessors of splendour", or by way of exaggeration, they being made the very splendour. The third: that it is accusative by an implied verb which «مَتَّعْنا» indicates, implied as "We made for them splendour". The third (again, as numbered in the source): accusative as blame (dhamm); al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is the accusative of specification (ikhtiṣāṣ)." The fourth: that it is a badal of the position of the relative. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "Some preferred it. Others said: it is not permissible, because His saying {لِنَفْتِنَهُمْ} belongs to the ṣila of «مَتَّعْنا», so there would be a separation between the ṣila and the relative by a foreigner." This is a fine objection.
The fifth: that it is accusative as a badal of the position of «به». The sixth: that it is accusative as a ḥāl of the relative «ما». The seventh: that it is a ḥāl of the hāʾ in «به», which is the pronoun of the relative, so it is like the preceding in meaning. If it is asked: how can a ḥāl be definite? The answer is that «زهرةَ» is made an indefinite with tanwīn, the tanwīn having been dropped only because of the meeting of two sukūns, as in: 3330 - «. . . . . . . . ولا ذاكرَ اللَّهَ إلاَّ قليلا» (. . . and not mentioning Allah except little). On this, why is «الحياة» genitive? It is said: as a badal of the relative «ما». The eighth: that it is a tamyīz for «ما» or for the hāʾ in «به»; so said al-Farrāʾ. They rejected it from him because it is definite, and a specifier is not definite. This is not binding on him, for making the specifier definite is permissible by the principles of the Kufans.
The ninth: that it is an adjective of «أَزْواجاً» through the two interpretations mentioned for its accusative as ḥāl. Abū l-Baqāʾ barred this view because the described is indefinite and the description definite, and this is answered as the answer given to justify its accusative as ḥāl, namely the dropping of the tanwīn because of the meeting of two sukūns.
The majority put sukūn on the hāʾ. al-Ḥasan, Abū l-Barhasam and Abū Ḥaywa read it with fatḥa; it is said: with the same meaning, like «جَهْرَة» and «جَهَرَة». al-Zamakhsharī allowed that it be the plural of «زاهر», like «فاجِر» and «فَجَرة», and «بارّ» and «بَرَرَة». al-Aṣmaʿī reported from Nāfiʿ «لنُفْتِنَهم» with ḍamma on the nūn, from «أَفْتَنَه», when he threw him into trial.
«الزَّهْرَة», with fatḥa on the hāʾ and with sukūn, like «نَهْر» and «نَهَر», is whatever delights of blossom. A lamp is «زاهر» for its gleam, a man «أزهر» and a woman «زهراء» from this. «الأنجمُ الزهرُ» are the shining stars.

semin-durr:132-132.t: His saying: {للتقوى}: i.e. "for the people of piety". This is supported by His saying in another place {والعاقبة لِلْمُتَّقِينَ} [al-Aʿrāf: 128]. Ibn Wathāb read «نَرْزقُك» assimilating the qāf into the kāf. The well-known view from him is that he assimilates only when the kāf is attached to the plural mīm, as in {خَلَقَكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 21], and that has been discussed.

semin-durr:133-133.t:
His saying: {أَوَلَمْ تَأْتِهِمْ بَيِّنَةُ}: Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr and Ḥafṣ read «تأتهم» with the feminine; the rest read it with the lower yāʾ, because the feminine is figurative. The majority read «بَيِّنَةُ ما» with «بَيِّنَة» annexed to «ما», nominative, and that is clear. Abū ʿAmr, in what Abū Zayd reported, read «بَيِّنَةٌ» with tanwīn, nominative. On this reading there are several views about «ما». One: that it is a badal of «بَيِّنَةٌ», a total substitute (badal kull min kull). The second: that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is what is in the former scriptures". The third: that «ما» is negative. The author of «al-Lawāmiḥ» said: "What is meant is what is in the Qurʾān of abrogating verses and decisive statement, which was not in other books."
A group read «بَيِّنَةً» with tanwīn and accusative. Its explanation is that «ما» is the agent and «بَيِّنَةً» accusative as a ḥāl, made feminine according to the meaning of «ما». Whoever read with the feminine tāʾ did so by carrying it over to the meaning of «ما», and whoever read with the yāʾ did so according to its wording.
Ibn ʿAbbās read it with sukūn on the ḥāʾ. [Translator's note: the source gives no word for this reading; presumably «الصُّحْف»/«الصُّحُف» is meant.]

semin-durr:134-134.t:
The hāʾ in «قَبْلِهِ» may refer to the Messenger, by the evidence of His saying {لولا أَرْسَلْتَ إِلَيْنَا رَسُولاً}. al-Zamakhsharī and others allowed that it refer to «بَيِّنَةٍ», considering that it has the meaning of proof and evidence.
His saying: {فَنَتَّبِعَ}: accusative by an implied «أَنْ» in the response to urging (taḥḍīḍ). In the iʿrāb of Abū l-Baqāʾ it is "in the response to the question", which is an oversight.
Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn al-Ḥanafiyya, al-Ḥasan and a great many others read «نُذَلَّ ونخزى», both in the passive.

semin-durr:135-135.t:
And «مُتَرَبِّصٌ» is the khabar of «كل»; it is singular, carried over onto the wording of «كل».
His saying: {مَنْ أَصْحَابُ}: two views are allowed for this «مَنْ». The clearer: that it is interrogative, a mubtadaʾ, with «أصحابُ» its khabar, and the sentence is in the position of accusative, filling the place of the two objects. The second, attributed to al-Farrāʾ: that it is relative, meaning «الذين», and «أصحابُ» is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are the companions"; this follows their school, since they omit such a returning pronoun even when the ṣila is not long. Then «عَلِمَ» may be of acquaintance (ʿirfāniyya), so it is content with this one object, or it may be in its usual sense, in which case the second must be implied.
The majority read «السَّوِيِّ» on the pattern «فَعيل», meaning "level". Abū Mijlaz and ʿImrān ibn Ḥudayr read «السَّواء» with fatḥa on the sīn and lengthening, meaning the good middle. Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar and al-Jaḥdarī read «السوءى» on the pattern «فعلى», considering that «الصراط» is treated as masculine and feminine. Ibn ʿAbbās read «السَّوْء» with fatḥa on the sīn, meaning evil.
It was reported from the two of them «السوى» with ḍamma on the sīn and shadda on the wāw. This allows two views. One: that he turned the hamza into wāw and assimilated the wāw into the wāw. The other: that it is «فُعْلى» from «السَّواء», its origin being «السُّوْيا», the yāʾ turned into wāw and also assimilated. The analogical form would be «السُّيَّا», because whenever a yāʾ and a wāw meet and the first is preceded by sukūn, the wāw is turned into yāʾ; here the opposite was done.
«السُّوَيِّ» has also been read with ḍamma on the sīn, fatḥa on the wāw and shadda on the yāʾ, a diminutive of «سُوْء»; so said al-Zamakhsharī. The Shaykh said: "It is not good, for if it were so the hamza of «سوء» would remain. The better view is that it is the diminutive of «سواء», like their saying «عُطَيّ» for «عَطاء»." I say: Abū l-Baqāʾ also made it the diminutive of «السَّوْء», meaning with fatḥa on the sīn. The objection raised against al-Zamakhsharī applies to him, but replacing a hamza of this kind is permissible, so there is no objection.
His saying: {وَمَنِ اهتدى}: three views. One: that it is interrogative, and its rule is like that of the one before it, except for the omission of the returning pronoun. The second: that it is in the position of nominative, as explained for the interrogative. The third: that it is in the position of genitive, a conjunction on «الصراطِ», i.e. "and the companions of him who was guided". On these last two views it is relative. Abū l-Baqāʾ said of the second view: "In it is the conjoining of a declarative to an interrogative, and in it is a strengthening of the saying of al-Farrāʾ", meaning that if he makes it relative it is declarative.

semin-durr:1-1.t:
The discussion of the disjoined letters came at the beginning of this topic, and "طه" is of that kind; this is the correct view. It has also been said that the meaning of "طه" is "O man" in the language of ʿAkk, or it is said ʿUkl, or it is said that it is a Yemeni language. Al-Kalbī related that if you said in ʿAkk "O man", he would not answer until you said "ṭā-hā".
Al-Ṭabarī said: "'طه' in ʿAkk means 'O man'", and cited the saying of their poet:
3269 - دَعَوْتُ بِطهَ في القتالِ فلم يُجِبْ ... فَخِفْتُ عليهِ أَنْ يكونَ مُوائِلا
(I called "Ṭā-hā" in the fighting and he did not answer, so I feared for him that he had sought refuge.) And the saying of another:
3270 - إنَّ السَّفاهةَ طه في خلائِقِكمْ ... لا قَدَّسَ اللهُ أرواحَ المَلاعينِ
(Indeed foolishness, O man, is in your natures; may Allah not sanctify the spirits of the accursed.)
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The trace of artifice is apparent in the verse cited as evidence", and he mentioned it. Al-Suddī said: "its meaning is 'O so-and-so'." Al-Zamakhsharī also said: "Perhaps ʿAkk altered 'yā hādhā', as though in their language they turn the yā' into ṭā', saying ṭā for yā, and abbreviated 'hādhā' to 'hā'." He means that it is as though the noble verse said "O this one". There is great remoteness in this.
The Shaykh said: "Then he conjectured and guessed about ʿAkk what no grammarian had said: that they turn the vocative yā into ṭā' and drop the demonstrative noun, keeping only the 'hā' of attention." I say: though this is close to what he said about him, he was harsh on him in his wording with "he conjectured".
It has also been said: "طه" is originally "طَأْها" with a hamza, "طَأْ" being an imperative from وَطِىء يَطَأُ ("to tread"), and "ها" an object pronoun returning to the earth; then the hamza was turned into an alif because of its sukūn, and it was not dropped in the imperative, having regard to its origin; that is: "tread the earth with your feet". It has come in exegesis: "He stood until his feet swelled."
Al-Ḥasan, ʿIkrima, Abū Ḥanīfa and Warsh in his own choice read it dropping the alif after the ṭā', with a hā' with sukūn. It has two views. One: the original is "طَأْ" with a hamza, also an imperative from وَطِىء يَطَأُ, then the hamza was turned into a hā', as they turned it in "هَرَقْتُ", "هَرَحْتُ" and "هَبَرْتُ", the originals being أَرَقْتُ, أَرَحْتُ and أَبَرْت. The other: the hamza was turned into an alif, as though he took it from وَطِي يَطا with the substitution, as in:
3271 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . لا هَنَاكِ المَرْتَعُ
(...may the pasture not be pleasant for you.) [Translator's note: the first hemistich is elided in the source.] then the alif was dropped, carrying the imperative over to the jussive and ignoring the origin of the hamza, then the hā' of pause was attached, and continuous reading was treated like pausing. The discussion of the imāla of "ṭā" and "hā" came at the beginning of Yūnus, which makes repeating it here unnecessary.

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {أَنَزَلْنَا}: this is the reading of the majority. Ṭalḥa read "ما نُزِّلَ" as a passive, with "القرآنُ" nominative because it stands in for the agent.
This sentence may be resumptive if "طه" is made an enumeration of the names of letters; it may be the khabar of "طه" if you make it the name of the sūra, in which case "القرآن" is an overt noun standing in the place of the pronoun, because "طه" is also a Qur'an; and it may be the answer to an oath, if you make "طه" the thing sworn by. The detailed discussion of this has already come.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {إِلاَّ تَذْكِرَةً}: There are several views on its accusative. One: it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and the governing word in it is the verb of sending down; likewise "تَشقى" is also a reason for it. The first must come with a lām because it is not the agent of the verb being explained, so it lacks the condition for being accusative as an object; the second may have the lām cut off and be accusative, since it fulfils the conditions. This is al-Zamakhsharī's statement, and then he said: "If you ask: 'May you say: "We did not send down ... that you be wretched" as in {أَن تَحْبَطَ أَعْمَالُكُمْ} [al-Ḥujurāt: 2]?' I say: yes, but this is an incidental accusative, like the accusative in {واختار موسى قَوْمَهُ} [al-Aʿrāf: 155]; as for the accusative in 'تَذْكِرةً', it is like that in 'I struck Zayd', because it is one of the five objects that are the principles and canons for the rest."
I say: Abū l-Baqāʾ forbade "تَذْكرةً" being a mafʿūl li-ajlihi of the "أَنْزَلْنا" mentioned, because it has already reached one object of purpose, namely "لتشقى", so it does not reach another of the same kind. This prohibition is nothing, because it is permissible to give a verb two or more reasons; this is built from him on the view that the governing word of these optional complements reaches only one, except through badal or conjunction.
Two: "تذكرة" is a badal for the position of "لِتَشْقَى", which is the view of al-Zajjāj, followed by Ibn ʿAṭiyya; Abū Jaʿfar found it unlikely, and al-Fārisī rejected it because the reminder is not wretchedness. This is a clear rejection. Al-Zamakhsharī clarified this, saying: "If you ask: 'May "تذكرةً" be a badal for the position of "لِتشقى"?' I say: no, because of the difference of the two kinds; rather it is accusative as a disconnected exception in which 'إلاَّ' has the sense of 'لكن'."
The Shaykh said: "He means by the difference of the two kinds that the accusative of 'تذكرةً' is a sound accusative, not incidental, while the accusative that is in 'لِتشقى' after removal of the preposition is an incidental accusative. And we say that it has no position at all, so a badal for it cannot be imagined." I say: al-Zamakhsharī means by the difference of the two kinds only what I mentioned from al-Fārisī in refutation of al-Zajjāj; and what effect does the difference of the two accusatives have in that?
Three: it is accusative as a disconnected exception, that is: "but We sent it down as a reminder". Four: it is a corroborating maṣdar of an implied verb, that is: "but We reminded", or "be reminded by it, you, as a reminder". Five: it is a maṣdar in the position of ḥāl, that is: "except as a reminder (mudhakkiran)". Six: it is a badal for "القرآن", the Qur'an being the reminder; so said al-Ḥawfī. Seven: it is also a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, but the governing word in it is "لِتَشْقَى", and the meaning is as al-Zamakhsharī said: "We sent down the Qur'an to you that you bear the hardships of conveying the message, of disputing with the tyrants among the enemies of Islam and fighting them, and other kinds of toil and the burdens of prophethood; and We did not send down this wearisome toil upon you except that it be a reminder.
On this view 'تذكرة' may be a ḥāl and a mafʿūl li-ajlihi." End.
If you ask: whence did you take it that, when he made it a ḥāl and a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, the governing word in it is "لِتَشْقَى"? What prevents him from meaning by the governing word the verb of sending down? The answer is that this view came earlier from him in his saying "each one of 'لتشقى' and 'تذكرة' is a reason for the verb". Moreover his interpretation of the meaning mentioned rests on "لِتَشْقَى" governing "تذكرة". But since this meaning that appeared to al-Zamakhsharī did not appear to Abū l-Baqāʾ, he forbade "لِتَشْقَى" governing "تذكرة", saying: "It is not sound that 'لِتَشْقى' govern it, because of the corruption of the meaning." The answer to him is what came earlier. And there is nothing strange in calling toil "shaqāʾ"; al-Zamakhsharī said: "'الشقاءُ' comes in the sense of toil. From it is the proverb: 'More wearying than the breaker of a colt' and 'more wretched than the breaker of a colt'."
{لِّمَن يخشى} is attached to "تذكرةً". The lām was added to the object to strengthen the governing word since it is derivative; it may also be attached to an omitted element as an adjective of "تذكرةً".

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {تَنزِيلاً}: There are several views on its accusative. One: it is a badal for "تذكرةً" if that is made a ḥāl, not if it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, because a thing is not given itself as its reason. I say: because the implied form would become: "We did not send down the Qur'an except for the sending down." Two: it is accusative through an implied "نزَّل". Three: it is accusative through "أَنْزَلْنا", because the meaning of "We did not send it down except as a reminder" is "We sent it down as a reminder". Four: it is accusative as praise and specification (madḥ wa-ikhtiṣāṣ).
Five: it is accusative through "يخشى" as a direct object, that is: "He sent it down as a reminder for whoever fears the sending down of Allah", which is a fine meaning and a clear i'rab.
The Shaykh said, and he was not fair to him: "The best is what we mentioned first, that it is accusative through an implied 'نزَّل'. What al-Zamakhsharī mentioned of its being accusative otherwise is strained. As for the first, it makes 'تذكرةً' and 'تنزيلاً' two ḥāls, though they are two maṣdars, and making a maṣdar a ḥāl is not analogical.
Moreover the referent of 'تذكرةً' is not the referent of 'تنزيل', and 'تنزيلاً' is not part of a 'تذكرة'. If it is a badal, it would be a badal ishtimāl on the view of those who hold that the second includes the first, because the sending down includes the reminder and other things. As for his saying 'because the meaning of "We did not send it down except as a reminder" is "We sent it down as a reminder"', it is not so, because the meaning of restriction is lost in his saying 'We sent it down as a reminder'. As for its being accusative as praise, that is remote. As for its being accusative through 'يخشى', that is extremely remote, because 'يخشى' is the head of a verse and a pause, so it does not suit 'تنزيلاً' to be accusative through 'يخشى'; and his saying about it 'it is fine and a clear i'rab' is a foreignness (ʿujma) and a distance from grasping eloquence."
I say: it is enough for him that he rejects the obvious without proof, and attributes to this man lack of eloquence and the presence of foreignness.
His saying: {مِّمَّنْ خَلَق}: "مِنْ" may be attached to "تنزيلاً", or to an omitted element as an adjective of "تنزيلاً". In "خَلَق" there is an iltifāt from the first person in His saying "أَنْزَلْنا" to the third. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed that "ما أنزَلْنا" be a report of the speech of Gabriel and some of the angels, in which case there is no iltifāt.
His saying: {العلى} is the plural of عُلْيا, like دنيا and دُنا. Its parallel among sound forms is كُبْرى and كُبَر, فُضْلى and فُضَل.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {الرحمن}: The majority read it in the nominative, with several views. One: it is a badal for the latent pronoun in "خَلَق"; Ibn ʿAṭiyya mentioned it. The Shaykh rejected it because a badal takes the place of what it replaces, and if it took its place here it would not be permissible, because the sentence attached to the relative would lack a link tying it to it. Two: it is nominative as khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, whose implied form is "He is the Merciful". Three: it is nominative as mubtadaʾ, its lām pointing to "مَنْ خَلَقَ", and the sentence after it is its khabar.
Janāḥ ibn Ḥubaysh read "الرحمنِ" in the genitive. There are two views. One: it is a badal for the relative. It is not to be said that this leads to a badal with a derived noun, which is rare, because "الرحمن" has come to be treated as a non-derived noun through its frequent following of governing words. Two: it is also an adjective of the relative.
The Shaykh said: "The school of the Kufans is that the incomplete nouns like 'مَنْ' and 'ما' are not qualified by adjectives, with 'الذي' alone excepted; so on their school it is not permissible that it be an adjective." He said that as a rejection of al-Zamakhsharī.
The sentence {عَلَى العرش استوى} is the khabar of His saying "الرحمنُ" on the view that it is a mubtadaʾ, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ if it is said to be nominative as khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, and likewise in the reading of the one who makes it genitive.
The agent of "استوى" is a pronoun returning to "الرحمن". It has also been said that its agent is the relative "ما" after it, that is: "he who has what is in the heavens settled". Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "Some extremists say that 'ما' is the agent of 'استوى'. This is remote, and moreover it does not help him in the interpretation, since His saying {الرحمن عَلَى العرش} remains a complete statement, and from that he fled." I say: this is transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he used to pause at the word "العرش" and then begin "استوى له ما في السماوات", and this is not sound from him.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {الثرى}: it is damp earth, and its lām is yā', as shown by its dual ثَرَيَيْن and their saying ثَرِيَتْ الأرَضُ تَثْرَى ثَرَىً. "الثرى" is used for the severing of affection. Jarīr said:
3272 - فلا تَنْبُشُوا بيني وبينَكُمُ الثرى ... فإنَّ الذي بيني وبينَكُمُ مُثْرِي
(Do not dig up the earth between me and you, for what is between me and you is moist/abundant.) And "الثَّراءُ" with madd is abundance of wealth. He said:
3273 - أَماوِيَّ ما يُغْني الثراءُ عن الفتى ... إذا حَشَرَجَتْ يوماً وضاقَ بها الصدرُ
(O Māwiyya, what does wealth avail a young man when one day the death-rattle sounds and his chest is constricted by it?)
How fine is the saying of Ibn Durayd:
3274 - يوماً تصيرُ إلى الثَّرى ... ويفوزُ غيرُك بالثَّراءِ
(One day you will go to the earth, and another than you will win the wealth.)
In this poem he combined the lengthened and the shortened with a difference of meaning.

semin-durr:7-7.t: His saying: {وأخفى}: they allowed two views in it. One: it is an elative, that is "and more hidden than the secret". Two: it is a past verb, that is: "and Allah hid His unseen from His servants", as in His saying: {وَلاَ يُحِيطُونَ بِهِ عِلْماً} [Ṭāhā: 110].

semin-durr:8-8.t: The Majestic Name is either a mubtadaʾ, with the negated sentence as its khabar, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is "He is Allah". "الحُسْنى" is the feminine of الأحسن. It has been said more than once that the broken plural of non-rational beings is treated as a single feminine.

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying: {إِذْ رأى}: it may be accusative through "الحديث", which is the apparent view. It may also be accusative through an implied "اذكر" ("remember"), as Abū l-Baqāʾ said, or through an omitted element after it, that is: "when he saw a fire, such-and-such happened", as al-Zamakhsharī said.
"هل" is in its normal sense of an interrogative of affirmation (istifhām taqrīr); it has also been said to have the sense of "qad", and to have the sense of negation. Ḥamza read "لأهلِهُ امكثُوا" with ḍamma on the hā'; it has been mentioned that this is the original and the dialect of the Hijaz, while Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "the ḍamma is by assimilation (ittibāʿ)".
His saying: {آنَسْتُ} means "I saw". "الإِيناسُ" is clear seeing, and from it the "insān" of the eye (the pupil), because things are seen with it; it has also been said to be finding, and to be perceiving, which is more general than seeing. They recited the verse of al-Ḥārith ibn Ḥilliza:
3275 - آنسَتْ نَبْأَةً وأَفْزَعَها القُنْ ... ناصُ عَصْراً وقد دنا الإِمْساءُ
(She perceived a faint sound, and the hunter startled her in the afternoon, when evening had drawn near.)
"القَبَسُ" is a brand of fire, the flame at the head of a stick or reed and the like. It is a فَعَل with the sense of مَفْعول, like القَبَض and النَّقَض, meaning المَقْبوض and المَنْقوض. One says أَقْبَسْتُ الرجلَ علماً and قَبَسْتُه ناراً, distinguishing between the two; this is the view of al-Mubarrad. Al-Kisāʾī said: فَعَلَ and أَفْعَلَ are both said in the two meanings, so one says قَبَسْتُه ناراً وعلماً, and أَقْبَسْته also علماً وناراً.
His saying {مِّنْهَا} may be attached to "آتِيكم" or to an omitted element as ḥāl from "قَبَس". Some pronounced the alif of "هدى" with imāla in pause. The good practice is not to apply imāla, because the best-known view is that it is a substitute for tanwīn.

semin-durr:11-11.t: His saying: {نُودِيَ}: the one standing in for the agent is the pronoun of Mūsā; it has also been said to be the pronoun of the maṣdar, that is "the call was called", which is weak. They forbade the sentence "يا موسى" from being the one standing in for the agent, because a sentence cannot be an agent.

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying: {إني}: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read it with fatḥa, on the implied bā' ("بأني"), because the call is linked with it; you say "I called him with such-and-such". The poet said, as al-Fārisī recited:
3276 - نادَيْتُ باسمِ ربيعةَ بنِ مُكَدَّمٍ ... إنَّ المُنَوَّهَ باسمِه المَوْثُوْقُ
(I called by the name of Rabīʿa ibn Mukaddam: indeed the one whose name is proclaimed is the trusted.)
Ibn ʿAṭiyya allowed it to have the sense of "for the sake of", which is not apparent. The others read with kasra: either on an implied saying, as is the view of the Basrans, or because the call has the sense of saying according to the Kufans.
His saying: {أَنَاْ} may be a mubtadaʾ with what follows as its khabar, the sentence being the khabar of "إنَّ". It may also be an emphasis for the accusative pronoun, and may be a separating pronoun (faṣl).
His saying "طوى": the Kufans and Ibn ʿĀmir read "طُوىً" with ḍamma on the ṭā' and tanwīn. The others read it with ḍamma without tanwīn. Al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿmash, Abū Ḥaywa and Ibn Muḥayṣin read it with kasra on the ṭā' and tanwīn, and Abū Zayd from Abū ʿAmr with kasra without tanwīn.
Whoever read it with ḍamma and tanwīn made it inflected because he interpreted it as the place. Whoever withheld the tanwīn has several possibilities. One: he withheld it for feminine gender in the sense of the tract of land, together with being a proper name. Two: he withheld it for ʿadl (deviation) to the pattern فُعَل, even though the word it deviated from is not known, treating it like عُمَر and زُفَر. Three: it is a foreign noun, so its withholding is for being a proper name and foreign.
Whoever read it with kasra without tanwīn did so also in regard to the tract of land. If it is a noun, it is like عِنَب; if an adjective, like عِدَى and سِوَى. Whoever gave it tanwīn did so in regard to the place. From al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī: it has the sense of الثنى with kasra and shortening, and الثنى is what is repeated twice, so the meaning of this reading is that it appeared twice, and it would be a maṣdar accusative through the word "المقدَّس" because it has its meaning, as if it were said: "sanctified twice", from التقديس.
ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read "طاوِيْ اذهَبْ".
"طوى" is either a badal for "الوادي", or an ʿaṭf bayān for it, or nominative with an implied mubtadaʾ, or accusative with an implied "أعني" ("I mean").

semin-durr:13-13.t:
His saying: {وَأَنَا اخترتك}: Ḥamza, among others, read "وأنَّا اخترناك" with fatḥa on the hamza, with the pronoun of the speaker magnifying himself. Al-Sulamī, al-Aʿmash and Ibn Hurmuz read likewise, except that they put kasra on the hamza. The others read "وأنا اخْتَرْتُك" with the pronoun of the speaker alone. Ubayy read "وأني اخترتك" with fatḥa on the hamza.
As for Ḥamza's reading, it is conjoined to His saying {إني أَنَاْ رَبُّكَ}, which is with fatḥa on the hamza there, so he did that when he conjoined another to it. Whoever put kasra did so because he reads "إنِّي أنا ربك" with kasra. Ubayy's reading is like Ḥamza's with respect to the conjunction. Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed the fatḥa to be on the implied form "ولأنَّا اخترناك فاستمع" ("and because We chose you, so listen"), attaching it to "استمع". The first is preferable. The second object of "اخترتك" is omitted, that is: "I chose you from among your people".
His saying {لِمَا يوحى}: the apparent view is that it is attached to "استمِعْ". It is possible that the lām is added to the object, as in His saying {رَدِفَ لَكُم} [al-Naml: 72]. Al-Zamakhsharī and others allowed the case to be one of tanāzuʿ (competition) between "اخْتَرْتُك" and "استمع", as if it were said: "I chose you for what is revealed, so listen to what is revealed." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "So he attaches the lām to 'استمعْ' or to 'اخترتُك'."
The Shaykh rejected this, saying: "Attaching it to 'اخترتك' is not permissible because it belongs to the chapter of ʿamal (governing), where it is obligatory or preferred to repeat the pronoun with the second, which would give 'فاستمعْ له لِما يوحى'; which shows that it is a case of giving effect to the second." I say: al-Zamakhsharī meant the attachment in meaning, as to suitability; as for the technical posited form, he did not mean it.
"ما" may be a maṣdar, or have the sense of "الذي", that is: "so listen to the revelation, or to that which is revealed".

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {لذكري}: the maṣdar may be annexed to its agent, that is: "because I mentioned it in the Books", or "because I remember you". It may also be annexed to its object, that is: "that you remember Me". It has also been said that its meaning is remembering the prayer after forgetting it, as in his saying, peace be upon him: "Whoever sleeps through a prayer or forgets it, let him pray it when he remembers it." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The proper wording would have been 'لذكرها'". Then he said: "Whoever strains for it may say: when he remembers the prayer he has remembered [Allah]; or on an omitted muḍāf, that is 'for the remembrance of My prayer'; or because remembrance and forgetting are from Allah the Exalted in reality."
Abū Rajāʾ and al-Sulamī read "للذكرى" with the lām of definiteness and the alif of feminine ending. Some read "لذكرى" indefinite, and some "للذكر" definite and masculine.
His saying: {أَكَادُ أُخْفِيهَا}: The majority read "أُخْفيها" with ḍamma on the hamza. There are several interpretations. One: the hamza in "أُخْفيها" is for privation and removal, that is "I remove its concealment", like أعجمتُ الكتابَ, "I removed its non-Arabic quality". There are then two senses to that. One: that "الخفاء" has the sense of covering, and when He removes its covering He has manifested it. The meaning: because it is certain to happen and near, I almost reveal it, were it not for what wisdom requires of delay. The other: that "الخفاء" is appearance, as will come. The meaning: I remove its appearance, and when He removes its appearance it is hidden. The meaning: because of the intensity of its obscurity I almost hide it so that I do not reveal it at all, though it must be revealed; and for that reason it is found in some codices, such as Ubayy's codex: "I almost hide it from Myself, so how would I show you it?" That is in keeping with the Arabs' habit of exaggeration in concealment. He said:
3277 - أيامَ تَصْحَبُني هندٌ وأُخْبِرُها ... ما كِدْت أكتُمُه عني من الخبرِ
(In the days when Hind accompanied me and I told her what I almost concealed even from myself of news.)
And how can concealing from oneself be imagined?
The second interpretation: "كاد" is redundant; so said Ibn Jubayr. Another cited as evidence the saying of Zayd al-Khayl:
3278 - سريعٌ إلى الهَيْجاء شاكٍ سلاحُه ... فما إنْ يكادُ قِرْنُه يتنفَّسُ
(Quick to battle, his weapons bristling, so that his opponent scarcely breathes.)
And another said:
3279 - وألاَّ ألومَ النفسَ فيما أصابني ... وألا أكادَ بالذي نِلْتُ أَبْجَحُ
(That I not blame myself for what befell me, and that I not exult at what I obtained.)
There is no proof in any of this.
The third interpretation: that "الكَيْدُوْدَة" has the sense of intending; it is ascribed to al-Akhfash and a group, and it does not serve what they intended.
The fourth interpretation: that its khabar is omitted, its implied form being: "I almost bring it, because of its nearness." They cited the saying of Ḍābiʾ al-Burjumī:
3280 - هَمَمْتُ ولم أفْعَلْ وكِدْتُ وليتني ... تَرَكْتُ على عثمانَ تَبْكي حلائِلُهْ
(I intended and did not do it, and I almost did; would that I had left ʿUthmān with his wives weeping over him.)
that is: "and I almost did", so the pause is on "أكادُ" and the beginning is with "أُخْفيها"; Abū Jaʿfar approved of it.
Abū l-Dardāʾ, Ibn Jubayr, al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid and Ḥumayd read "أَخْفيها" with fatḥa on the hamza. The meaning: "I reveal it", by the interpretation given before. One says خَفَيْتُ الشيءَ, "I revealed it", and أَخْفَيْتُه, "I concealed it"; this is the well-known view. It was transmitted from Abū l-Khaṭṭāb that خَفَيْتُ and أَخْفَيْتُ have one meaning. It was related from Abū ʿUbayd that "أَخْفى" is one of the words of opposite meanings, meaning both "revealed" and "concealed", and on this the two readings are the same. An example of خَفَيْتُ in the sense of "I revealed" is the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
3281 - خَفَاهُنَّ مِنْ أَنْفاقِهِنَّ كأنما ... خفاهُنَّ وَدْقٌ مِنْ عَشِيٍّ مُجَلِّبِ
(He brought them out of their burrows, as though a downpour from a thundering evening had brought them out.)
and the saying of another:
3282 - فإنْ تَدْفِنوا الداءَ لا نَخْفِهِ ... وإنْ تُوْقِدُوْا الحربَ لا نَقْعُدِ
(If you bury the disease we shall not unearth it, and if you kindle the war we shall not sit still.)
His saying: {لتجزى}: this is the lām of purpose (lām kay), and does not have the sense of an oath, that is "لَتُجْزَيَنَّ", as Abū l-Baqāʾ transmitted from some. This lām is attached to "اُخْفيها". Some made it attached to "آتيةٌ", but this is not complete unless you posit that "أكاد أُخْفيها" is a parenthetical clause between what is attached and what it is attached to; but if you make it an adjective of "آتِيَةٌ" it does not work on the school of the Basrans, because an active participle, when it is qualified, does not govern, though if it governed and was then qualified it would be permissible.
Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is also said to be attached to 'آتِيَةٌ', and for that reason some paused on it with a slight pause, to signal its separation from 'أخفيها'."
His saying: {بِمَا تسعى} is attached to "تجزى". "ما" may be a maṣdar or a nominal relative, and a muḍāf is necessary, that is: "she is requited with the punishment for her striving", or "with the punishment for what she strove".

ukberi-tibyan:9-10.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَهَلْ أَتَاكَ حَدِيثُ مُوسَى (٩) إِذْ رَأَى نَارًا فَقَالَ لِأَهْلِهِ امْكُثُوا إِنِّي آنَسْتُ نَارًا لَعَلِّي آتِيكُمْ مِنْهَا بِقَبَسٍ أَوْ أَجِدُ عَلَى النَّارِ هُدًى (١٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ رَأَى): «إِذْ» is an adverb (ẓarf) for «حَدِيثُ», or a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "remember [when]".
(لِأَهْلِهِ): with kasra and with ḍamma on the hāʾ; this has already been mentioned. Whoever reads it with ḍamma makes it follow what comes after it.
And (مِنْهَا): it may be attached to آتيكم, or be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «قَبَسٍ».
The best course with «هُدًى» here is that it be written with alif and not pronounced with imāla (inclination of the vowel), because the alif is a replacement for the tanwīn according to the verified view. Some, however, have pronounced it with imāla, and there are three explanations of this. The first: that he likened the alif of the tanwīn to the final radical (lām) of the word, since in the shortened (maqṣūr) noun the pronunciation of the two is the same. The second: that it is the final radical of the word, and nothing was substituted for the tanwīn in the accusative, as occurs in:
وَآخُذُ مِنْ كُلِّ حَيٍّ عَصُمْ ("and I take from every tribe a pledge [of protection]"). The third: that it follows the view of those who pause in all three states (nominative, accusative and genitive) without any substitution.

ukberi-tibyan:11-12.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَلَمَّا أَتَاهَا نُودِيَ يَا مُوسَى (١١) إِنِّي أَنَا رَبُّكَ فَاخْلَعْ نَعْلَيْكَ إِنَّكَ بِالْوَادِي الْمُقَدَّسِ طُوًى (١٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (نُودِيَ): the object standing in place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent) is a concealed pronoun, i.e. "Moses was called". It is also said: it is the maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "the calling was called", and what follows explains it. And «يَا مُوسَى» cannot stand in place of the agent, because it is a clause.
(إِنِّي): it is read with kasra, i.e. "and He said: indeed I…", or because calling is a kind of saying. And with fatḥa, i.e. "he was called with [the words] that I…", just as you say: نَادَيْتُهُ بِاسْمِهِ ("I called him by his name").
And (أَنَا): a mubtadaʾ (subject), or a tawkīd (emphasis), or a separating pronoun (faṣl).
His saying, Exalted is He: (طُوًى): it is read with ḍamma and tanwīn, and it is a proper name for the valley, and it is a badal (substitute) from it. It may also be nominative, i.e. "it is Ṭuwā".
It is also read without tanwīn, on the basis that it is a definite feminine noun, a name for the spot of ground.
It is also said: it is maʿdūl (a form diverted from another), even if the wording of the form it was diverted from is not known; it is as though its origin were «طَاوِي». In that respect it is like جُمَع and كُتَع.
It is also read with kasra, on the basis that it is like عِنَب among nouns, and عِدًا and سِوًى among adjectives.

ukberi-tibyan:13-13.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَأَنَا اخْتَرْتُكَ فَاسْتَمِعْ لِمَا يُوحَى (١٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَأَنَا اخْتَرْتُكَ): in the singular form, and this fits better with what precedes it.
It is also read: وَأَنَّا اخْتَرْنَاكَ, in the plural, and the implied form is: "because We have chosen you, so listen"; the lām is then attached to استمع. It may also be conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أَنِّي, i.e. "[he was called] with: Indeed I am your Lord, and with: We have chosen you".

ukberi-tibyan:14-14.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّنِي أَنَا اللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنَا فَاعْبُدْنِي وَأَقِمِ الصَّلَاةَ لِذِكْرِي (١٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لِذِكْرَى): the lām is attached to أقم, and the implied form is: "at your remembering Me". So the maṣdar (verbal noun) is annexed to its object. It is also said: to its agent, i.e. "for My remembering you", or "[My remembering] it [i.e. the prayer]".
«[Translator's note: the heading is printed «لِذِكْرَى» in the source, while the ayah reads «لِذِكْرِي».]»

ukberi-tibyan:15-15.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّ السَّاعَةَ آتِيَةٌ أَكَادُ أُخْفِيهَا لِتُجْزَى كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا تَسْعَى (١٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أُخْفِيهَا): with ḍamma on the hamza, and there are two views on it. One of them: "I conceal it", i.e. from Myself, because He has not disclosed it to any created being. The second: "I reveal it"; it is said that it is one of the words with opposite meanings (aḍdād).
It is also said: the hamza is for privation (salb), i.e. "I remove its hiddenness".
It is also read with fatḥa on the hamza, and its meaning is "I reveal it"; one says: خَفَيْتُ الشَّيْءَ, i.e. "I revealed the thing".
(لِتُجْزَى): the lām is attached to أخفيها. It is also said: to آتية; and for that reason some paused on it with a slight pause, to signal its separation from «أُخْفِيهَا». It is also said: its wording is the wording of kay, while its implied sense is that of an oath, i.e. لَتُجْزَيَنَّ ("it shall surely be recompensed"). And «مَا» is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun). It is also said: it is in the sense of الذي, i.e. "[for what] it strives in".

ukberi-tibyan:16-16.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَلَا يَصُدَّنَّكَ عَنْهَا مَنْ لَا يُؤْمِنُ بِهَا وَاتَّبَعَ هَوَاهُ فَتَرْدَى (١٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَتَرْدَى): it may be accusative (manṣūb) as the answer to the prohibition, or nominative, i.e. "for then you will perish".

ukberi-tibyan:17-17.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمَا تِلْكَ بِيَمِينِكَ يَا مُوسَى (١٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَا تِلْكَ): «مَا» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «تِلْكَ» is its khabar (predicate), and it is in the sense of هذه ("this").
And (بِيَمِينِكَ): a ḥāl (circumstantial), governed by the meaning of pointing contained in the demonstrative.
It is also said: it [تلك] is in the sense of الذي; then بيمينك is a ṣifa for it.
«[Translator's note: «صِفَةً لَهَا» here means its complement, i.e. the ṣila (relative clause) of تلك taken as a relative noun.]»

ukberi-tibyan:18-20.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ هِيَ عَصَايَ أَتَوَكَّأُ عَلَيْهَا وَأَهُشُّ بِهَا عَلَى غَنَمِي وَلِيَ فِيهَا مَآرِبُ أُخْرَى (١٨) قَالَ أَلْقِهَا يَامُوسَى (١٩) فَأَلْقَاهَا فَإِذَا هِيَ حَيَّةٌ تَسْعَى (٢٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (عَصَايَ): the proper course is fatḥa on the yāʾ because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.
It is also read with kasra, and this is weak, because it is felt heavy on the yāʾ.
It is also read عَصَىَّ, and its parallel has been mentioned in [Sūrat] al-Baqara.
And (أَتَوَكَّأُ): it and what follows it are resumptive (mustaʾnaf). It is also said: its position is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the yāʾ, or from the staff. It is also said: it is the khabar (predicate) of «هِيَ», and عصاي is the object of an omitted verb. It is also said: it [عصاي] is a khabar, and «أَتَوَكَّأُ» is another khabar.
And (أَهُشُّ): with the dotted shīn, i.e. "I lean on it over the sheep", or "I frighten [them]", and the like.
It is also read with kasra on the hāʾ, i.e. "with it I break down for my sheep what falls on them [of leaves]", from your saying: هَشَشْتُ الْخُبْزَ, when you break bread after it has dried.
It is also read with ḍamma on the hāʾ and an undotted sīn, from your saying: هَسَّ الْغَنَمَ يَهُسُّهَا, when he drives them. It is made transitive with عَلَى because its meaning is "I stand over them with it", or "I frighten [them]".
And (أُخْرَى): according to the feminine of the plural; had He said أُخَر, it would have followed the wording.
(تَسْعَى): it may be a second khabar, and it may be a ḥāl.
And «إِذَا» of surprise (mufājaʾa) is an adverb of place; what governs it is «تَسْعَى» or something omitted. This has already been mentioned.
